#### B.11.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The hand-off | `ReplicaOpener.admitJob`: a `More` from `admit` goes to `registry.onReplacementRequested` (dispatch only; the open still holds its admission), and `Updating.scheduled` tells the host that the worker has it | `SharedReplicaStoreOpen.kt`, `ReplicaHandles.kt` |
| The run on the worker | `ReplicaWorker.scheduleReplacement`. There is one job per store (registry): a newer one handed over while a run goes on replaces it for the next run, and a store's runs never overlap. Each run is under one `acquireForJob("replacement:<app>")` token whose expiry asks the run to stop between chunks. A refused token is logged and answered `Stopped`. The outcome goes to `onReplacementOutcome`. A job that ended for good (`Finished`, `Skew`, `Corrupt`) is forgotten; any other is run again at `kick()` | `ReplicaConfirmationWalk.kt` (`ReplicaWorker`) |
| The hold after a counted run | a `Stopped` caused by `MigrationRowFailed` records `ReplicaProtection.foregroundEntries`. Until that count moves, the store's job is answered `Stopped("… not again before the next foreground")` with no token taken and no run | same, `ReplicaProtection.kt` |
| The refusal | `ReplicaReplacement.chunk`: once the marker is judged and decoded, a **migration** chunk outside the foreground rolls back and ends the run `NeedsForeground`. A wipe's chunk is not asked | `ReplicaReplacement.kt` |
| "In the foreground" | `ReplicaGate.inForeground()` = no deadline, the store's one statement of it. `CKPT_MAX`'s `deferWhile` now uses it too | `ReplicaHandles.kt`, `ReplicaCheckpointer.kt` |
| The end-of-job checkpoint | `ReplicaReplacement.endOfJob(outcome)`, called by the worker after `run` with the token still held. It acts only in protected background time and only when the `-wal` is past `Wmax/4`: one `PASSIVE` checkpoint in an admission of its own, under the registry's lock | `ReplicaReplacement.kt` |
| One run per object | `run` refuses a second run of the same object while one is going | same |

#### B.11.2 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.10.

146. ⚠⚠ **S13 is asked by every migration chunk, under the write lock, after the marker is
     judged.** The marker rule already re-reads which job the marker names in each chunk, so the
     refusal sits there. The case of B.3 (56) is covered by construction: a run obtained for a wipe
     in a wake that meets a migration a sibling started meanwhile. So is a run begun in the
     foreground and carried past a backgrounding. Its next chunk is refused, the chunks already
     committed stand (`NeedsForeground`'s KDoc now says so), and the backgrounding token's quiesce
     is not held up by a long migration. The check sits after `classify` and the marker's decode, so
     damage and a marker of another format are still judged in the background, as at the open.
     **A wipe's chunk is not asked.** A wipe may be resumed in a wake (§5.1), and the store-less
     wipe in the background still runs to its end (tested).
     ⚠ One consequence: a wipe call that meets a migration started after a sibling finished its wipe
     now ends `WipeNotFinished(NeedsForeground)` where it used to run the migration (Q21).
147. ⚠ **"Not again before the next foreground" is the worker's, and is counted in foregrounds,
     not in launches.** `ReplicaProtection.foregroundEntries` counts `enteredForeground` calls.
     A launch in the foreground does not count, so a run that counts in a launch's first
     foreground waits for the next one. The hold is in memory, per store and per process: a new
     process starts unheld, as a new launch should. A sibling app is not held either, since one
     count per run is the store's rule and each app's runs are its own. With no protection
     attached nothing counts foregrounds, and a hold then lasts for the process (tests only;
     B.11.4). A kick while held is answered held.
148. ⚠⚠ **The end-of-job checkpoint runs before the token is released, only in protected
     background time, and keeps the job's outcome.** In the foreground the 30 s trigger is the
     opportunistic one (B.9), so `endOfJob` does nothing there. `afterCommit` already checkpoints
     past `Wmax/4` after every commit of a chunk. This trigger is for the log as the job leaves it:
     after a `PASSIVE` that a reader blocked, after a run that stopped with nothing committed, or
     after a sibling's commits. It takes its own gate admission (the chunk's has been given back),
     and with the gate closed it does nothing. The checkpointer's own admission check
     (`CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE`) still applies. Its result changes the outcome only when it **finds the
     marker** or its **code is confirmed** (then `Corrupt`). An unconfirmed code, `NotReset` or a
     `NOT_DURABLE` marker leave the job's own outcome: a finished job stays `Finished`, and the
     checkpoint's rule (the second code in a row confirms, (52)) is kept by the counter the
     checkpointer moves. Only the `REPLACEMENT` run calls it. The walk is read-only, and a wipe
     call's end is the binding slice's (its token).
149. **The open hands its job off itself when a worker is attached, and says so.** This mirrors the
     walk's hand-off (B.8): `attach` sets both callbacks. `Updating.scheduled` is the host's
     signal not to run the job as well; with no worker attached (every earlier test) the host runs
     it, as before. The callback only dispatches, because the open still holds its admission. A
     dispatch inline on the open's thread would nest the run's admissions inside the open's, so
     production uses a serial queue of the worker's own (as for the walk).
150. **One run of one `ReplicaReplacement` at a time is enforced** (`run` throws
     `IllegalStateException` before registering anything). The class always said "one thread at a
     time". With the worker and a host both able to hold the object, that is now a guard. Two runs
     would share `current`, the `-wal` probe and `inAdmission`. A worker run that meets it is
     answered `Stopped("the run threw")`.
151. **One job per store in the worker, the latest handed over wins.** Two opens in one process can
     each answer `Updating` with a fresh object. Running both would be correct (two resumers are
     safe by the marker rule) but would double the work and the tokens. So the worker keys by
     registry, and a newer job replaces the one waiting. A job is forgotten once it ended for good,
     so a `kick()` never re-runs a finished store; one that stopped is kept for the next kick.
152. **`ReplicaGate.inForeground()` is the store's one statement of "in the foreground"**
     (`remainingMs() == null`). The refusal (146), the end-of-job trigger (148) and `CKPT_MAX`'s
     `deferWhile` (B.10 (143), refactored, unchanged in behaviour) all ask it, so B.11.4's
     constraint has one place to hold.

**Fix round of the independent review (2026-10-17).**

153. ⚠⚠ **"In the foreground" is answered from the protection's state, never by the platform.**
     `inForeground()` went through `remainingMs()`, so in the background it asked
     `backgroundTimeRemaining`: in every migration chunk with the registry's lock and the write
     lock held, in `endOfJob` under the registry's lock, and every 100 ms from the watchdog's queue
     (`CKPT_MAX`'s `deferWhile`). An adapter answering with a `dispatch_sync` to main, while main
     waits on either lock, deadlocks. Now `ReplicaGateProtection.isForeground` answers it, and
     `ReplicaProtection` reads its own `foreground` flag. **Equivalent to `remainingMs() == null`:**
     `ReplicaProtection.remainingMs` returns null exactly when `isForeground` holds, and otherwise
     the platform's value (0 on a throw), never null. The latch, the tokens and an expiry move
     neither: they change `protected`, not `foreground`. `remainingMs()` stays where the value
     itself is needed, in the admission checks (B.11.4 (6)).
154. **The end-of-job checkpoint is inside the run's guard.** `run`'s `running` was released
     before the worker called `endOfJob`, so a host's `run()` could overlap the checkpoint. The
     two share the probe, `inAdmission` and the checkpointer. The worker now calls
     `runToEndOfJob`: one guarded section holding the run and its end-of-job checkpoint. A direct
     `endOfJob` (the tests') is guarded on its own.
155. **Nits.** The worker judges a run's outcome with a sealed `when` in functions of its own,
     outside the lock's `try`/`finally`, so the K/N 2.4.10 type-test shape cannot come back
     there. `Updating.scheduled`'s KDoc says that a second `run()` throws
     `IllegalStateException`.

#### B.11.3 Open questions for the maintainer

| # | Question | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Q21 | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-17: the recommendation.** A wipe call in a wake whose later chunk meets a **migration** marker now ends `WipeNotFinished(NeedsForeground)` (146). That happens only when a sibling finished the wipe and then started a migration over the emptied store. The forget then keeps custody and reports "not finished". Is that acceptable, or should a wipe call that meets a migration it did not start count as finished? | **As built.** The case is narrow and the conservative answer is D3's: custody is never purged over a store whose state the call did not establish. A forget repeated in the foreground completes (S0b-1's binding tests) |
| Q22 | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-17: the recommendation.** The hold after a counted run is per process and in memory (147). Should it be durable, so that a relaunch in the background (a wake) also waits for a foreground? | **No, as built.** A wake cannot run a migration anyway (146 and the open's `StoreNeedsForeground`), so the only runs a hold could stop are foreground ones, and a new launch's foreground is "the next foreground" |
| Q23 | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-17: the recommendation.** Should the end-of-job checkpoint also run in the foreground, in place of the 30 s trigger until the adapter exists? | **No.** §4.2.1 names it for protected background jobs, and in the foreground `afterCommit` already checkpoints after every chunk. The 30 s trigger lands with the adapter |

#### B.11.4 Constraints for the binding and UIKit-adapter slices

From B.10's last review, and generalized by this slice (152):

1. ⚠⚠ **A process with no protection attached is "in the foreground" everywhere.**
   `remainingMs()` is null, so `inForeground()` is true. Such a process therefore gets:
   - no `CKPT_MAX`: with no protection, `deferWhile` is always true, so a background process
     without protection (an app extension, say) defers it for good;
   - no admission check (B.7);
   - no refusal of a migration chunk (146).

   - and, if it counts a migration failure, a hold on its migration that lasts until the process
     is relaunched (`foregroundEntries()` is 0 for good, (147)), with "Updating storage…" on
     screen meanwhile. That is the safe direction, but it is a stuck surface.

   **Every process that can open the store, an app extension included, must attach a
   `ReplicaProtection` before its first open.** The binding slice asserts it, for all four
   consequences above. The
   alternative, a protection-less process counting as background, would make every existing test
   a background test; the default is for the tests and must not reach a device.
2. ⚠⚠ **`backgroundTimeRemainingMs()` is called from any thread.** While a foreground checkpoint
   runs past `CKPT_MAX`, the watchdog's queue polls `deferWhile` every `DEFERRED_RECHECK_MS`
   (100 ms), and in the background that is `ProtectionAssertions.backgroundTimeRemainingMs()`.
   The refusal (146) and the end-of-job trigger (148) ask it on the worker's thread under the
   registry's lock. **The adapter must keep it safe to call from any thread, and must never
   `dispatch_sync` to main** (B.5.3: sampled on main, the rest from monotonic time, or a
   main-updated `@Volatile`). `DBL_MAX` is clamped to "no deadline".
3. **A host given `Updating(scheduled = true)` does not run the job itself** (149); a second run of
   the object is refused (150).
4. **The worker's dispatch is a serial queue of its own, never inline on the open's thread** (149).
5. Q13 still applies: name the walk, and now the job token's reason, by the bundle, so that an
   extension's process and its app's are told apart.
6. ⚠⚠ **The admission checks still ask the platform under the registry's lock** (B.7: an access's
   and a job chunk's in `acquire`, a checkpoint's in `ReplicaCheckpointer.run`), because the
   check is made at the operation's start, with its admission held. In the foreground
   `ReplicaProtection.remainingMs` answers null without asking. In the background each admission
   check is one platform call under the registry's lock, never under the write lock. So (2)'s
   "never `dispatch_sync` to main" is not a nicety: a main thread waiting on the registry's lock
   would deadlock against it.

#### B.11.5 Tests and mutations

New suite `ReplicaReplacementWorkerTest`, 11 tests (13 after the fix round), every store made up and the watchdog off (131):
- **(146):** a migration run outside the foreground is refused at its first chunk, with nothing
  committed, the marker unchanged and no handle left, and in the foreground the same object runs to
  its end. A run begun in the foreground and backgrounded as its first chunk commits stops at the
  next chunk, keeps the 7 rows it committed, and resumes with every row migrated once. A
  store-less wipe in the background still runs to its end.
- **(149):** an open's job is handed to the worker (`scheduled`) and run on a real background queue
  under exactly one job token, and the next open is `Ready` at the new stamps. With no worker
  attached, `scheduled` is false.
- **(150):** a second run of one object, from inside the first, is refused and registers nothing;
  the object runs again once the first has returned.
- **(147):** a run that counted is held: the next open's job and a kick are answered held, with no
  token and no count. After `enteredBackground` and `enteredForeground` a kick runs it, and it
  counts the second attempt.
- **(151):** a job stopped by a closed gate is run again at a kick; a finished one is not. Two jobs
  handed over for one store take one dispatch and run the latest.
- **(148):** a background job past `Wmax/4` (a sibling's commits) checkpoints once, with the wake's
  token and the job's both live, and the log is reset; the job's token is released after it; the
  next job's end, under `Wmax/4`, checkpoints nothing. In the foreground, or with the gate closed,
  nothing runs. A run that ended `Stopped` checkpoints too and keeps its outcome.

### B.12 The UIKit adapter (2026-10-17)

**What it is.** B.5.3's adapter, the slice B.11's "what is left" named next, built as Q1–Q4 decided
(B.5.4) and **bound nowhere**: nothing calls its `install`, and no app's runtime opens the shared
store. It drives the protection as built in `:core-common`; it re-decides none of Q1–Q4.
- **A deliberate public surface** (the B.11 table's "first step"): one opt-in seam of
  `:core-common`, everything else of the store still `internal`.
- **The adapter**, `SharedReplicaUiKitAdapter` in `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core` beside
  `FirstPartyLocalRuntime` (Q4): `ProtectionAssertions` over `beginBackgroundTask` /
  `endBackgroundTask`; the two notifications driving `enteredBackground` / `enteredForeground`
  with Q3's split; `install` at launch; `backgroundTimeRemainingMs()` safe from any thread.
- **The worker's serial queue and `kick()`** at each foreground and each wake (B.8's split-off).
- **The 30 s foreground checkpoint** (B.9's split-off): the adapter's timer on the worker's queue,
  and in `:core-common` what one tick does.

#### B.12.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The opt-in | `@SharedReplicaPlatformApi`, `RequiresOptIn(level = ERROR)`: a caller must write `@OptIn(SharedReplicaPlatformApi::class)` | `SharedReplicaPlatform.kt` (`:core-common`, `iosSqliteMain`) |
| The platform seam | `SharedReplicaBackgroundTime`: `begin(reason, onExpired)`, `end(id)`, `backgroundTimeRemainingMs()`. The adapter implements it; a private bridge turns it into the internal `ProtectionAssertions` | same |
| The lifecycle handle | `SharedReplicaLifecycle.create(backgroundTime, workerDispatch)`: one `ReplicaProtection` and one `ReplicaWorker` on that dispatch, behind `install`, `enteredForeground`, `enteredBackground`, `kick`, `foregroundCheckpointTick` and `isForeground`. Its `protection` and `worker` are `internal`, for the binding to attach registries to | same |
| The adapter | `SharedReplicaUiKitAdapter` (internal): the assertions, the notifications, the sampling of `backgroundTimeRemaining`, the timer, `install()` and `wake()`. Over a seam of `UIApplication` (`UiKitApplication`), a worker queue (`ReplicaWorkerQueue`) and a clock | `SharedReplicaUiKitAdapter.kt` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, `iosMain`) |
| The worker's queue | `DispatchReplicaWorkerQueue`: `dispatch_queue_create("org.tenshu.replica.worker")` at `QOS_CLASS_USER_INITIATED`, serial; its repeating timer is a chain of `dispatch_after`s on that queue with a cancel flag | same |
| The 30 s tick | `ReplicaProtection.foregroundCheckpointTick()` calls each live handle's `onForegroundTick`, which a `SharedReplicaStore` sets to `foregroundCheckpoint()`: one `PASSIVE`, in an admission of its own, under the registry's lock, if this handle committed a write since the last tick | `ReplicaProtection.kt`, `SharedReplicaStore.kt`, `ReplicaHandles.kt` |

#### B.12.2 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.11.

156. ⚠⚠ **The public surface is an interface the adapter implements plus an opaque handle made by
     a factory, under an `ERROR`-level opt-in, and nothing else.** `ReplicaProtection`,
     `ProtectionAssertions`, `ProtectionTimer`, `ProtectedWork`, `ReplicaWorker`, the gate and the
     registry stay `internal`. The handle exposes the five calls the platform makes, and
     `isForeground`; it does not expose tokens, `acquire`, `protect`, the latch or the quiesce, so
     a second module cannot take a token or start a shutdown. Every declaration under the opt-in is
     also `@HiddenFromObjC`: `:core-common` is exported to every app framework, and the adapter is
     driven from Kotlin. The adapter itself is `internal` to `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, since
     `FirstPartyLocalRuntime` is in the same module. ⭐ **So no Swift-visible API changes.**
     *Rejected:* making the internals public behind the opt-in (the whole state machine would
     become API), and a new module (the seam would still have to cross `:core-common`'s `internal`).
     *The binding will widen it*, under the same opt-in. It will need, callable from
     `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`:
     - an `attach` of the App Group path's registry to both `lifecycle.protection`
       (`ReplicaProtection.attach`) and `lifecycle.worker` (`ReplicaWorker.attach`), before
       `install`, e.g. `SharedReplicaLifecycle.attach(directory)`;
     - the loops (`ProtectedWork`) passed to `install`;
     - the worker's two outcome callbacks, given to `create`.

     Each is internal to `:core-common` today. That surface is the binding slice's, because what
     each call takes is its decision.
157. **The notifications are `UIApplicationDidEnterBackgroundNotification` and
     `UIApplicationWillEnterForegroundNotification`.** They pair one to one on a real transition.
     `WillResignActive` and `DidBecomeActive` also fire for Control Centre, a call or an alert with
     no suspension in sight, so leaving on the first would quiesce for nothing, and arriving on the
     second would count a "foreground" (B.11 (147)'s hold) that was never left. `DidBecomeActive`
     also fires at launch, which `install` already covers. A foreground launch is `install`'s
     `applicationState != .background`, not a notification. The observers use `queue: nil`, so
     the block runs synchronously on the posting thread, which is main for both: Q3's "in the
     notification" is literal.
158. ⚠ **The worker's queue is serial, the process's own, at `QOS_CLASS_USER_INITIATED`.** Its runs
     take the registry's lock and SQLite's write lock, and a main-thread access then waits behind
     them; a migration run is what "Updating storage…" waits for. At `UTILITY` or `BACKGROUND` the
     run would be throttled (CPU and, at background, I/O) while the main thread waits on it, which is
     a priority inversion `NSRecursiveLock` does not resolve, and the chunk would run past the
     budgets the admission checks assumed (B.7.2). Its competition with the launch is the device's
     to settle (B.11.6 (3), B.12.6).
159. ⚠⚠ **The 30 s trigger: what a tick does is the store's, when it fires is the adapter's.**
     - "Committed since" is this handle's own commits **that wrote** (`seqBumped`, the same
       flag that moves `meta.seq`): an access that only read commits an empty transaction and
       adds nothing to the `-wal`. A sibling's commits are its own tick's.
     - There is no `Wmax/4` threshold: §4.2.1 names none for this trigger, and `afterCommit`
       already covers the log past `Wmax/4`.
     - The store asks the foreground itself, under the registry's lock, from the protection's
       state (B.11 (153)), never the platform. A tick that fired just as the app left the
       foreground then does nothing. Nothing also runs when the handle is fenced, when the tick
       is inside an access on this thread, or at a closed gate.
     - The "since" is cleared only by a tick that runs, whatever the checkpoint's outcome. A
       refused one keeps it, so the next open tick checkpoints. A `PASSIVE` a reader kept short
       is left to the next commit's `Wmax/4` trigger and to the ceiling's `RESTART`.
     - The ticks are serialised behind the worker's runs on one queue, so a long run delays a
       tick. That is accepted: the trigger is opportunistic.
     - A tick that throws is logged and never leaves the tick, since a throw on a dispatch queue
       ends the process.
160. ⚠⚠ **`backgroundTimeRemainingMs()` is a published sample less the monotonic time since.**
     - `UIApplication.backgroundTimeRemaining` is read **only on the main thread**: at `install`;
       before and after `enteredBackground` in its notification; at `WillEnterForeground`; after
       each assertion begun (synchronously when begun on main, otherwise by a
       `dispatch_async` to main that nobody waits for); and in each expiration handler.
     - The sample is a `@Volatile` immutable value. Between samples the value is the last one less
       the monotonic ms since, floored at 0. That is conservative: real background time runs down
       no faster, and a new grant is only ever under-read until its sample lands.
     - **No sample yet is 0**, as a throwing seam is (B.7.1): nothing starts on time nobody can
       name.
     - **"No deadline" is `Long.MAX_VALUE` however long ago it was read.** A reading at or past
       one day (`DBL_MAX`, an infinity) is never converted to ms. A NaN or a negative reading
       is 0.
     - Nothing on this path touches UIKit or waits, so it is safe under the registry's lock and on
       the watchdog's 100 ms poll (B.11.4 (2), (6)).
161. **`beginBackgroundTask` and `endBackgroundTask` are called on whichever thread the store calls
     them** (main for the `background` token, the worker's queue for a job's token, any thread for
     an implicit one). UIKit documents both as safe to call off the main thread, and routing them
     through main would put a main-thread wait under `acquireForJob`, the very thing B.7's
     constraint forbids. `UIBackgroundTaskInvalid` is "no time granted" (null). The platform's
     expiration handler samples (on main) and then calls the store's own, which ends the assertion
     before it returns (70).
162. **At a foreground, the order is: sample, `enteredForeground`, `kick()`, the timer.** The kick
     comes after the gates are open and the foreground is counted, so a job held "until the next
     foreground" (147) runs on that kick. `kick()` only dispatches, so it is safe on main. `install`
     does not kick: nothing is known to the worker before the first open, which schedules its own
     work. **`wake()` kicks from any thread** and is ignored before `install`. The wake's own token
     and the `BGTaskScheduler` registration are PIO-7 PR-6/PR-7's.
163. **`install` is main-only and once, and comes after every registry is attached**
     (`ReplicaProtection.attach` already refuses an attach after install). A background launch
     installs with its gates closed (lease draft §5.3 step 6), starts no timer and does not kick.
164. **No second foreground check in the protection's tick.** A first version also returned 0 from
     `foregroundCheckpointTick()` outside the foreground. No test could tell it apart, because each
     store asks again under its lock, and the store's check is the one that holds against a tick
     that fires as the app leaves. It was removed, not kept untested.

**Fix round of the independent review (2026-10-17).**

165. ⚠⚠ **The elapsed time between samples is measured on a clock that counts through device
     sleep: `clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW)`.** The first version used Kotlin's
     `TimeSource.Monotonic`, an uptime clock on Darwin (libc++'s `steady_clock` there reads
     `CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW`; ⚠ not verified here, since K/N's reading is process-relative). Across a sleep it would
     leave the sample too large, and the store would admit work into time that no longer exists.
     `man clock_gettime` (Darwin): `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` "will continue to increment while the system
     is asleep", `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW` is like it without frequency adjustments, and
     `CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW` (`mach_absolute_time`) "does not increment while the system is asleep".
     A clock that includes sleep can only under-report. On this Mac the two read 268,551 s and
     99,157 s (the host has slept since boot), so the test tells them apart. Whether the
     allowance itself runs down during sleep is a device item (B.12.6).
166. **Smaller:**
     - The `samples` test list is filled only behind `recordSamples` (off in production), so it
       never grows.
     - A tick that throws is caught at both ends: in the adapter's timer block, and in
       `DispatchReplicaWorkerQueue`'s `dispatch_after` chain, which keeps going after a throw.
       `foregroundCheckpointTick()` now also catches the registry and handle listing.
     - `foregroundCheckpoint` says why setting `admitted` from the worker's thread is safe: every
       reader and writer holds the registry's lock, and `depth == 0` means no access of the
       handle is open.

#### B.12.5 Tests and mutations

**`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, new suite `SharedReplicaUiKitAdapterTest`, 13 tests**, over a fake
`UIApplication` whose "main thread" is the test's thread. It answers `isMainThread` for that thread
alone, records any main-only call made from another thread, and runs nothing on main unless the
test drains it. The suite also uses a fake worker queue and timer and a fake clock. Real UIKit is
covered only by the compile and the Swift build.
- **Q3's split:** with the real `SharedReplicaLifecycle`, the background notification begins the
  `background` assertion on the main thread before it returns. Its release, the quiesce, ends that
  assertion off the main thread.
- **Any thread, never main:** `backgroundTimeRemainingMs()` from a real background thread, while
  the main thread is blocked and drains nothing, returns the sampled value less the clock's
  advance, and the platform is never asked off main. An assertion begun off main samples
  through the main queue later and never waits for it.
- **The derivation and the clamp:** the sample less elapsed time, floored at 0. No sample is 0.
  `Double.MAX_VALUE` stays `Long.MAX_VALUE` five seconds later. The conversion maps `DBL_MAX`,
  an infinity and one day to "no deadline", and NaN, negatives and 0 to 0.
- **Expiry:** the platform's handler calls the store's and samples on main. With the real
  lifecycle, the background token's expiry returns only with its assertion ended, exactly once,
  however far its release had got.
- **The transitions:** `install(true)`, `enteredBackground`, `enteredForeground`, `kick`, in that
  order. A background launch installs `false`, with no timer and no kick. A wake kicks from any
  thread and is ignored before `install`. `install` is main-only and once.
- **The 30 s timer:** one 30 s timer on the worker's queue from `install` in the foreground; each
  fire is one tick. It is cancelled at the background, a new one starts at the foreground, and a
  second foreground notification starts no second timer.

**Fix round, `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core` (18 tests):**
- the default clock is `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW`, and not the uptime clock on a host that has slept;
- leaving the foreground samples **before** the store flips, so a reader at the flip sees the
  background's time, not the foreground's "no deadline";
- a foreground before the background's quiesce has ended leaves the process foregrounded, its
  assertion ended exactly once off main, and the timer running;
- outside the tests no sample is kept;
- a throwing tick neither leaves the adapter's timer nor stops the real `dispatch_after` chain.

**`:core-common`, new suite `ReplicaForegroundCheckpointTest`, 8 tests (9 after the fix round)**,
every store made up.
- **A tick after a write** runs one `PASSIVE` in an admission it gives back. The next tick, with
  nothing written, runs none.
- **No checkpoint:** after an access that only reads; outside the foreground, even with a commit
  and a wake's token keeping the gate open; at a closed gate (the commit stays owed, and runs at
  the next open tick); on a fenced store; or inside an access.
- **The store's own check:** with the protection's check bypassed, the store's own foreground
  question still refuses.
- **A throwing tick** is logged and never leaves the tick.
- **The lifecycle surface** drives the same tick.
- *Fix round:* **background, then foreground before the quiesce's drain ends.** Driven through
  the public lifecycle as the adapter drives it, with the real dispatch, and an access held open
  on another thread so the drain is still running. The shutdown ends `REGAINED`, the gate is
  open, the held access commits, and a new access succeeds unfenced. This half is here rather
  than in the adapter's suite because attaching a registry is still internal (156).

### B.13 The binding, behind an off-by-default switch (2026-10-18)

**What it is.** The slice B.12.3 named next: the store connected to the iOS first-party runtime,
**behind a build switch that is off in every build**. With the switch off (every shipped,
TestFlight and App Store build) no app changes: `FirstPartyLocalRuntime` binds
`openFileObjectStore` exactly as before, and no adapter, lifecycle or SQLite file is made. With it
on (a dev build), a route-1 app makes the UIKit adapter at launch, attaches the App Group
`replica/` registry to its lifecycle, installs it with the runtime's loops, and binds
`SharedReplicaStore` in place of the file store. ⚠ The ship blockers of §13 are still open
(B.13.2), so the switch stays off; this slice is what makes the bench pair of §13's S0b-2 row
runnable (B.13.8).

#### B.13.3 The switch, and the proof that "off" is unchanged

- ⚠⚠ **Off is the plist's `"NO"`, and anything that is not exactly `YES`** (a missing key, an
  unset setting's empty string, an unsubstituted `$(…)`, `yes`, `1`).
- **With it off, nothing new runs.** `sqliteBindingFor` answers null without making a binding,
  `assembleBase` binds what it bound before, `purgeCustody` purges as before and makes nothing,
  `wakeSharedReplica` returns. Tests: the switch's parsing; the test host's own plist (no key) is
  off; with the switch off no binding is made on the production path (the factory fails the test
  if called); a test replica directory never takes the SQLite store even with the switch on; the
  custody purge with the switch off. The existing suites (`SyncActivitySharedReplicaTest`, the
  adapter's, every app's `DeclaredServiceVersionsTest`) are unchanged and pass.
- **Entitlements and signing do not change**: the App Group `group.app.tenshu.shared` is in every
  app's simulator and device entitlements already (`ios-signing.md` §6). Only `project.yml` changes:
  in each of the nine apps, one Info.plist key (`TenshuSharedReplicaSqlite:
  $(TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE)`) and one build setting (`TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE: "NO"`)
  in the app target's `settings.base`. `xcodegen` regenerates all nine; the generated plists carry
  the key. Control, the inference harness and the UI-test targets are untouched.
- ⭐ **No threat-model amendment.** A4 and Decision C are unchanged: the keys reach a route-1 app
  as before (`RealmKeyMaterialBridge`, the shared Keychain), the store lives in the same App Group
  container as the file store does, with the same default protection, and nothing key-related is
  written to it. Appendix A (A5, the store at rest) still lands with S0b-4's cutover, which is
  when a default build first writes `replica/`.

#### B.13.4 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.12.

167. ⚠⚠ *(Superseded by B.24, 2026-11-05: the registry's chains are bound and each floor is the oldest version its chain reaches; a store behind is **migrated**, and wiped only below that floor.)* **No migration chain is registered, and each floor is the version itself.** A store behind
     this build is below its floor and is **wiped and re-synced**, never migrated. That is what the
     file store does on iOS today (`PlatformProxyModule`: its migrations config "says *wipe*, not
     *migrate*"), so the switch changes no outcome of a version bump. A floor below the version
     would start a migration that `NoMigrationChains` could only turn into a wipe. The schema
     registry's chains as `ReplicaMigrationSteps` (B.2) are their own slice. An unstamped (new)
     service needs no step: it is stamped with no row read (`ReplicaJobMarkers`).
168. ⚠⚠ *(Superseded by B.14 (189)–(191), 2026-10-23: Control is bound, and its callers with it.)* **Control is not switched; the binding is `FirstPartyLocalRuntime`'s, the nine route-1
     apps'.** §13's rule puts the forget and wipe callers' handling of `WipeNotFinished` in the
     same change that makes the store reachable from them, and those callers are Control's
     (`ForgetThisDevice` from its settings, `ControlSurface.wipeDeviceState`). Not switching Control
     keeps them on the file store, so the rule holds by construction. ⚠ **The cost: a switched phone
     runs two replicas under one device identity** (the switched apps on SQLite, Control and any
     unswitched app on files). Each pulls the realm from the relay. Whether a write on one side
     reaches the other is not determined (B.13.6 Q30). The runbook says to use a throwaway realm.
169. **The loops are the sync runtime's scheduler and schedule drain**, resolved when the protection
     asks (`SyncRuntimeLoops`). `stop()` cancels both and is remembered; `start()` restarts only
     after such a stop, so a foreground never starts a loop that the runtime's own election did not.
     ⚠ `awaitStopped` returns at once: neither loop exposes the job it cancelled, and waiting needs
     a change to `:sync-service-proxy`. What waits for an in-flight tick's store access is the
     gate's drain after it (10 s). The loops are bound after the graph, so a foreground launch's
     `start()` at `install` finds none, which is right: the runtime starts them itself. A later
     assembly in the process rebinds them.
170. **`isProtectedDataAvailable` is the main thread's last reading**, taken at `install` and at
     `UIApplicationProtectedDataDidBecomeAvailable` / `…WillBecomeUnavailable`, and read by the store
     from any thread. ⚠ No reading yet is **false**: the store reads "locked" as "retry later",
     never as damage, so false is the safe error. `WillBecomeUnavailable` is posted before the data
     goes, so the sample is never "available" while it is not.
171. ⚠⚠ **With the switch on, the custody purge wipes the store first (the D3 order, §5.1).** Control
     tearing the provisioning down (a reset, a forget, a sign-out) wipes Control's file store; a
     switched app's SQLite store would otherwise keep the old realm's rows under a purged custody,
     the state D3 forbids. `purgeCustody` runs the store-less wipe, and **keeps custody** when it
     throws `WipeNotFinished` or anything else: the purge then runs again at the next launch, and
     `meta.wipe` makes the next open finish the wipe first. It returns whether it purged (it
     returned nothing before; no caller reads it yet). A sign-out therefore re-syncs a switched
     app, which is the safe direction for a dev build.
172. ⚠⚠ **Q24's assertion is the production open's, for every process, and the binding's refusal in
     an extension.** `SharedReplicaStore.open` and `wipeSharedReplica` refuse a registry that is not
     under an **installed** protection (`ReplicaGateProtection.isInstalled`, true by default for the
     tests' stand-ins, the protection's own state otherwise). The suites open through
     `ReplicaOpener` on registries of their own and never meet it. And `installAtLaunch` refuses in
     a process whose bundle is an `.appex` before it makes anything, since the adapter needs
     `UIApplication.sharedApplication`. Today no extension links the runtime.
173. **An open that cannot hand out a store ends the app's `install()`.** A wipe the open handed to
     the worker is waited for on the calling (main) thread, at most 10 s, on the worker's outcome;
     a finished job is opened again once. `Skew`, `Corrupt`, a stopped run or the deadline throw
     `SharedReplicaNotReady` with the reason, which each app's `install()` logs before it rethrows.
     The surfaces ("Refreshing…", the update surface) are S0b-3's. A small wipe is about 40 ms per
     1,000 rows (§5.1), far inside the launch watchdog.
174. **One runtime handle per path per process (§2.8): the binding keeps the store it opened** and
     hands the same one to a later assembly (a re-provision in the same process). A fenced store is
     released and opened anew; a graph still holding the fenced one is S0b-3's rebuild.
175. **The outcomes reach the host as a summary**, `SharedReplicaJobOutcome`, not the worker's
     internal outcome types, so B.12 (156)'s "nothing else of the store is API" still holds.
176. **The directory is `<group container>/replica/`**, beside the file store's `objects/` (§2.2's
     name). Not added to the legacy reclaimer's list: that list is the app-local leftovers of a
     pre-App-Group build, and `replica/` never lived there.
177. **Smaller:** the adapter's `install(driver, loops)` keeps `driver` first for its suite;
     `create`'s new callback is last, so the two trailing-lambda callers in the tick's suite name
     `workerDispatch`. The custody purge's binding is the process's one, made on first use, so a
     launch that deprovisions before any assembly installs it then.

**Carry-overs from B.12's review:** the mid-drain test's deadlines are 30 s (they were 5 s); and
the dispatch chain's throwing-block test routes each tick through an `outermost` seam of
`DispatchReplicaWorkerQueue`, so a removed guard is caught there and fails the test (M243) instead
of ending the test process.

**Fix round of the independent review (2026-10-19).** "Off" was verified unchanged; four
items for "on", and the maintainer's D14.

178. ⚠⚠ **The custody purge's wipe is handed to the worker.** The first version ran the whole
     store-less wipe inline (`ReplicaOpener.wipeAdmitted` → `replacement.run()`), from
     `deprovision()`, which runs on the main thread at launch (the bridge-vanished gate). A large
     replica would trip the 20 s launch watchdog at every launch, since `meta.wipe` survives and the
     next launch deprovisions again. Now `startWipeSharedReplica` classifies, commits the first chunk
     (the marker and the epoch) on the caller and hands the rest to the worker
     (`SharedReplicaWipeStart.HANDED_OFF`); `purgeCustody` answers "not purged" at once and **keeps
     custody**. The keys go on the worker's queue when the wipe is told `REPLACEMENT_FINISHED`, and
     only if Control's bridge is **still gone** then (a re-provision meanwhile keeps the new
     adoption). A run that stops leaves custody and `meta.wipe`; the next launch's deprovision joins
     the wipe. ⚠ A re-provision that writes custody keys **before** the bridge, racing the purge,
     can have keys it had just written deleted: recoverable, since the next launch re-adopts from
     the bridge. The purge asks again after it ran and logs that case; it does not repair it. The purge is owed **before** the wipe starts, so a worker that finishes before the
     start returns still finds it (⚠ that ordering has no test: it needs a worker that runs inside
     the start). A hand-off with no worker attached is refused.
179. ⚠⚠ **D14 (decided by the maintainer 2026-10-19): a store that can never be wiped has its files
     deleted, then custody is purged.** A refusal for `Corrupt` or `Skew` deletes every file of
     `replica/` (`deleteSharedReplicaFiles`). §5's rule "never unlink under open connections" is
     kept by proving there are none, with SQLite's own locks rather than a new mechanism:
     - this process's runtime handle is released first, and the registry must hold no handle (a
       worker's run counts), under the registry's lock, held to the end;
     - a connection of its own runs `PRAGMA journal_mode = DELETE`, which leaves WAL only when it is
       the one connection on the database: **any other connection, in any process, idle or not,
       refuses it**. Measured on the simulator: with an idle sibling connection the pragma fails
       `SQLITE_BUSY` (it does not answer `wal`), so the deletion answers `BUSY` with nothing touched
       and the sibling still reads its rows. The `wal` answer (SQLite's documented alternative)
       and a refused `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` are kept as further refusals; with the `BUSY` first,
       neither is reachable in a test (M248, M264). ⭐ Recorded as **covered by stronger guards**
       (the second review): the registry's handle check sees this process's handles, a
       connection opened and never read included, whose locks POSIX would not report; the
       `fcntl` probe of (184) sees every other process's; and `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` makes an open that
       starts after the pragma wait rather than read. Then `locking_mode = EXCLUSIVE` and `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`,
       and the unlinks under that lock;
     - ~~a file SQLite cannot read as a database (`NOTADB`, a damaged header) cannot be connected
       to usefully by anyone, and is unlinked without the proof~~ ⚠⚠ *wrong, and replaced in (184):
       a sibling that opened before the damage keeps a working connection on its cached pages.*
     *Why not the wipe's own machinery:* the epoch and the marker fence a sibling only through a
     write to the store, and these are exactly the stores this build may not write (a newer one) or
     cannot (a corrupt one). *Why not rename aside:* a connection keeps its descriptors through a
     rename as through an unlink, the same ghost. **Edge cases:** a sibling with the store open
     makes the deletion `BUSY`: custody kept, the next deprovision tries again (that sibling is
     about to deprovision too, since the bridge is gone for all). ⚠ A sibling whose open begins in
     the milliseconds between the exclusive lock and the unlink reads the old inode once the lock
     goes, with no marker beside it; accepted, for the same reason. The deletion leaves Appendix
     A's A5 at rest no worse: the files are gone. **A4 is kept, not changed** (no custody at rest
     once Control cleared the bridge, now also over such a store): no threat-model amendment.
180. ⚠⚠ **The switch binds only on the dev lab's relay.** Two replicas under Control's one device
     id (168) can corrupt a real realm: the same `(deviceId, HLC)` can carry different ops; the
     per-device relay cursor the reclamation barrier reads is moved by whichever store acked last,
     so content can be reclaimed from under the other store for good; and the roster sees one
     device acting as two. So `SharedReplicaSwitch.allows` needs the plist's `YES` **and** a relay
     whose host is `tenshu.xyz` or under it, where no real realm lives. *Chosen over a second plist
     key* because the relay is reliably known at that point: a route-1 app's relay is
     `PlatformProxyModule`'s production constant unless `TENSHU_DEV_RELAY` overrides it, and that
     override is honoured by **debug binaries only** (`devRelayOverride`), so no release build can
     ever pass. It is checked twice: against the `relayBaseUrl` the runtime passes `assembleBase`
     (before the adapter is made) and against the graph's own `syncRelayUrl` when the store is
     bound (an override module could repoint it). A `YES` with another relay logs why and uses the
     file store.
181. ⚠⚠ **A store the open cannot hand out never crashes the launch.** `SharedReplicaNotReady` (a
     `Skew`, a `Corrupt`, an `Updating` with no worker or past its wait), or any other failure of
     the open, threw out of Koin's resolution of `ObjectStore` and ended every launch. It is now
     caught where the store is bound: **this launch uses the file store**, with a loud line, and
     `DatabaseLock` follows the store actually bound. (Since (180) that file store is the dev
     lab's realm's.) The surfaces stay S0b-3's. ⚠ *Superseded by B.17 (254), Q40 (2026-10-28):*
     still never a crash, but the stand-in, never the file store, for every refusal.
183. ⚠⚠ **The deferred purge is bound to its own wipe** (the second review). Any
     `REPLACEMENT_FINISHED` used to release it, so an earlier migration or wipe job of the same
     store finishing after the hand-off would purge custody while this wipe's chunks were still
     pending: custody gone over a present store, which D3 forbids. Now each `ReplicaReplacement`
     has a `jobId` (process-unique, never reused), the outcome carries it, and
     `startWipeSharedReplica` tells the caller the handed-off job's id **before the dispatch**
     (`beforeHandOff`), where the binding owes the purge to that id alone. A worker that runs the
     whole wipe before the start returns still finds it (tested with a dispatch that runs inline,
     which also closes (178)'s untested ordering). ⚠ When the worker's "latest job wins" (B.11)
     replaces the handed-off job with a newer one of the store (an open during the wipe hands its
     own over), the purge's job never finishes: custody is kept for this launch and the purge is
     redone at the next deprovision. **Late, never early.**
184. ⚠⚠ **The deletion proves no other process holds a SQLite lock, without SQLite** (the second
     review). The two branches that skipped (179)'s proof could unlink under a live sibling:
     *any* open failure deleted (a `CANTOPEN` while protected data is unavailable at a background
     launch, `EMFILE`, a sandbox refusal), and a damaged header deleted without the lock, though a
     sibling that opened before the damage keeps a working connection on its cached pages and its
     own `-wal`/`-shm` descriptors, would pass its marker check after the unlink, write into the
     ghost, and could even write `CORRUPT` from it and fence the fresh store. Now:
     - **every open failure, and every pragma failure but `NOTADB`/`CORRUPT`, answers `BUSY`**;
     - before any descriptor of SQLite's on the files (closing one drops every lock the process
       holds on that file), POSIX write locks are taken **without waiting** on exactly the bytes
       SQLite's unix VFS locks, verified in the vendored `sqlite3.c`: `objects.db`'s
       `[PENDING_BYTE, SHARED_FIRST + SHARED_SIZE)` = `[0x40000000, +512)` (16727-16733), which
       every reader and writer holds while it reads or writes, and `-shm`'s dead-man switch, byte
       128 (`UNIX_SHM_DMS`, 44799-44800, asserted at 48762), which **every connection with the WAL
       index open holds for its life, idle or not**. A lock any other process holds fails the take:
       `BUSY`. Taken (`F_SETLK`, which both tests and holds; the review's `F_GETLK` only tests),
       they also make an open that starts meanwhile fail its first lock, until SQLite's own locks
       on this process's connection take over (a POSIX unlock by SQLite is the process's);
     - so a damaged header reaches the unlinks only once no other process holds either lock.
     ⚠ POSIX does not report this process's own locks; the registry's handle check covers those.
     ⚠ That check is `ReplicaHandles.forPath`'s registry, **keyed by the path string**: `/var/…`
     and `/private/var/…` would be two registries, the second's handles uncounted. The binding
     always passes the one App Group path (`sharedReplicaDirectory("replica")`), so it never meets it.
     Tested with a **forked child process** holding each range (the simulator allows `fork`):
     `BUSY` and nothing deleted, then `DELETED` once it exits. ⚠ Device item B.13.8 (9).
186. ⚠⚠ **"Not a database" is decided without SQLite** (the third review). In (184)'s
     damaged-header branch the deletion's own SQLite connection replaced the probe's write locks
     (POSIX locks are the process's, not the descriptor's: SQLite's SHARED read on the lock range and
     its `-shm` downgrade took their place), and released them on the failed read, so nothing was
     held at the unlink. Now the 16-byte magic (`SQLite format 3\0`) is read with `pread` through the
     probe's own descriptor; a file without it is unlinked with the probe's locks held and SQLite
     never opens it (tested: a forked child cannot take the range at the moment of the unlink, and
     the connection seam is never called). An empty file is SQLite's empty database and goes the
     readable path. The readable path is unchanged (the pragma, then `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`). ~~Every
     pragma failure is now `BUSY`: a damaged header behind a valid magic keeps its files and
     custody~~ ⚠⚠ *that regressed D14 (the fourth review): such a store is `WipeRefused(Corrupt)`
     and was never deleted, custody kept for good. Replaced by (188).* A failed `pread` (`-1`, an
     `EIO`) is `BUSY`, never "not SQLite"; `0` bytes is the empty database.
187. ⚠⚠ **The cached store is released when the custody wipe starts**. A switched
     app deprovisioned and provisioned again without process death got the cached pre-wipe store
     back from the binding; once the wipe moved `meta.epoch`, its first access threw
     `ReplicaReplaced`, past (181)'s fallback, and the runtime was unusable until a restart.
     Released *at the start*, not at the finish: from the first chunk on the store is being
     replaced, and an assembly during the wipe must get the open's own answer, `Updating` (waited
     for, or the file-store fallback), never the old handle. Tested: deprovision, then an open
     and a whole assembly during the wipe (`NotReady`, the file store), then after it a fresh,
     unfenced, empty store.
188. ⚠⚠ **A valid magic over a header or schema SQLite cannot read is deleted, under the probe's
     locks taken again** (the fourth review; D14 kept). On a pragma or `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`
     failure that is `CORRUPT` or `NOTADB` **only**: SQLite's connection is closed, which drops
     every lock this process holds on the file; the probe's write locks are taken again with
     `F_SETLK` on the probe's still-open descriptors (`objects.db`'s range, `-shm`'s byte 128); all
     taken, the unlinks run under them; any refused (a process that opened in between), `BUSY`.
     Every other code (`BUSY`, `LOCKED`, `CANTOPEN`, `IOERR`) stays `BUSY`. Tested with a database
     made in rollback mode, its magic intact and page 1's b-tree header overwritten (its schema
     read fails `CORRUPT`, asserted): deleted with no other process holding a lock, `BUSY` with a
     forked child holding the range. That test failed on the previous tree, which is the
     regression, before the fix. Custody's purge follows a `DELETED` as for every unwipeable
     store (179's binding tests). ⚠ The lock test's helper opens and closes a descriptor of its
     own on the file, which drops the probe's locks: it proves them held **up to** `beforeUnlink`,
     after every SQLite decision, not through the unlink itself.
185. **Smaller:** `installAtLaunch()` runs inside the purge's `try`, so an extension or an off-main
     call answers "not purged" instead of throwing out of `deprovision()`;
     `ReplicaGateProtection.isInstalled` has no default (a stand-in says what it is).

#### B.13.7 Tests and mutations

**`:core-common`, new suite `SharedReplicaBindingSurfaceTest`, 9 tests**, through the production
entries and the process's registry for each made-up path:
- the production open with no protection attached is refused and creates nothing; attached but not
  installed, the same; the store-less wipe with no protection, the same;
- attach, then install, then open serves a store, and the store-less wipe is admitted after it;
- an attach after install, and a second attach of one directory, are refused;
- the loops start at a foreground install, stop at the background, and start again at the
  foreground; a background launch starts none;
- a wipe the open handed to the worker is told to the host as `REPLACEMENT_FINISHED` for that
  path, and the store opens after it, without the rows;
- every run and walk outcome maps to its kind, and `reopen` only for a finish or a clean walk.

**`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, new suite `SharedReplicaBindingTest`, 22 tests**, over a fake
`UIApplication` (its "main thread" the test's), the adapter's real worker queue, and real stores:
- the switch: the exact `YES` only; the test host's plist is off; off, no binding is made on the
  production path; a test replica directory never takes the SQLite store; the custody purge off;
- switched on, a whole assembly binds `SharedReplicaStore` as `ObjectStore` with its own
  `databaseLock`, in the binding's directory, attached and installed first; a second assembly gets
  the same store and makes no second adapter;
- Q24: an extension makes no adapter, attaches nothing, and never opens; `installAtLaunch` is
  main-only and once; an open before it is refused;
- a wipe handed to the worker is waited for and the store opens; a newer build's store is not handed
  out; a released store is opened anew and a live one handed out again;
- **kick at foreground:** a wipe whose run was refused protected time stops; the next foreground's
  kick runs it to its finish. **And at a wake**, the same;
- protected data: no reading is false, `install` reads it, the notifications move it;
- the open's wait is answered by a `REPLACEMENT` outcome, not by a walk's told meanwhile;
- the custody purge goes on only when the wipe finished; switched on, custody is kept over an
  unfinished wipe and purged once the store is gone;
- the loops: started again only after rule P stopped them; no runtime and a throwing loop contained;
  the deferred loops delegate once bound and a later bind replaces.

   over 1 s. ⚠ "A task expiry simulated while foregrounded" needs a wake or the debugger. ⚠ §13 says
   the device steps before S0b-4 use the bench apps on their own group; a switched pair runs on
   the product group instead, which is why the runbook asks for a throwaway realm (168).
2. Every item of B.12.6 is reachable through a switched build, and B.5.6's, B.8.7's, B.9.5's,
   B.10.5's and B.11.6's with it.
3. **The protected-data sample on a locked phone** (170): lock with the app in the background,
   wait past the notification, and check that a failure is read as "locked", not as damage.
4. **The wait at launch** (173): the time a switched app's launch spends in a handed-off wipe, at
   the store sizes Q0 (u) measured.
5. **Q24 in a real extension**, when one exists: the refusal in its log, and nothing in `replica/`.
6. **Q30**: on a switched phone, a write in a switched app and whether Control shows it.
7. ⚠ **The data-protection class of the new files** (B.13's review): `objects.db`, `-wal`, `-shm`
   and the marker in `replica/` must read back the same class as the file store's files in
   `objects/` (the container's default today, `CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication`; D3 sets it
   explicitly in S0b-4). `getattrlist`/`NSURLFileProtectionKey` on the phone, after a first launch.
8. **The custody purge on the phone** (178, 179): a deprovision with a large switched store returns
   inside the launch, custody goes once the worker's wipe ends; a corrupt or newer store's files are
   deleted with no sibling running, and kept (custody too) with one in the foreground.
9. **The lock probe on the phone** (184): a sibling app in the background with the store open
   (its DMS lock held through a suspension) makes the deletion `BUSY`; and the probe's `open` of
   `-shm` is allowed by the device's sandbox in the App Group container.

### B.14 Control's binding, its forget over the shared store, and one replica per phone (2026-10-23)

**What it is.** The slice Q27 chose (decided by the maintainer 2026-10-22): **Control is bound
behind the same switch**, so that with the switch on every first-party process uses the same
replica, and **Control's forget wipes the shared store for every app before it purges custody**
(§13's rule, which B.13 (168) had kept true by leaving Control on the file store). With the switch
off nothing changes, Control included.

#### B.14.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Control's switch | `TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE: "NO"` in `control-ios/project.yml`'s app target `settings.base`, written into the Info.plist key `TenshuSharedReplicaSqlite` (the nine apps' pattern). Only the exact `YES`, and only with the dev lab's relay (`TENSHU_DEV_RELAY`, debug binaries only) | `control-ios/project.yml`; `SharedReplicaSwitch` |
| `ControlSharedReplica` | Control's use of the one `SharedReplicaBinding` per process: `runtimeModule()` (installs the binding at `installRealRuntime`, on main, before the graph; the store's bindings, or null for the file store), `bindLoops`, `wake` (from Control's background refresh), `liveFileStoreToWipe`, `wipeForForget` and `wipeThenPurgeCustody`. Public but `@HiddenFromObjC`: Swift never sees it | `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, `ControlSharedReplica.kt` |
| The store's bindings, one copy | `sharedReplicaStoreModule(binding, fallback, onBound)`: the SQLite `ObjectStore` (or B.13 (181)'s file-store fallback) and the `DatabaseLock` that follows it, moved out of `FirstPartyLocalRuntime`, now used by the nine apps and by Control | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| The replica choice | `<group container>/replica.choice`: Control declares `sqlite`, `files` or `reset`; a switched app binds SQLite only on a `sqlite` reading with no file-store write since (190) | `SharedReplicaChoice.kt`; `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.sqliteBindingForAssembly` |
| The custody wipe, three answers | `SharedReplicaBinding.startCustodyWipe` (`PURGE_NOW`, `HANDED_OFF`, `KEEP`), with an `onNotFinished` told the handed-off job's other outcomes; `wipeBeforeCustodyPurge` (the apps' purge) is it, unchanged in behaviour | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| Control's forget | `ControlSurface.wipeDeviceState`: the bridge cleared, the row retired, the queues purged, the file store wiped (never the SQLite store, `liveFileStoreToWipe`), then `wipeThenPurgeCustody { custody + mock account }`; "⚠ not finished" returned with custody kept | `ControlSurface.kt` |
| The common half (§5.1 steps 3 and 4) | `StoreWipeNotFinished` in `:core-common` (`WipeNotFinished` extends it); `ForgetThisDeviceImplementation` tells it apart, keeps custody and says "⚠ not finished"; `StoreHandleFenced` (`ReplicaReplaced` extends it) is the one refusal `SyncManagerImpl.forgetThisDevice`'s cursor reset tolerates (192, as revised) | `WipeableObjectStore.kt`, `ForgetThisDeviceImplementation.kt`, `SyncManager(Impl).kt` |

#### B.14.2 The switch, and "off" unchanged

- ⚠⚠ **Off, Control is exactly as before.** `runtimeModule()` is null (the graph is
  `runtimeModules()` alone, the list `ControlDeclaredServiceVersionsTest` pins), `bindLoops` and
  `wake` do nothing, `wipeThenPurgeCustody` runs the custody purge at once, and
  `liveFileStoreToWipe` is the `as? WipeableObjectStore` it replaces. Nothing is made, read or written
  (the test's factories fail if called), beyond reading the plist key and the debug-only relay
  variable.
- **Entitlements and signing do not change.** The App Group is in both of Control's entitlements
  files already. `project.yml` gains one Info.plist key and one build setting; nothing else in
  `control-ios/` changes, and **no Swift source changes**.
- ⭐ **No change to A4 or Decision C**, and nothing key-related reaches the container: the choice
  file holds one word. The threat model's A4 paragraph on "Forget this device" gains one sentence:
  on a switched dev build Control keeps its custody when the shared store's wipe did not finish
  (D3's order, §5.1), which narrows nothing it promises.

#### B.14.3 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.13.

189. ⚠⚠ **Control is bound with the apps' switch, guard and binding, not a fork of them.** The
     store's two bindings moved into `sharedReplicaStoreModule`, used by both; Control's graph is
     `runtimeModules()` plus that module last. Control installs the binding **whatever the choice
     says** (190), because its forget needs the protection and the worker even on a launch that runs
     the file store. Rule P's loops are bound only over the SQLite store; a file-store launch keeps
     today's loop behaviour. Control's background refresh (`runPendingRequestRefresh`) is a wake, as
     Drive's is. The store records Control as `app.tenshu.control.ios`, its `platformPackageName`.
190. ⚠⚠ **One replica per phone: Control declares, the apps follow, and any write to the file store
     turns the SQLite store off (the mixed-switch rule).** Control on with an app off, or an app on
     with Control off, would otherwise run both replicas under one device id, the corruption (180)
     names. The off path cannot help (it must stay unchanged), so the rule is enforced from the
     switched side with what the off side already does:
     - a switched Control writes `replica.choice` with what it bound, `sqlite` or `files`, when the
       store is resolved; a switched app binds SQLite **only on a `sqlite` reading**, else the file
       store with a loud line;
     - ⚠⚠ **a `sqlite` or `reset` declaration whose file store has changed since reads as
       `FILE_STORE_WRITTEN_SINCE`.** Every write of `FileObjectStore` is a create, an atomic rename or
       an unlink in `objects/`, each of which changes the directory (tested: a new row, a row written
       over, a row deleted; a read does not). How "changed" is judged is (197). So an unswitched app, an
       unswitched Control, a switched launch that fell back (181), and a `YES` the relay guard
       refused all turn it off, and Control, at its next runtime install, joins the file store and
       declares `files`: the phone converges on one replica, the file one, which is the safe
       direction;
     - **sticky:** `files` stays until Control's forget writes `reset`, from which the next switched
       Control launch starts again from SQLite, unless the file store changes first. No app follows
       a `reset` until Control has declared. Nothing declared has no recorded file store to compare
       with: it is the first switched launch, and the declaration it writes once bound is the
       reference from then on;
     - an app's custody purge does not read the choice: a store a switched app once wrote is wiped
       before custody goes whatever the choice says now.
     ⚠ **What it does not cover, accepted under the dev-lab guard (180):** the window between a
     file-store write and each bound process's next foreground (196), and a switched process's own
     fallback launch (181), which ends at its next launch.
     *Chosen over refusing a mixed state outright* because the switched side cannot see an
     unswitched process at all; *over a heartbeat or a lease* because those need the off path to
     write. The choice file is outside `replica/`, whose files D14's deletion removes.
191. ⚠⚠ **Control's forget wipes the shared store through the worker and waits for that job.**
     `wipeForForget`, between the file-store wipe and the custody purge of `wipeDeviceState`, on
     every switched launch whatever store Control's graph runs on (`replica/` may hold the realm
     being left):
     - the start on the main thread (`withContext(Dispatchers.Main)`: the binding installs there,
       and the first chunk, the marker and the epoch, is short), with this process's cached store
       released first (187), so Control's own graph is fenced before the wipe;
     - the rest handed to the worker, as the apps' purge does (178); the forget **waits, suspended,
       never blocking main**, for that job's own outcome (183's job id), at most `FORGET_WAIT_MS`
       (120 s): §5.1's contract that the forget reports a wipe only once it has happened;
     - ⚠⚠ **custody goes only on a finished wipe, no store, or an unwipeable store's files deleted
       (D14, (179), (188))**. A stopped run, a refusal, a deletion that found the store open, a
       failure or the deadline keep custody, and the forget returns "⚠ not finished — …; try
       again" (the `⚠` marker of the forget notice). `wipeThenPurgeCustody` is the one place the
       purge is gated; the marker stays, so any qualifying open finishes the wipe, and the repeated
       forget completes;
     - every exit declares `reset` (190): the file-store wipe just before it moved `objects/`.
     **Siblings** meet the first chunk's epoch at their next access: their handle fences
     `REPLACED`, reads answer absent, and their binding opens anew, never handing out the stale
     store (tested with a sibling on its own registry over the same files).
192. **The common half of §13's rule.** `ForgetThisDeviceImplementation` catches
     `StoreWipeNotFinished` as a third outcome: no step 4, custody kept, "⚠ not finished".
     ~~After a wipe that returned true it calls `forgetThisDevice(storeWiped = true)`, which skips the
     cursor reset~~ ⚠⚠ *withdrawn in review: the reset closes the window in which a pull
     tick writes a non-zero cursor into the freshly wiped store, on every platform, and skipping it
     after every wipe reopened that desync off iOS.* Now **the reset always runs**, and only its
     refusal by a handle that no longer serves is tolerated: `StoreHandleFenced` (common; the iOS
     store's `ReplicaReplaced` extends it, and no other store throws it), told and never thrown past
     the purge. Off iOS the forget is the code master had. ⚠ **No iOS caller reaches the op today**
     (every Swift forget is `wipeDeviceState`), so §5.1's iOS-only `onForgetSharedCustody` hook is
     not built; it is owed the day an iOS surface calls `ForgetThisDevice`.
193. ⚠ **Control's own graph is not rebuilt after its forget.** The released store answers absent
     and refuses writes (`ReplicaReplaced`), so a genesis in the same process fails until Control
     is relaunched. Rebuilding a fenced graph is S0b-3's (§6). Until then: the
     forget's answer ends "quit and reopen Tenshu Control before setting it up again" on every
     switched forget, and the forget **retires the old graph's sync loops for good**
     (`DeferredReplicaLoops.retire`: stopped, and no later foreground or bind starts them), so
     nothing of the old graph spins against the released store. The post-forget surfaces
     (onboarding's genesis, pairing, the landing probe) reach the store only through operations, whose
     catch-all (`LocalTaskExecutor`) turns the refusal into a failed result, never a crash; the
     direct reads of the store (`rehydrateSharedReplica`) answer -1 for it (*Read*, from
     `ControlSurface`; not exercised by a test). ⚠ Not run on a device
     (B.14.7 (3)). The file store's path is unchanged.
194. **A late finish never purges Control's custody behind the forget.** The job's `onFinished` only
     completes the forget's wait; a run that stopped and is finished by a later kick leaves custody
     to the repeated forget. Automatic completion of an interrupted forget stays the tech-debt
     follow-up §5.1 names.
195. **The other wipe callers, checked against §13's rule.** On iOS "Start fresh" (the reinstall
     gate) and the locked screen's forget are `wipeDeviceState`; the realm data reset deletes rows
     through ops and never wipes; `discardSupersededRealm` writes the live store and never wipes;
     the debug `-clearDriveSession` clears the bridge only, after which each switched app's purge
     wipes (Q28). ⚠ The dev write probe (`-appGroupWrite`) still writes `objects/` with its own lock:
     on a switched phone it turns the SQLite store off (190), which is safe; its deletion is owed with
     S0b-4, when the file store goes. (Deleted 2026-11-05, with the rest of `AppGroupProbe`.)

196. ⚠⚠ **Every bound process re-reads the choice at each foreground** (bound
     processes never re-checked, so a file-store write left two replicas in steady state). The
     binding is told at every `WillEnterForeground` (the adapter's `onForeground`, after the
     worker's kick); a process whose open SQLite store the choice no longer allows (an app: anything
     but `sqlite`; Control: `files` or a file-store change since) **fences it**: the store is
     released (reads answer absent, writes refused), its loops retired, a loud line logged, and
     Control declares `files` so the apps follow at their own foreground. *Why fencing mid-process
     is acceptable:* it is the state a sibling's wipe already leaves a graph in (§6), every write
     path already meets it, and the alternative is a second replica until the next launch. The next
     launch binds the file store. ⚠ The residual window is the time between a file-store write and
     each bound process's next foreground (a process that stays foregrounded keeps serving until it
     is backgrounded once).
197. ⚠⚠ **"Changed since" is an inequality over the directory's identity, never a clock ordering**
     (a clock set back made a write look older than the declaration, a false
     "unchanged" in the unsafe direction). Each declaration records `objects/` as one `stat`:
     `dev:ino:mtime_ns:ctime_ns`, or `absent`; a reading whose current record differs in any field
     is "written since". The status-change time is set only by the kernel, so a write whose
     modification time is put back to the recorded one is still seen (tested with `utimensat`); a
     directory removed and remade changes its inode. A declaration with no record reads as written.
     The declaration is read through one descriptor (`open`/`read`), and replaced whole by an atomic
     write, so a reading never mixes two declarations; its own modification time is no longer used.
198. **D14 from Control, told apart.** A store that can never be wiped whose deletion is refused
     because it is open in another process (`CustodyWipe.KEEP_BUSY`) is the likely case while apps
     are resident, so the forget's "not finished" says "close the other Tenshu apps and try again".

| Q32 | Is the file store's directory time the right "someone runs the file store" signal (190), and is `files` being sticky until a forget acceptable? | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-23: the recommendation** (hardened by (196), (197) in the same spirit). **Yes, for the dev switch.** It needs nothing from the off path and errs toward one replica; a dev who sees `CONTROL USES THE FILE STORE` resets with Forget this device. 1. **The whole phone switched** (Control and the nine apps, [`how-to/s0b-switched-build.md`](../how-to/s0b-switched-build.md)):
   Control's output shows no `CONTROL USES THE FILE STORE` line, each app's shows no
   `THIS APP USES THE FILE STORE` line, and `replica.choice` reads `sqlite`.
2. **Q30, measured** (the runbook's section): a write in Control seen in a switched app and back,
   with both on the SQLite store, and the same with one of them made to fall back.
3. **The forget on the phone** (191): a large switched store; the time `wipeDeviceState` spends in
   the worker's wipe, a sibling app open in the foreground meanwhile (it shows its fallback line or
   waits, and is never handed the old store), and a forget backgrounded mid-wipe reporting
   "not finished" with Control's custody kept.
4. **The mixed state** (190): Control switched and Drive unswitched; after Drive's first sync,
   Control's next launch logs `CONTROL USES THE FILE STORE` and every switched app follows; a
   forget then a relaunch of a fully switched set returns to `sqlite`.
5. Every item of B.13.8, now with Control on the same replica.

### B.15 Entries wrapped, and the general token-expiry interrupt (2026-10-23)

**What it is.** The slice B.13.5 and B.14.4 named next, behind the same off-by-default switch:
- **Every entry wrapped.** Each way a process's work reaches the shared store in the background
  now runs under protection: an explicit token for the entries the lease draft's §5.4 lists, a
  job's token for the worker's runs, the implicit token at the gate for anything else, and none
  for the foreground's UI paths, which have no deadline (B.7). The table below is every entry,
  found by reading the runtime wiring.
- **The general token-expiry interrupt** (B.9, B.10 and B.11 split it off): when the protection
  that covers the store's work ends with nothing left to cover a lock, every transaction of the
  process is stopped before the drain, so the drain waits for rollbacks and nothing holds a file
  lock into suspension (`0xdead10cc`). **And a job's own token** reaches its own run's statements,
  the chunks' and the checkpointer's (B.11's split).
- **Three carry-overs:** the runbook's warning about the dev write probes, `ForgetWipe`'s explicit
  `relaunchControl`, and `awaitStopped` that waits (B.13 (169)).

⚠ With the switch off nothing changes: no binding is installed, so `SharedReplicaEntries`
runs every block as it is, and the interrupt lives in the store, which only a switched build
opens.

#### B.15.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The entry's token | `SharedReplicaLifecycle.protectEntry(reason, onExpired)`: one assertion (`entry:<reason>`) behind an opaque `SharedReplicaEntryToken`, under the same `ERROR`-level opt-in and `@HiddenFromObjC` | `SharedReplicaPlatform.kt` (`:core-common`) |
| The wrapper | `SharedReplicaEntries.withProtection(reason) { … }`: the token taken off the main thread before the block, released after it (off the main thread, before it returns); null when no time is granted (the block never runs) or the token expired (the block is cancelled). Unwrapped when no binding is installed | `SharedReplicaEntries.kt` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`) |
| The binding's half | `SharedReplicaBinding.protectEntry`, for an installed binding only | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| The interrupt, store-wide | `ReplicaHoldWatchdog.expireAll(why)` and `endExpiry()`: every hold armed now, and every one armed until the end, past its deadline at once. `ReplicaHold.expire(why)`: a running statement interrupted (again every `REINTERRUPT_MS` while it runs), the next statement and the `COMMIT` refused | `ReplicaHoldWatchdog.kt` |
| The interrupt's trigger | `ReplicaProtection`'s shutdown with `interrupt = true` (the expiry that ends protection, the background with no time granted), issued in step 4 under the state lock; an expiry during its own release's drain, at once or at its quiesce's close; the expiry ended in the quiesce's `finally` before the gates reopen. `expiryInterrupts` for the tests and the log | `ReplicaProtection.kt` |
| A job's own token | `ReplicaExpiryScope`: the holds a job arms on its thread while its run goes on are the scope's; the job token's expiration handler expires them, and any armed after, whatever else protects. The worker wraps the `REPLACEMENT` run (with its end-of-job checkpoint) and the walk's run in one | `ReplicaHoldWatchdog.kt`, `ReplicaConfirmationWalk.kt` (`ReplicaWorker`) |
| The refusal | `ProtectionExpired`, a `HoldCeilingExceeded` by kind (now `open`), so every handler of the watchdog already treats it: rule (a) for an access, `ChunkStop("ProtectionExpired")` for a job's chunk, a retryable `StoreUnavailable` for the open (not counted as a slow open), `NotReset` for a checkpoint (not counted as a `CKPT_MAX` stop) | `ReplicaVerdicts.kt`, `ReplicaReplacement.kt`, `SharedReplicaStoreOpen.kt`, `ReplicaCheckpointer.kt` |

| The wrapped entries | Drive's and Fit's background refresh, Control's request refresh, Drive's new-folder notification action, Timeline's location events (a seam on `IosLocationCapture`) | `DriveLocalRuntime.kt`, `FitLocalRuntime.kt`, `ControlSurface.kt`, `DriveBackupSurface.kt`, `IosLocationCapture.kt`, `TimelineCaptureRuntime.kt` |
