#### B.15.3 The expiry rules

When a token's assertion expires (its handler, on the platform's thread, usually main):

| Case | What it stops | What it lets finish |
|---|---|---|
| ⚠⚠ **It ends protection**: the last token's expiry (an explicit one, an implicit one or a job's), the same expiry arriving during that token's own release's drain, or the background entered with no time granted | **Every transaction of the process, on every attached store** (200): the running statement is interrupted (`sqlite3_interrupt`, again every 50 ms while it runs); the next statement and the `COMMIT` are refused with `ProtectionExpired` before SQLite. The access rolls back (rule (a): fenced `COMMIT_FAILED`, 204), a job's chunk rolls back and its run stops, the open is a retryable `StoreUnavailable`, a checkpoint is "not reset". Holds armed until the quiesce ends are expired as they are armed (201). New accesses meet the closed gate, and off main the latch parks them. Then the 2 s drain, which now waits for rollbacks | everything (202) below |
| **Another protection remains** (the foreground, or another token) | **No statement** (W7): the token's own work is cancelled (`onExpired`: an entry's coroutine, a job's stop), and its assertion ends | every access and every write: "loops still running, writes still succeed" |
| **A job's own token** (a `REPLACEMENT` run, a walk's run) | **Its own run's statements, whatever else protects** (203): its chunk's watch, the checkpointer's `CKPT_MAX` watch (its foreground deferral included), the end-of-job checkpoint's; the run stops between chunks as before. If it also ended protection, the row above applies too | other accesses, if something else protects |

**What an expiry never stops** (202), each a decision:
1. **A `COMMIT` already issued.** The watch is disarmed in the same step as the `COMMIT` is issued
   (B.9 (124)), so an expiry finds nothing armed; the commit and its sync finish (R2) and the drain
   waits for them. Interrupting a commit's sync is not possible (*GK*) and would leave its outcome
   unknown.
2. **File work under the lock that is not a statement:** the marker lookup, a directory's
   `F_FULLFSYNC`, the open's exempt windows (B.10 (140)). Not interruptible; the expiry marks the
   hold, and the next statement after the window is refused.
3. **The marker writes:** `replica/CORRUPT` (its two syncs are reserved up front and it is never
   deferred, §4.2.1) and the walk's position file. Both are file work after the transaction, and a
   half-written marker is worse than a late one.
4. **Opening a connection** (a possible WAL-index rebuild): exempt, bounded by `R(Wmax + δ)`
   (§4.2.1's table), admitted only with that time left.
5. **A `ROLLBACK`.** Never watched (B.9 (128)): an interrupted rollback would leave the write lock
   held, the very thing the expiry is for.
6. **A close.** O(1), and it checkpoints nothing (`NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE`).
7. **The walk's reading and the confirmation's second reading** are not under the watchdog (Q18):
   their own progress handler stops them at a closed gate, at `stop` (the job token's expiry) or
   at `CONFIRM_MAX`, inside the drain.
8. **Kotlin code computing between statements**: nothing stops it; its next statement is refused.

#### B.15.4 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.14.

199. ⚠⚠ **The entries' token is the one widening of B.12 (156)'s surface, and an entry never runs
     unprotected.** `SharedReplicaLifecycle.protectEntry` hands out an opaque token, not
     `acquire`, `protect`, the latch or quiesce. `SharedReplicaEntries.withProtection` takes it off
     the main thread (on main the wait for an owed reopen is bounded, B.5.2 (71)), releases it off
     the main thread before returning (the release of the last token quiesces: up to 1 s plus the
     2 s drain, and a completion handler the caller then calls comes after the drain, Q2), and
     answers **null with the block never run** when no time is granted: the lease draft's §5.4
     ("it must not fall back to running unprotected"). Each entry turns null into its status line
     (`bg-refresh: no protected time, or it expired`). An expiry cancels the block's own scope,
     never the caller's; a cancellation of the caller is rethrown. *Rejected:* running the block
     anyway on a null token: its accesses would take the implicit token, which iOS refuses at
     the same moment, and park.
200. ⚠⚠ **Which shutdowns interrupt: exactly those no assertion covers.** The expiry that ends
     protection, the same expiry during its own release's drain, and the background entered with no
     time granted. A **release** does not interrupt: its own assertion is live through its drain
     (Q2), and `HOLD_MAX` already bounds each transaction it waits for. Issued in step 4, under the
     state lock, right after the gates close (lock order: state, then a watchdog's, then a hold's;
     none of the latter two is ever held while the state lock is taken), so the drain that follows
     waits for rollbacks, not for transactions.
201. **The expiry covers holds armed after it, and ends before the gates reopen.** A hold is
     registered and the expiry read in one step of the watchdog's lock, so an access that passed the
     gate just before it closed and arms its watch just after the interrupt is expired as it arms.
     The quiesce's `finally` ends the expiry under the state lock **before** `endQuiesce` applies an
     owed reopen, so an access admitted by protection that came back is never met by it. An expiry
     during its own release's drain interrupts at once if that quiesce has closed its gates, and
     otherwise when it does (the same bookkeeping as (81)'s drain cut), so it can never land after
     that quiesce ended and leave the store expiring for good.
202. **What an expiry lets finish**, B.15.3's list: the `COMMIT` issued, file work, the marker
     writes, an open's connection, a `ROLLBACK`, a close, the walk's and the confirmation's
     readings, Kotlin between statements.
203. ⚠ **A job's own token reaches its own run, attributed by thread.** A job runs synchronously on
     the worker's queue, so `ReplicaExpiryScope` makes the holds armed on that thread while the run
     goes on its own (a thread-local current scope, set by `around`), and the job token's
     expiration handler expires them, whether or not something else protects. An entry's work is a
     coroutine that hops threads, so it has no scope: its statements are reached only when
     protection ends (200). *Rejected:* passing the scope through every `arm` call (the chunk, the
     checkpointer, the open, the walk's judgement), which changes every signature for the one caller
     that needs it.
204. ⚠ **An access an expiry interrupted is rule (a), as at `HOLD_MAX`**: fenced `COMMIT_FAILED`.
     Its memory above the store may be ahead of the database, as for any rolled-back access. Until
     S0b-3's rebuild the process's graph keeps the fenced store, so that app's store work stops
     until it is relaunched (a log line says why). *Why accept it:* the alternative is the drain
     timing out (`[quiesce] TIMED OUT`) and the process killed with `0xdead10cc`, which loses the
     same work and the process with it. A hold reached between statements is refused the same way.
     ⚠ *(Fix round.)* **The likeliest way a user meets it is a `REGAINED` quiesce:** the app
     foregrounded within the 2 s drain after an expiry. Protection is back and the gates reopen,
     but the accesses the expiry interrupted stay fenced until relaunch, so the app comes back to
     the foreground with its store refusing work. ⚠ **And it has a second path:** entering the
     background with no time granted now interrupts too (200), so a process iOS gives no
     background time at all fences whatever was mid-transaction at that moment.
205. **`awaitStopped` waits** (B.13 (169) owed it to this slice), with no change to
     `:sync-service-proxy`: each loop's own `stopAndAwait()` is started undispatched in `stop()`,
     so the cancel still happens synchronously under the protection's lock and never blocks, and
     `awaitStopped` (off main, no lock held) waits at most its 1 s for the joins. Step 3's second is
     then the cancelled ticks finishing, with the gate still open.
206. **`ForgetWipe.relaunchControl` is an explicit flag** set by `wipeForForget`: true on every
     switched forget, false only for the unswitched one (it read `note != null`).
     Behaviour unchanged; the unswitched case is now pinned.
207. **Drive's background `URLSession` events are not wrapped, and nothing waits per batch.** Their
     Kotlin side touches Drive's own files only (row 9). The lease draft's §5.4 put a token around
     the whole batch, from `handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession` to `urlSessionDidFinishEvents`; with
     no store work in it there is nothing for that token to protect, and it would be a Swift
     change.
208. **An entry's token is taken after the runtime's install.** The binding is made and installed
     inside `assembleBase`, so before it there is nothing to take a token from; the install's open
     is admitted by the implicit token, as every background launch's is (B.5 (80)).
209. ⚠ **A Timeline location event with no time granted is dropped**, as a write that fails while
     the graph is sealed already is (`IosLocationCapture`'s KDoc): the segmenter does not see the
     fix. The open move stays durable in its journal. Q37 asks whether to journal instead.
210. ⚠ *(Fix round of the review.)* **Timeline's capture takes one token per burst, not per
     task.** `drainInEntries` waits for a task, then inside one entry runs it, every task queued
     behind it and any that arrive within `CAPTURE_ENTRY_IDLE_MS` (500 ms, a placeholder) of the
     last, then releases once. A token per task was released after each one, and in the
     background with nothing else protecting each release is the last one and quiesces (the
     loops stopped, step 3's wait of up to 1 s since (205), the gates closed and drained, then
     reopened by the next task's token), so a burst of significant-change fixes on one wake could
     spend its ~10 s on quiesces and lose its later events to (209).

211. ⚠⚠ *(Second fix round.)* **Two lost-work races closed.**
     - **A capture task at the idle window's edge.** The window waited with
       `withTimeoutOrNull { receive() }`; by prompt cancellation, a receive the timeout cancels
       after an element was handed over throws and drops it, so a fix enqueued at the 500 ms edge
       vanished. Now a `select` over `onReceiveCatching` and `onTimeout`, which is atomic: the
       task is either taken and run or left in the channel. The channel's `onUndeliveredElement`
       logs (`task_undelivered`) as the backstop for the one case left, a drain cancelled by its
       entry's expiry mid-select.
     - **An entry token taken while its caller is cancelled** (Codex P2). The token was acquired
       inside a cancellable `withContext`, which checks cancellation on its way out, so a granted
       token could be thrown away with nobody to release it: the assertion and the protection
       alive until the platform expired it, the last-token quiesce never run. Now it is acquired
       under `NonCancellable`, and the cancellation is met by `ensureActive()` inside the `try`,
       whose `finally` releases it; the block never runs. **The other acquire sites were checked:**
       the worker's job token (`acquireForJob`) is a plain, non-suspending call followed at once
       by its `try`/`finally`, and Timeline's drain takes its token through `withProtection`, so
       neither has the window.

| `posix_spawn` in place of `fork()` in `ReplicaFileDeletion`'s tests (`SharedReplicaBindingSurfaceTest`, a review nit) | **not cheap, so not done**: the child must hold POSIX locks on exactly SQLite's bytes, and the simulator runtime ships no helper that takes an `fcntl` lock, so a spawned child would be a second test executable to build, sign and locate. The forked child only makes cinterop calls on native memory allocated before the fork (`fcntl`, `write`, `read`, `_exit`), so the K/N safepoint the nit fears has nothing to wait on there; if it ever hangs, that is the place to revisit |

Should the release then interrupt, as an expiry does, before ending it? | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-24: the recommendation.** **Measure first** (the bench pair): with `HOLD_MAX` at 1 s and the drain at 10 s, a timed-out release needs a holder outside any watched statement. If the bench shows one, interrupt at the drain's deadline |
| Q37 | A Timeline location event with no time granted is dropped (209). Journal it instead? | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-24: the recommendation.** **Yes, with Timeline's iOS write outbox** (the capture's KDoc names it as future work), not here |
| Q38 | An interrupted access fences its store until relaunch (204), including after a `REGAINED` quiesce (the app foregrounded within the drain), the likeliest way a user meets it, and after a backgrounding with no time granted. Acceptable until S0b-3's rebuild? | ⭐ **DECIDED by the maintainer, 2026-10-24: the recommendation.** **Yes**: the alternative is a `0xdead10cc` kill; S0b-3's rebuild lifts it. If S0b-3 slips, a cheaper interim is to rebuild only the store handle on the foreground that follows a `REGAINED` quiesce |

#### B.15.7 Tests and mutations

**`:core-common`, new suite `ReplicaExpiryInterruptTest`, 15 tests**, over real stores, fake
assertions whose expiration handlers the test calls, the production timer, and the hold watchdog's
own timers off (B.9 (131)), so only the expiry interrupts:
- the expiry that ends protection interrupts a statement running on another thread (SQLite's own
  `SQLITE_INTERRUPT` under a `ProtectionExpired`), the drain ends `QUIESCED` in well under its 2 s,
  the handle is fenced `COMMIT_FAILED`, everything is rolled back and nothing is left armed or
  expiring;
- between statements it refuses the next one before SQLite, with nothing interrupted;
- a `COMMIT` issued as it lands finishes and commits, with no hold reached;
- the background entered with no time granted interrupts the same way;
- an expiry during its own release's 10 s drain interrupts at once, and one before its release
  closes the gates interrupts when they close, both `QUIESCED`;
- ⭐ W7, pinned by two tests: an expiry with the foreground still protecting stops nothing
  (`anExpiryWhileTheForegroundProtectsStopsNothingAndWritesGoOn`: the idle holder's transaction
  commits, the loops are not stopped, no interrupt), and an entry token expiring while another
  token protects (`anEntryTokenExpiringWhileAnotherProtectsStopsNoStatement`: the idle holder
  commits): §13's "loops still running, writes still succeed";
- the expiry ends with its quiesce, so the next foreground writes normally;
- *(fix round)* the expiry ends **before** the gates reopen: protection regained during the
  quiesce's end (a seam between the two calls) admits a waiting access that commits, unfenced
  (`anAccessAdmittedAsTheQuiesceReopensIsNotMetByItsExpiry`);
- the watchdog: a hold armed during the expiry is expired as it is armed and none after
  `endExpiry`; a disarmed hold is not reached; an exempt window and a deferred `CKPT_MAX` watch do
  not shield a hold from it;
- a job's scope reaches its own holds alone (a deferred checkpoint's included), and one armed
  after the expiry; a job's token expiring interrupts its running chunk on the worker while the
  foreground still protects (`Stopped("ProtectionExpired")`, the wipe still owed), and stops its
  checkpoint without counting a `CKPT_MAX` stop.

Three `ReplicaProtectionTest` cases changed meaning by design (an idle holder through an expiry
that leaves nothing protecting now has its `COMMIT` refused with `ProtectionExpired`, where it
committed after the drain): `anExpiryDuringItsOwnReleasesDrain…`, `anExpiryBeforeItsReleaseClosesTheGates…`
(the unwatched variants) and `anExpiryBetweenReleasingAndTheShutdownWaitsForTheRelease`.

### B.16 S0b-3 slice 1: the fence lifecycle core (2026-10-24)

**What it is.** The first slice of §13's S0b-3 row, behind the same off-by-default switch, and
Kotlin only:
- **The `replaced` signal and the rebuild (§6).** Each process's runtime host (`FirstPartyLocalRuntime`
  for the nine route-1 apps, `ControlSurface` for Control) hands every graph it builds to the
  process's `SharedReplicaHost`, which collects the store's fence. At a fence it runs §6's steps 1
  to 3 (the state, the graph stopped, custody kept); in the foreground it runs step 2b (the fenced
  handle released through the binding) and step 4 (the shipping-gate probe, then the runtime's own
  reinstall, which opens through the binding's normal open). **At most once per foreground.** This
  lifts B.15 (204) (an access an expiry interrupted, a `REGAINED` quiesce's included), B.14 (193)
  (Control's graph after its own forget) and B.13 (173)'s dead end where the refusal is retryable.
- ⭐ **Q35 as decided (2026-10-24):** a retryable refusal at open is **"not ready, try again"**: the
  graph gets a not-ready stand-in, never the file store, so nothing writes `objects/` and nothing
  declares `files` (B.14 (190)); the host rebuilds at the next protected entry or foreground.
  Non-retryable outcomes keep their paths (B.13 (181)'s fallback).
- **A host lifecycle state**, `SharedReplicaHost.status: StateFlow<SharedReplicaHostStatus>`
  (`READY`, `REFRESHING`, `UPDATING`, `CHECKING`, `SKEW`, `CORRUPT`, `NOT_READY`, each with its reason
  and whether the host retries by itself), under the `ERROR`-level opt-in and `@HiddenFromObjC`.
  ⚠ **No Swift in this slice**: "Refreshing…", "Updating storage…", "Checking storage…", "Storage
  damaged" and the update surface are slice 2's (B.16.4).

⚠ With the switch off nothing changes: no binding is made, so no host exists; the runtimes'
`rebuildWith` only stores a closure nobody calls, `SharedReplicaEntries` runs every block
unwrapped with no retry, and Control's `graphInstalled` and its forget's rebuild return at once
(B.16.2).

#### B.16.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The signal | `SharedReplicaStore.fenced: StateFlow<ReplicaFence?>`: null while the handle serves, then its fence, once (`COMMIT_FAILED` may still become `CORRUPT`). The existing `fence` field reads and writes it, so every path that fences emits | `SharedReplicaStore.kt` (`:core-common`) |
| The host | `SharedReplicaHost`, one per `SharedReplicaBinding` (so per process): `graphInstalled(store, stop, rebuild, mayRebuild)`, the fence collector, `onForeground`, `retryAtEntry`, `hold`/`resume` and `forgetGraph`, and `rebuild(trigger)`: step 2b's release (a failure latches), the probe, the reinstall. A `rebuilding` guard released in a `finally` | `SharedReplicaHost.kt` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`) |
| The state | `SharedReplicaHostState` and `SharedReplicaHostStatus(state, detail, willRetry)`, `@SharedReplicaPlatformApi`, `@HiddenFromObjC`; read through `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.sharedReplicaStatus` and `ControlSharedReplica.hostStatus` | `SharedReplicaHost.kt`, `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.kt`, `ControlSharedReplica.kt` |
| The not-ready stand-in | `NotReadyReplicaStore`: reads absent, the pagers null, `isEmpty` false, listeners never fire, writes throw `StoreNotReady` (a `StoreHandleFenced`); an in-process `DatabaseLock` | `SharedReplicaHost.kt` |

#### B.16.2 The switch, and "off" unchanged

As B.13.3, and nothing new runs off:
- **No binding, no host.** The host is a member of `SharedReplicaBinding`, which only a switched
  process makes (`sqliteBindingFor`, `ControlSharedReplica.isSwitched`). Every new call site is
  behind a binding that is null off: `sqlite?.host?.graphInstalled(…)` in `assembleBase`,
  `boundSqlite` in Control's `graphInstalled`, `isSwitched` before the forget's `resume`, and
  `installedBinding()` in `SharedReplicaEntries` (null, so the block runs unwrapped with no retry).
- **The nine apps' one line** (`runtime.rebuildWith(::rebuildGraph)`) stores a closure; only a
  host calls it. The `rebuildGraph` functions are dead code off.
- **Control off:** `runtimeModule()` returns null before it touches `boundSqlite`;
  `wipeThenPurgeCustody` returns `wipeForForget`'s answer unchanged (`relaunchControl` false).
- **`SharedReplicaStore.fenced`** is the store's own field behind a flow: the store is opened only
  switched.
- Tests: `withTheSwitchOffNoHostIsMadeAndNothingIsRebuilt` (the binding factory and the reinstall
  both fail the test if called, the file store is bound, no state exists, an entry runs unwrapped);
  the existing switch-off tests of B.13.3, B.14.2 and B.15 pass unchanged.
- **No `project.yml`, entitlement, signing or Swift change.**
- ⭐ **No threat-model amendment.** A4, A9, Decision C and custody are untouched: the rebuild of an
  app's graph reads the key material through `RealmKeyMaterialBridge` exactly as its launch does
  (it is the re-provision path that already exists), and a bridge that is gone means **no**
  rebuild (219), never a rebuild over residual custody; Control's forget still purges custody only
  on a finished wipe (B.14 (191)), and its rebuilt graph is the pre-genesis graph a relaunch gives.
  Nothing is written to `replica/` that was not before, and the stand-in writes nothing at all.

#### B.16.3 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.15.

212. **The signal is `fenced: StateFlow<ReplicaFence?>`**, §6's `replaced` under the name of what
     it carries. §6 drafted `Replacement(reason, replacedBy)` read from `meta` in the same
     transaction; this slice does not read `meta.replaced_by`, because **the host does not need
     it**: what follows a `REPLACED` or `COMMIT_FAILED` fence is always the rebuild's own open, and
     that open's answer (`Ready`, `Updating`, `Skew`, `Corrupt`, a retryable refusal) is the state
     the host publishes. `SKEW` and `UPDATING` are therefore states of the host, never fences of a
     handle. The setter only stores the value: a fence taken under the registry's lock runs no
     collector inline.
213. ⚠⚠ **When the rebuild runs.** §6's step 4 is "in the foreground only"; the brief says "on the
     next foreground (once per foreground)". Built:
     - at **each foreground** (the adapter's hook, on main, after the gates reopened and the
       worker was kicked), if one is owed, ⚠ *scheduled* on the main thread, never run inside
       the notification (221, as revised in the fix round);
     - ⚠ **and at once when the fence lands while the process is in the foreground**, scheduled on
       the main thread: a handle is fenced at its next access (§3.1), so a sibling's wipe met just
       after a foreground, a rule-(a) failure mid-session, and the `REGAINED` race of B.15 (204)
       (the foreground arriving inside the expiry's drain, before the interrupted access is
       refused) would otherwise wait a whole background and foreground;
     - **at most once per foreground** for both (§6: "a second failure leaves the runtime fenced
       on an error state", `NOT_READY` with "storage unavailable"), so a full disk or a repeated
       `ROW_MAX` row cannot loop rebuilds. The launch counts as no foreground's rebuild: a graph
       fenced in its launch's foreground is rebuilt once;
     - at a **protected entry** and on the runtime's **explicit** ask (217), outside that budget:
       each is one discrete event.
214. ⚠⚠ **Q35's "not ready" is a stand-in store, not a missing one.** The graph must have an
     `ObjectStore` (Koin resolves it while the client is built, and an app's `install()` that
     throws aborts at the ObjC boundary), so a retryable refusal binds `NotReadyReplicaStore`,
     which answers as a fenced handle does (§6: reads absent, never a throw into Swift). Its graph
     is **stopped at once** (its loops would only spin against a store that refuses every write)
     and a rebuild is owed. ⚠⚠ **It never writes `objects/` and never declares**: Control's
     `onBound` skips the declaration for it, where it declared `files` for any non-SQLite store,
     which would have held the phone on the file store until a forget (190).
215. ⚠ **What counts as retryable, slightly wider than Q35's three.** Q35 named `StoreUnavailable`,
     `ProtectionExpired` and `HoldCeilingExceeded`. Built: every `StoreUnavailable` (protected
     data, a closed gate, an unverified `-wal` reset, a store that kept changing, and
     `StoreBeingChecked` as `CHECKING`), `HoldCeilingExceeded` with its `ProtectionExpired`, **and**
     `StoreNeedsForeground` (`UPDATING`: a background open that may not start a migration or a
     wipe) **and** an `Updating` the binding's wait did not see finish (stopped, needs the
     foreground, or past `UPDATING_WAIT_MS`). Each of the last two is "try again later" by
     definition, and falling back for them is the sticky-`files` path Q35 closed. **Not retryable,
     unchanged:** `Skew`, `Corrupt` (from the open or from the job's run), an `Updating` with no
     worker, `SharedReplicaUnprotected`, an extension, anything else: the file store for this
     launch, with the state recorded as `SKEW` or `CORRUPT` and "this launch uses the file store"
     (Q40). Q44 asks to confirm the widening.
216. **A rebuilt graph's loops are unbound, not retired.** B.14 (193) retired Control's loops for
     good because nothing rebuilt; now the host's stop calls `DeferredReplicaLoops.unbind()` (the
     old graph's loops stopped and forgotten) and the rebuilt graph's `bindLoops` binds its own.
     Rule P meanwhile drives nothing. `retire()` stays where nothing is rebuilt: (196), the choice
     that no longer allows the store.
217. ⚠⚠ **Who owns a release the binding makes itself.** The custody wipe releases the store, which
     fences it `RELEASED`, and the host must not take that for a fence to rebuild from:
     - **an app's deprovision** (B.13 (171)) **forgets the graph** before the release: stopped,
       never rebuilt; the app's own gate shows the connect screen;
     - **Control's forget** **holds** it: stopped, and nothing is rebuilt while the forget waits
       for the worker (a rebuild then would open into the wipe, and adopt custody the forget is
       about to purge); then `wipeThenPurgeCustody` **resumes** it, rebuilding **at once on a
       finished wipe** (on the main thread: the onboarding that follows needs a store that takes
       writes) and at the next foreground or entry after an unfinished one. ⭐ This lifts B.14
       (193): `ForgetWipe.relaunchControl` is true only when that rebuild left no serving graph,
       and "quit and reopen Tenshu Control" is said only then;
     - **the choice's re-read** (196) forgets the graph too (the next launch binds the file store).
218. ~~**Control's stop is its loops alone, never `SyncManager.lock()`.**~~ ⚠⚠ *Revised in
     the fix round (the independent review):* a Control graph left unlocked kept its pairing
     monitor, request collector and pollers talking to the relay with the old keys, whose local
     persist then fails (a half-applied step). **Control's stop now locks the old graph's
     `SyncManager`** (verified in memory only: `lock()` drops the session's keys, ownerId and A13,
     and persists nothing, so the rebuilt graph starts locked as a relaunch does), **stops its
     pairing session** (`SyncManager.stopPairing()`, the ephemeral key zeroed, and the
     `HostPairingMonitor`'s own countdown and flows) and **cancels its OS-alert collector** (228).
     The apps' stop is `SyncManager.lock()` too (purges the in-memory keys; the reinstall
     re-adopts them from the bridge). ⚠ So a fence in the middle of a host-pairing SAS comparison
     ends that session: the approval would have failed anyway (its persist goes to the released
     store), and telling the user is slice 2's surface.
219. ⚠ **Step 4's shipping-gate probe is "is the bridge there?", and a gone bridge means no rebuild,
     not a deprovision by the host.** §6 says "bridge gone with custody left → `deprovision()`". The
     app's own gate (`RootView.recheck()`, at every foreground) already does exactly that, and a
     second caller of `deprovision()` racing it is worse than leaving the graph fenced for the
     moment it takes. Control has no probe (it is the bridge's source).
220. **The entry's retry runs inside its token, before its work, on the main thread.** A not-ready
     background launch's next entry (Drive's or Fit's refresh, Control's request refresh, a
     Timeline location burst, Drive's notification action) first rebuilds, so its work runs over the
     real store. ⚠ **Cancellation**: the token is taken under `NonCancellable` as (211) built; the
     retry is a `withContext(main)`, so a caller cancelled or expired before it is dispatched never
     starts it (the rebuild stays owed), and one cancelled while it runs lets it finish (a
     reinstall is not interruptible) and leaves the host consistent, the guard released in a
     `finally`; the token is released in the entry's `finally`; the entry's block never runs.
221. ~~**The foreground's rebuild runs inside `willEnterForeground`, synchronously on main.**~~
     ⚠⚠ *Revised in the fix round (the independent review):* a release (which may wait behind
     an access, about `HOLD_MAX`), an open (a classification and a write transaction, each under
     `HOLD_MAX`), a wait of up to `UPDATING_WAIT_MS` (10 s) and the app's whole `install()` inside
     the notification sat on the resume watchdog. **`onForeground` now only schedules** the rebuild
     on the main thread (as `onFenced` does) and returns at once; and **a rebuild never waits for a
     job** (227). The launch's own open still waits up to 10 s (Q29's wait), which slice 2 replaces
     with "Updating storage…" (Q41).
222. **A failed release latches the process**: §6 step 2b's failure (the registry latched
     unusable) means no step 4, now or at any later foreground, `NOT_READY` with
     `willRetry = false` ("storage unavailable"). The next launch is the retry.
223. **The rebuild is each app's re-provision path**, which every app already runs (`deprovision`
     then `install` in one process): `installed = null; install()`. The old graph is orphaned until
     process death, as `deprovision`'s is, holding no open handle (released in step 2b). ⚠ SwiftUI
     screens built over the old graph's view models keep them; slice 2's surfaces re-create them
     (B.16.4).
224. **A stand-in at a foreground launch waits for the next foreground**: no timer and no retry
     loop in this slice; protected data becoming available does not retry either (Q42).
225. **`CORRUPT` is never rebuilt, and is re-read at the rebuild**: a `COMMIT_FAILED` fence whose
     confirmation then makes the marker durable is promoted on the handle, and the rebuild reads
     `fencedBy` again before it starts.

#### B.16.8 Fix round 1: what outlives a rebuilt graph

**What it fixes.** Codex's three P2s were one class, and the independent review named
its general form: **a rebuild ran `installed = null; install()` and orphaned everything the old
graph had set up outside itself**: process-level components built over its client (Timeline's
capture, Drive's backup loop, Control's OS-alert collector), the scopes each assembly made, and
the old Koin graph itself, all still bound to the released store. The review added two more: the
foreground's rebuild ran inside the notification (221, revised), and Control's old graph stayed
unlocked (218, revised).

Numbered on from (225).

226. **A job's finish rebuilds a graph waiting for it** (Q43 in part). A graph on the stand-in for
     `UPDATING` is rebuilt when the binding is told this store's `REPLACEMENT_FINISHED`, in the
     foreground, on the main thread (`Trigger.JOB_FINISHED`, outside the per-foreground budget:
     a finished job is a discrete event, and its open either serves or meets a new job).
227. ⚠⚠ **A rebuild never waits for a job** (`FOREGROUND`, `EXPLICIT`, `JOB_FINISHED`). Inside
     one, an open answered `Updating` throws a retryable `SharedReplicaNotReady(UPDATING)` at once,
     never the `UPDATING_WAIT_MS` wait: the graph gets the stand-in (Q35's path) and (226) rebuilds
     it when the job finishes. The launch's open keeps its wait (Q29, Q41). ⚠ *Narrowed in the
     re-review:* **an `ENTRY` rebuild keeps the bounded wait**. A background entry has no
     foreground to come back to, and a stand-in there would never be rebuilt in the background, so
     a Timeline visit arriving during a wipe would be lost where it used to wait and be served.
228. ⚠⚠ **Every component bound to a graph stops with it, and is built anew over the next.** A new
     seam, `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.onCurrentGraphStop(block)`: an app registers, right after its
     assembly, what that graph owns beyond its Koin (its scopes, a process-level component over its
     client); the host's stop runs the blocks once, with `SyncManager.lock()`, at the fence, a hold
     or a deprovision (§6 step 2), and the rebuild's `install()` builds them over the new graph. A
     process-level component is detached only if it is still over **that** graph's client
     (`detachIfOver(client)`), so a late stop never takes down its successor. The table below is
     the audit of every app's `iosMain`.
229. ⚠⚠ **The old Koin graph is closed at the rebuild**, before the new one is built
     (`FirstPartyLocalRuntime`'s rebuild for the nine apps, `ControlSurface.rebuildRealRuntime`
     for Control): its singletons are dropped instead of orphaned one per rebuild, and nothing more
     resolves from it. ⚠ **A residual, recorded:** `Koin.close()` drops references and runs
     `onClose` callbacks, and no definition of the proxy graph has one, so the coroutine scopes its
     singletons create for themselves (the model downloader's, `MediaIndexRunner`'s, the region
     components', the proxy's `serviceScope` and its session scopes, the schema announcer's) are
     **not cancelled**. They are neutered rather than stopped: the store answers absent and refuses
     writes (released), the `SyncManager` is locked (no ownerId, so no device JWT is minted:
     *Read*, from `jwtTokenProvider`, not tested), and the sync loops are unbound. A model or
     region download already running (network and its own file database, never `replica/`) may
     finish in the orphaned graph. The structural fix, one root `Job` per graph that every scope of
     `buildProxyModule()` derives from, is a `commonMain` change on every platform, and is owed to
     `docs/tech-debt.md` (Q45). ⭐ **Built (B.16.15, 2026-10-30):** the close now cancels the
     graph's `ProxyGraphJob`, and every scope the module makes is its child, so this residual is
     closed.
230. **A failed write over the stand-in is a failure, never shown as done** (the review's item 4,
     checked). `DatabaseImpl.saveData` records only the id mapping before `storeObject`, and
     `addToArray` pre-updates its listener snapshot, but no listener of the stand-in ever fires and
     the op returns the refusal as a failed result (`LocalTaskExecutor`'s catch-all), so a screen
     never shows the write as applied. ⚠ **Reads are an empty success** until slice 2's surfaces
     (Q39): a switched build's screens show empty listings over the stand-in or a fenced store.
     **Recorded as a known user-visible residual of a switched (dev-only) build**, not bridged now:
     the Swift surface is slice 2's whole job.

#### B.16.9 Second fix round (Codex's second round and the re-review)

Numbered on from (230).

231. ⚠⚠ **A job's finish is latched.** If a `REPLACEMENT_FINISHED` lands while a rebuild runs, for
     example between its open's `Updating` and its stand-in graph's install, the host is still
     showing the old state (or is mid-rebuild) and drops it, and the graph would sit on the
     stand-in until the next foreground or entry (Codex P2). The host now counts every finish. A
     rebuild that ends with its graph waiting on the stand-in for `UPDATING`, and whose count has
     moved since it began, schedules the next rebuild (`JOB_FINISHED`).
232. ⚠ **A fence inside a background entry is rebuilt then.** The fix covers a Timeline location
     burst, a refresh or a notification action (the re-review). Before, it waited for the user to
     open the app, with Timeline's capture detached meanwhile. A rebuild runs once per background,
     until the next foreground, so a failing store cannot loop. `SharedReplicaEntries` now counts
     the entries running.
233. ⚠ **A detached capture keeps its monitoring registered** (the re-review, P2). See the

#### B.16.10 Third fix round (Codex's third round and the re-review of `8b9774c`)

Numbered on from (236).

237. ⚠⚠ **A new-folder answer is never lost, and never applied through a stopped graph**
     (Codex P2). After a background fence with no entry, the stop drops Drive's new-folder
     decisions (228). `answerNewFolderPrompt` read them **before** its entry, so it returned in
     silence and the entry's retry never ran.
     - The decisions are now looked up **inside** the entry, after its retry has rebuilt the
       graph.
     - If no graph serves even then, the answer is kept, with a loud line, and the next graph's
       `start()` applies it.
     - With the switch off it is exactly as before.
238. ⚠⚠ **A parked location manager lives only while a successor needs it** (Codex P2, a privacy
     matter, and the re-review's cases). (233) parks the manager of a detached capture, still
     monitoring. `ParkedLocationMonitor` (in `timeline-shared-data`) holds at most one, and
     stops and releases it:
     - when the next capture's manager has started monitoring, so no two managers are alive;
     - when the user turns capture off: `stopCapture()` releases it **whatever is live**,
       including `active == null` after a detach;
     - at a later `startIfEnabled()` with capture off;
     - when authorization is denied (through `stopCapture()`);
     - when the graph is **given up with no rebuild to follow**.
     The last case uses a new host hook, `abandon`, that runs once per graph:
     - triggers: a `CORRUPT` fence, a latched release, a refused probe, a fence on a graph after
       the latch, and `forgetGraph` (a deprovision, a choice that no longer allows the store);
     - the hook reaches the apps as `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.onCurrentGraphAbandoned`; a late
       registration runs at once;
     - Timeline registers the parked manager's release there.
     None of these writes through a graph.
239. ⚠⚠ **The background rebuild of (232) runs under a token of its own** (the re-review, P2).
     - **The problem.** In Timeline's case the detach cancels the drain whose entry met the fence,
       so that entry's token may already be released, and its release may quiesce, before the
       queued rebuild runs. The rebuild then opened the App Group store with no protection,
       possibly waiting up to `UPDATING_WAIT_MS` while holding the shared lock across a
       suspension. That is the `0xdead10cc` case.
     - **The fix.** The rebuild now takes `entry:rebuild` through the binding's `protectEntry`
       (`SharedReplicaEntries.protectedBy`, under `NonCancellable` as (211)) and runs inside it.
     - **No time granted:** nothing is rebuilt, and the next entry's retry or the foreground does
       it.
240. **A reinstall that throws after it assembled a graph stops that half-built graph's
     components** (the re-review, low). The half-built graph is never handed to the host, and its
     `onCurrentGraphStop` blocks run before the throw propagates.
241. **A stopped graph's index pass is waited for before the next graph opens the same files**
     (the re-review, low; *joined* rather than *tolerated*).
     - `teardownGraph` starts `OwnedInferenceStores.stopWriter`, which runs `cancelRunningPass()`:
       cancel and join. It runs on a scope of the process's.
     - ~~The next graph's store check joins that job first, for up to 5 s.~~ *Replaced by (246):*
       no deadline, and the gate waits too.
     - ~~Every store write of a pass goes through the stores' `Mutex`.~~ *Corrected in the fourth
       round (245):* each graph's Koin has its own stores and its own `Mutex`, so **only this join**
       serialises the two graphs' writes.
     - ⚠ **Not unit-tested:** an append in flight at the moment of the cancel cannot be staged in
       the suite, so this is device-only (B.16.7).
242. **Smaller:** `detachIfOver`'s KDoc now says what a detach does (the delegate and the worker
     go, and monitoring stays parked).

#### B.16.11 Fourth fix round (the third re-review and Codex on `5f214b7`)

Numbered on from (242).

243. ⚠⚠ **A kept new-folder answer is removed only once its preference write has succeeded**
     (Codex P2 and the re-review). (237) took the kept answers and cleared them, then applied them
     in a launched entry. Four cases then dropped them in silence:
     - no protected time;
     - the controller's scope cancelled before the apply ran. ⚠ That happens **every** time a
       rebuild lands on the not-ready stand-in: `installLocked()` calls `start()` before
       `graphReady()`, which stops the stand-in's graph;
     - a failed preference write;
     - a live answer with no token, which was neither applied nor kept.

     Now:
     - one answer per bucket is kept, the latest;
     - live answers and the kept answers' apply are serialised under one `Mutex`;
     - the apply reads the kept answers at apply time, and removes each one only after its write
       succeeded (and only if it was not replaced since);
     - a live answer first removes its bucket's kept answer, so an older kept answer can never
       overwrite a newer live one;
     - a live answer is kept when it gets no protected time, when its write fails, and when its
       caller is cancelled (re-applying is idempotent).
244. **Kept answers do not cross a realm.** They wait for the next graph *of the same realm*, so
     the graph's abandon hook drops them (238): a deprovision, a corrupt store, a latch. Drive
     registers it with `onCurrentGraphAbandoned`. With the switch off there is no binding, and
     answers are dropped as before.
245. **Photos' writer stop is resolved while the graph's Koin is open** (the re-review, low).
     - **The bug.** `stopWriter(koin)` looked up `MediaIndexRunner` on `teardownScope`, after the
       rebuild might already have closed that Koin. Then nothing was cancelled or joined.
     - **The fix.** `OwnedInferenceStores.writerStopper(koin)` resolves the runner synchronously
       in `teardownGraph`. Only the cancel and the join run later.
     - **Comment corrected.** (241)'s comment now says that only this join serialises the two
       graphs' writes.

  stands.
- **Kept answers are dropped when their graph is given up.**

#### B.16.12 Fifth fix round (Codex at `970551b`)

246. ⚠⚠ **No graph opens the inference files until a stopped graph's index pass has really
     ended.** (Codex P2.)
     - **The bug.** (241) joined the pass for at most 5 s and then opened the files anyway. A
       synchronous file write already in progress is not interrupted by cancellation, and the new
       graph's `DefaultEmbeddingStore` and face store have their own `Mutex` and their own cached
       append offsets. The new graph could therefore read a half-written log, or append over the
       old graph's write.
     - **The fix.** `OwnedInferenceStores.holdOpensUntil(writer)` takes the stop job that Photos'
       `teardownGraph` starts. Until that job completes:
       - `OwnedInferenceStores.check` waits for it, with **no deadline**, off the main thread as it
         already was;
       - **every inference gate waits for it too**: the gate a query or a pass reaches first is
         now a `WriterBarrierGate` over the custody, which waits before the custody may open the
         files;
       - the stores stay unusable, so on-device AI reports not-ready, as during any pending
         check.
     - The `withTimeoutOrNull(5 s)` in Photos' check is gone.
     - One wiring test now asserts that the gate is the custody's behind the barrier, where it
       asserted the gate *is* the custody.

**Test.** `PhotosOwnedInferenceStoresTest` (+1): with a stopped graph's writer still running,
5.5 s later the next graph's check and its gate have not completed and its stores are unusable;
once the writer ends, both open and the stores are usable.

247. ⚠⚠ **No store reads its log before a stopped graph's writer has ended** (Codex P2 at
     `60158b2`). (246) delayed the custody's *check*, but not the stores' *construction*.
     `DefaultEmbeddingStore` and `DefaultFaceTemplateStore` read their log and cache its append
     offset as they are built, and the stores are built as soon as anything resolves them.
     **Every path that resolves them** on the iOS Photos graph:
     - the custody (`InferenceStoreCustody`, so `WriterBarrierGate` too);
     - the index runner and its indexer (`ProxyModule`'s `MediaIndexRunner` and its indexer);
     - the query backend (iOS `PlatformProxyModule`'s `embeddings = get()`);
     - the Models screen's coverage (`PhotosOnDeviceAi`'s `size()`);
     - `ForegroundIndexSource.runnerStanding()`, through the runner;
     - the tests.

     All of these resolve the one binding of `ownedInferenceStoresModule`, which is now
     `AfterPriorWriterEmbeddingStore` / `AfterPriorWriterFaceTemplateStore`. That makes an early
     resolve **harmless by construction** rather than guarded at each resolver. Nothing is built,
     and so no log is read, until the first call, and that call first waits for every held writer
     with no deadline. A caller meanwhile suspends: it never crashes and never blocks a thread.
     The Models screen sees the custody unusable, so not-ready.
248. ⚠ **The writer barrier is chained, and says when it holds** (the re-review).
     - **Chained.** `holdOpensUntil` no longer overwrites its slot. Each new writer is joined
       after every earlier one, so if graph 1's writer hangs and graph 2's ends at once, graph 3
       still waits.
     - **⚠ A writer that never ends** leaves on-device AI not-ready until the next launch. The
       barrier logs it once, about 5 s in: `inference stores held: a stopped graph's index pass
       has not ended`.
     - **⚠ A deprovision's `relinquish` does not wait for the barrier.** It would `runBlocking` on
       the main thread. Fragments an old pass may still write are cleared by the next `check`'s
       clear, the backstop the stamp already provides.
     - The suite resets the held writers before and after each test
       (`clearPriorWritersForTests`).

**Tests.** `PhotosOwnedInferenceStoresTest` (+2):
- **No store reads its log while a stopped graph's writer runs.** The stores, the custody, the
  gate and the runner are all resolved. No log is read and a call waits. Once the writer ends,
  the stores are built over the whole log.
- **A hung writer still holds the stores after a later writer ends.**

#### B.16.13 Sixth fix round (Codex at `a340906`, and the re-review's low item)

251. ⚠⚠ **A stop and a rebuild never overlap, and a teardown reaches only its own graph's loops**
     (Codex P2).
     - **The race.** The fence collector, on `Dispatchers.Default`, marked a graph stopped before
       it ran the stop's steps. A foreground or entry rebuild on main then found the stop
       "done", released the handle and installed a successor. The collector's late
       `unbindLoops()` then stopped the **successor's** sync loops, and the rebuilt graph reported
       `READY` with no sync running.
     - **The fix.** Each graph now has two separate marks:
       - `stopped`: the stop has been claimed;
       - `stopDone`: a `CompletableDeferred` that completes in the stop's `finally`.
     - **A rebuild that finds a claimed stop still running** does not proceed. Nothing of the
       per-foreground budget is spent on it. It hands itself back and runs again when `stopDone`
       completes, scheduled on the main thread. It never waits on main.
     - **A graph is installed with the loops binding it had**, and its teardown calls
       `DeferredReplicaLoops.unbindIf(thatBinding)`, which does nothing once a successor's loops
       are bound. This is the `detachIfOver` rule applied to the loops.
252. **Once a stopped graph's index pass is being awaited, no pass starts** (the re-review, low).
     - `MediaIndexRunner.stopAndAwaitEnded()` latches the runner as retired under its lock before
       anything else. From then on `start()` answers false and `runToCompletion()` answers
       deferred.
     - It then cancels **every** pass in its snapshot, not only the one in flight, and joins them.
     - The runner is per graph, and only a stopped graph's teardown calls it.

**Tests.**
- `SharedReplicaHostTest` (+2):
  - **A late stop never reaches the rebuilt graph's loops.** The collector is paused between the
    claim and its steps, and a foreground rebuild meanwhile does nothing. Once resumed, the order
    is the old graph's stop, then the rebuild. The successor's loops are still bound and never
    stopped.
  - **A graph's teardown unbinds only its own loops.**
- `MediaIndexRunnerTest` (+1): a `start` between the stop's cancel and its snapshot is refused,
  as is every later one. `runToCompletion` answers deferred, and the stop still waits for the pass
  it found.

#### B.16.14 Seventh fix round (the re-review of `5a47ae56d`, Codex at `e3e7f5a`)

253. ⚠⚠ **A rebuild held back by a claimed stop comes back, and in the background under its own
     token.**
     - **The bug.** (251)'s back-off was dead code. The pending-stop branch returned null from the
       claim, so `val target = claimed ?: return false` returned before the retry was ever
       registered. It was covered only because `onFenced` schedules its own rebuild after its
       stop. When the claimer schedules nothing afterwards, the rebuild was dropped until the next
       foreground or entry. Examples: a fence collector that found the app in the background with
       no entry; a `hold` racing a `resume(now)`; a background entry that met the claimed stop
       and ended before the stop did.
     - **The fix.** The retry is registered on `stopDone` **before** that early return.
       `retryAfterStop` decides when the stop has ended:
       - **in the foreground:** on the main thread, as asked; an `ENTRY` retry runs as a
         `FOREGROUND` one, so it does not take the entry's bounded wait on main;
       - **in the background:** under a token of its own (`entry:rebuild`, as (239)) through
         `rebuildInBackground`, and **not at all** when no time is granted. It then stays owed for
         the next entry or foreground, and it never runs unprotected. The entry that asked may
         well be over.

**Tests.** `SharedReplicaHostTest` (+2):
- **A rebuild held back by a claimed stop comes back when the claimer schedules nothing.** The
  collector sees the background at the fence. A foreground rebuild meanwhile is held. After the
  stop it comes back exactly once.
- **A background entry held back by a claimed stop is retried under its own token.** The entry
  meets the claimed stop and ends, and the collector sees neither the foreground nor an entry.
  With time granted, the retry runs under `entry:rebuild`. With none, it does not run, and the
  rebuild stays owed.

`aLateStopNeverReachesTheRebuiltGraphsLoops` alone passed with the back-off dead, which is why
these two siblings exist.

Mutations (`SharedReplicaHostTest`, 33 tests; each mutant red, the suite green without it):

| # | Mutant | Red |
|---|--------|-----|
| M410 | the retry's `invokeOnCompletion` registration removed | the background test |
| M411 | the background retry runs `rebuild` unprotected instead of `rebuildInBackground()` | the background test (no `entry:rebuild` begun) |
| M412 | the retry's foreground branch does nothing | the foreground test |

⚠ M410 does **not** turn the foreground test red, and that is the test's answer order, not a gap:
with the retry gone, the collector's own post-stop check is the first to ask and is told
"foreground", so it rebuilds itself. M412 is the mutant that reaches the foreground branch.

**What it fixes.** (229)'s residual: `Koin.close()` dropped the old graph's singletons but
cancelled none of the scopes they had made for themselves, so a model or region download already
running could finish in the orphaned graph. Built as decided (B.16.8 Q45). Its own `commonMain`
change; nothing here is behind the switch, and an unswitched build behaves as before (294).

     `control-shared-proxy/.../di/ProxyGraphJob.kt`): a root `SupervisorJob`, and `scope(owner)`
     makes a supervisor child of it. Every scope the module makes goes through it (`graphScope`):
     the model downloader's, `MediaIndexRunner`'s, the map-region components', `ClientRegistry`'s

     cancelled the scope and every sibling; a supervisor child is the nearer one of the two. Android, desktop and the web never close their

295. ⚠⚠ **The graph's teardown cancels it, then closes it** (`closeProxyGraph`, from

296. ⚠ **Never at the stop.** A stopped graph keeps serving its stand-in until the rebuild, which

**Not derived from the root, recorded.** Scopes made outside `buildProxyModule()`: the platform

### B.17 S0b-3 slice 2: the host lifecycle, the user-facing half (2026-10-28)

**What it is.** The second slice of §13's S0b-3 row, behind the same off-by-default switch. The
maintainer decided Q39–Q44 on 2026-10-28, each as recommended (B.16.5). ⚠ **Split in two PRs**
(268): **PR A** (this section, Kotlin only) builds Q40–Q44, the Swift-visible surface's API and
the slice-1 carry-over; **PR B** mounts that surface in the ten apps' `RootView`s (Swift). Until
PR B lands, a switched build's screens over a stand-in show empty, as since B.16 (230).

- ⭐ **Q40: no file-store fallback at open.** Every refusal gives the graph the stand-in with its
  state, `SKEW` and `CORRUPT` included, so a newer sibling's store no longer moves an older app,
  and with it the whole phone, onto the file store (254). B.13 (181) is gone.
- ⭐ **Q41: no open on the graph's path waits for a job.** A launch that meets a wipe or a
  migration takes the stand-in at once ("Refreshing…" or "Updating storage…"), and the job's
  finish installs (226). Q29's 10 s main-thread wait is gone. **A scheduled rebuild runs in two
  turns** (258): off the main thread the probe, the fenced handle's release and the open; then on
  it the reinstall, whose open finds the store open.
- ⭐ **Q42: "Try again" and one automatic retry.** `StorageStateSurface.tryAgain()` rebuilds a
  not-ready graph (260); `UIApplicationProtectedDataDidBecomeAvailable` retries a
  `ProtectedDataUnavailable` refusal once (259).
- ⭐ **Q43: a sibling's job is noticed at the next access.** A read of the stand-in while the store
  is being replaced re-opens it, throttled and off the main thread; only an open that serves is
  followed by a rebuild (261).
- ⭐ **Q44: confirmed.** The retryable set is what B.16 (215) built; the code and this section now
  say the same (262).
- **Q39's API**: `StorageStateSurface` in `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, a snapshot, a callback, a "Try
  again" and a generation that re-creates the root (257). The ten `RootView`s are PR B's.
- **The carry-over of slice 1**: Drive's kept new-folder answers are replayed at each foreground
  and with the next answer, and a late keep after an abandon's drop is refused (265, 266); the
  (253) completion handler cannot throw (264); the budget note (267).

⚠ With the switch off nothing changes: no binding is made, so no host is attached to the surface,
whose snapshot is `READY`, covering nothing, generation 0, for the life of the process (B.17.2).

#### B.17.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The surface | `StorageStateSurface`: `snapshot()`, `observe(onChange)` → `StorageStateObservation.cancel()`, `tryAgain()`; `StorageStateSnapshot(state, covers, title, message, canTryAgain, generation)`, a data class of plain values; the copy in one table | `StorageStateSurface.kt` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`, Swift-visible) |
| Its host | attached once, when the process's binding is made (`SharedReplicaBinding.process`); nothing attached off | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| The state | `SharedReplicaHostState.NO_GRAPH` (255); `SharedReplicaHostStatus.wipe` (256), `.protectedDataUnavailable` (259), `.generation` (257) | `SharedReplicaHost.kt` |
| No fallback | `sqliteStoreOrFileStore`: every refusal → `NotReadyReplicaStore(status, onAccess)`; the file store only for a graph whose relay is not the dev lab's | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| A stand-in given up | a `SKEW` or `CORRUPT` stand-in's graph is stopped and abandoned (238) at its install | `SharedReplicaHost.graphInstalled` |
| No wait on the graph's path | `open(build)` never waits; `preOpen(waitForJob)` is the host's off-main open, with the build of the last open, refused on main; the bounded wait survives only there, for a background rebuild | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| The two turns | `schedule` → `rebuildScheduled` → `prepareOffMain` (probe, `release()`, `preOpen`) on `offMainContext`, then `rebuild` on `mainContext`; `releaseForRebuild` releases only a fenced handle; `resumeAndRebuild` for Control's forget | `SharedReplicaHost.kt`, `ControlSharedReplica.kt` |
| Try again | `SharedReplicaHost.tryAgain()` / `canTryAgain`, `Trigger.TRY_AGAIN` | `SharedReplicaHost.kt` |
| Protected data | the adapter's `onProtectedDataAvailable` → the binding → `SharedReplicaHost.onProtectedDataAvailable()`, `Trigger.PROTECTED_DATA` | `SharedReplicaUiKitAdapter.kt`, `SharedReplicaBinding.kt`, `SharedReplicaHost.kt` |
| A sibling's job | `NotReadyReplicaStore`'s `onAccess` → `SharedReplicaHost.onStandInAccess()`, `REOPEN_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS` = 2 s, `Trigger.SIBLING_FINISHED` | `SharedReplicaHost.kt` |
| A graph's foreground | `graphInstalled(…, foreground)`, `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.onCurrentGraphForeground(block)` (263) | `SharedReplicaHost.kt`, `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.kt` |
| Drive's kept answers | `DriveBackupSurface.replayKeptAnswers()` (at `start()` and at each foreground), the kept answers applied with a live one, the drop generation | `DriveBackupSurface.kt`, `DriveLocalRuntime.kt` |

#### B.17.2 The switch, and "off" unchanged

As B.16.2, and nothing new runs off:
- **No binding, no host, so nothing attached to the surface.** `StorageStateSurface.attach` is
  called only from `SharedReplicaBinding.process`, which only a switched process reaches. Its
  snapshot is then the constant `READY`, covering nothing, generation 0; `tryAgain()` answers
  false; an observer gets that one value and nothing after it.
- **The protected-data hook, the stand-in's access hook and the graph's foreground hook** are
  members of the binding, the stand-in and the host, none of which exist off.
- **Drive's replay** is reached only from `start()` (with no kept answer off: an answer with the
  switch off is applied or dropped as before, never kept) and from a foreground hook only a host
  calls.
- Tests: `withNoHostTheSnapshotIsReadyCoversNothingAndNeverChanges`; the existing switch-off tests
  of B.13.3, B.14.2, B.15 and B.16.2 pass unchanged.
- **No `project.yml`, entitlement, signing or Swift change in PR A.** ⭐ **No threat-model
  amendment**: no asset, key path or relay shape moves. The stand-in writes nothing, and the
  removed fallback was a write path (`objects/`), so the change only narrows what a switched app
  writes.

#### B.17.3 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.16.

254. ⚠⚠ **Q40 as built: the stand-in for every refusal, and a `SKEW` or `CORRUPT` stand-in is
     given up.** `sqliteStoreOrFileStore` no longer opens the file store for an open that cannot
     hand out a store; the file store is left only for the switch's own second half (the graph's
     relay is not the dev lab's, B.13 (180)), which is not a fallback. Every refusal binds
     `NotReadyReplicaStore` with its state: retryable as Q35, and the rest (`SKEW`, `CORRUPT`, an
     `Updating` with no worker, `SharedReplicaUnprotected`, anything else) with `willRetry` false.
     Control's `onBound` already declared nothing for the stand-in (B.16 (214)), so a newer
     sibling's store no longer declares `files` either.
     - ⚠ **`SKEW` and `CORRUPT` are never re-opened in this process**, where §6's table says the
       host re-opens at the next foreground. For `SKEW` the only way out is an update of this app,
       which relaunches it; for `CORRUPT` the marker never goes away by itself (§6). A re-open
       would be a reinstall per foreground that can only meet the same answer. Their graph is
       stopped and **abandoned** at its install (238): Timeline's parked manager is let go and
       Drive's kept answers dropped, as for a corrupt fence. Q48 asks to confirm.
     - The other non-retryable refusals are not retried by themselves either, but the user can
       ask (260).
255. **A host with no graph says so: `NO_GRAPH`**, before the process's first graph and after
     `forgetGraph` (a deprovision, a choice that no longer allows the store). It was `NOT_READY`
     ("no graph"), which a cover would have shown over the app's own connect screen. Nothing
     covers on `NO_GRAPH`: the app's gate decides.
256. **An `UPDATING` carries whether its job is a wipe** (`SharedReplicaNotReady.wipe`, from the
     open's `ReplicaOpenResult.Updating.job`), so the copy says "Refreshing…" for a wipe and
     "Updating storage…" for a migration, as §6 asks. A `StoreNeedsForeground` does not say which
     job it needs, and shows "Updating storage…".
257. ⚠⚠ **Q39's surface, as built.**
     - **The shape**: `snapshot()` and `observe(onChange)` returning a `StorageStateObservation`
       to `cancel()`, plus `tryAgain()`. The snapshot is a data class of a state name, `covers`,
       a title, a message, `canTryAgain` and `generation`: finished values, the copy in one Kotlin
       table, no enum or sealed type across the bridge (the `RealmStorageSurface` rule). The
       callback runs on the main thread, first with the state now, then at each change.
     - **What covers**: every state but `READY` and `NO_GRAPH`.
     - **The generation**: the host counts the graphs **after the process's first** that reach
       `READY`, and stamps the count on every status. The first graph's screens are built over it
       already (each app remounts at its first install), so only a rebuilt graph moves it, and the
       root's `.id(generation)` (PR B) re-creates every screen, view model and engine over the new
       graph. A deprovision then a re-provision moves it too; the app remounts there anyway.
     - **Attached at the binding's making**, not read at call time, so a root that observes
       before the runtime exists follows it from then on.
     - ⚠ The update surface names this app (§7, `core-schema-skew-surface.md`: on route 1 the app
       to name is the app itself), from `CFBundleDisplayName`, and has no button: there is no
       platform route.
     - ⚠ "Storage damaged" promises no export: Control's snapshot of `replica-damaged/` (§6
       step 4's `CORRUPT` column) is not built (Q47). ⭐ *Built in B.18: the cover now says what the
       copy's state is, Control's offers "Export damaged data" over a complete copy, and every
       other app's names Control.*
258. ⚠⚠ **Q41 as built: no wait on the graph's path, and a rebuild in two turns.**
     - **The graph's open never waits for a job** (`SharedReplicaBinding.open`): an `Updating`
       the worker runs is a retryable `SharedReplicaNotReady(UPDATING)` at once, and the job's
       finish rebuilds the graph (226, 231). This is B.16 (227) widened to the launch. The
       launch's 10 s wait on main (Q29) is gone.
     - **A scheduled rebuild's slow half runs off the main thread** (`prepareOffMain`, on
       `offMainContext`): the shipping-gate probe, step 2b's release of the fenced handle (its
       failure latches here, as in `rebuild`), and the open, through `preOpen`, with the build
       of the graph's last open (the same binary, so the same vector). The reinstall that follows
       on main finds the store open, so its turn is the Koin assembly and the app's `install()`
       and no SQLite work. `releaseForRebuild` now releases only a fenced handle: the only
       unfenced one cached at a rebuild is the one `preOpen` just opened (every path that ends a
       graph otherwise releases its handle itself).
     - **Only for a graph a rebuild may claim, and only once its stop has ended** (§6: step 2
       before 2b; B.16 (251)). Otherwise `prepareOffMain` does nothing and `rebuild` decides as
       before; a synchronous `rebuild` (`rebuildNow`, `resume(now = true)`) still does all of it
       on its caller's thread. Control's forget now uses the two-turn `resumeAndRebuild`.
     - **The bounded wait for a job survives only in `preOpen`**, for a background rebuild (an
       entry's retry, a fence inside an entry, a retry under `entry:rebuild`): B.16 (227)'s
       narrowing, so a Timeline visit during a wipe is still served. It never runs on main
       (`preOpen` refuses there).
     - ⚠ **What is left on main**: the reinstall itself, one turn, Koin and the app's components.
       Its length is the device figure of B.16.7 item 5 (B.17.7 item 3).
     - ⚠ `recheckChoice` (at each foreground, on main) reads the cached handle **without**
       `opening`, which `preOpen`'s wait may hold for up to 10 s; it is `@Volatile`.
259. **Q42's automatic retry**: at `UIApplicationProtectedDataDidBecomeAvailable` (the adapter's
     new `onProtectedDataAvailable`, on main), once per stand-in graph, and only when that
     graph's open was refused for `ProtectedDataUnavailable` (`SharedReplicaHostStatus.
     protectedDataUnavailable`, set by `hostStatusOfOpenFailure` before the `StoreUnavailable`
     case it belongs to). In the foreground it is scheduled as any rebuild; **in the background**
     (the first unlock is usually a background moment) under a token of its own
     (`entry:rebuild`, as (239)), and not at all with no time. A retry that is refused again
     installs a new stand-in, which has its own one retry at the next notification: a
     notification is a user's unlock, so this cannot loop. Outside the per-foreground budget.
260. **Q42's "Try again"**: `StorageStateSurface.tryAgain()` → `SharedReplicaHost.tryAgain()`.
     Offered (`canTryAgain`) on `NOT_READY` only, with a graph, not latched (222) and not held;
     **a non-retryable refusal's `NOT_READY` included**, since the user asking is new information.
     It marks the rebuild owed and schedules it (`Trigger.TRY_AGAIN`), outside the per-foreground
     budget: one press, one rebuild. The latched process's surface is "Storage unavailable … Quit
     and reopen", with no button.
261. ⚠⚠ **Q43 as built: a stand-in read is when the host looks again.** `NotReadyReplicaStore`
     tells the host each `getObject` and `setListener` (`onAccess`). While the state is
     `UPDATING`, in the foreground, with a rebuild owed and none running, **at most every
     `REOPEN_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS` (2 s) and one at a time**, the host runs `prepareOffMain` (no
     wait): a sibling's finished job moved the epoch, and the open now serves, which is followed
     by a rebuild (`Trigger.SIBLING_FINISHED`, outside the budget); an open that does not serve
     rebuilds nothing. The access itself never blocks. ⚠ A re-open hands an `Updating` job to
     this process's worker again; the worker dedups by registry (`scheduleReplacement`), so that
     is at most one more run of a job a sibling also runs. ⚠ **What it does not cover**: with the
     root covered (PR B) and the graph stopped, a stand-in may see no read at all, and then the
     host looks at the next foreground or entry as before. Q46 asks about a bounded poll.
262. **Q44 confirmed against the code.** `hostStatusOfOpenFailure`'s retryable set is B.16
     (215)'s: every `StoreUnavailable` (`ProtectedDataUnavailable` now marked, (259)),
     `StoreBeingChecked` as `CHECKING`, `HoldCeilingExceeded`, `StoreNeedsForeground` as
     `UPDATING`, and an `Updating` the open did not wait for or whose wait (now only `preOpen`'s)
     did not see finish. Since (258) "an `Updating` past the wait" is the background rebuild's
     case only: every other `Updating` with a worker is retryable at once.
263. **A graph's foreground hook** (`graphInstalled(…, foreground)`,
     `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.onCurrentGraphForeground`): run by `onForeground`, on main inside the
     notification, only while that graph serves (not stopped, `READY`), after the owed rebuild is
     scheduled. It must only dispatch. Drive is its one user (265).
264. **The (253) completion handler cannot throw.** `stopDone.invokeOnCompletion`'s body runs on
     whatever thread ends the stop, and on K/N a throw there reaches the global handler and ends
     the process; it is wrapped and logged.
265. **Drive's kept new-folder answers are replayed, not persisted.** The brief allowed either.
     Built: the kept answers are applied by the serving graph **at each foreground**
     (`onCurrentGraphForeground` → `replayKeptAnswers()`, which only launches on the controller's
     scope) and **with the next live answer** (inside the same `Mutex`, before the live write, so
     the live answer is still the one written for its bucket), as well as at `start()`. Each is
     still removed only once its write succeeded (243). ⚠ **Not persisted**: a kept answer dies
     with the process, as before. A persisted one would have to carry its realm (a deprovision at
     a launch builds no graph, so no abandon drops it), which is more than this slice. Q49.
266. **A keep after its graph was given up is refused.** An answer captures the drop generation
     when it begins, and every `keepAnswer` it reaches is refused (with a line) once
     `dropKeptAnswers` has moved it: a no-token answer that ended after a deprovision's drop no
     longer waits for the next realm's graph.
267. ⚠ **The per-foreground budget, stated** (the slice-1 carry-over). Only `FOREGROUND` counts
     against §6's "at most once per foreground". `ENTRY` (once per background since (232)),
     `JOB_FINISHED`, `EXPLICIT`, `TRY_AGAIN`, `PROTECTED_DATA` and `SIBLING_FINISHED` are each
     one discrete event and skip it. A rebuild held back by a claimed stop (251) is attempted
     **at most twice** for its event: the back-off, then the one retry when `stopDone` completes
     (253). ⚠ M410 has no foreground test (B.16.14: the collector's own post-stop check answers
     first there); M412 is the mutant that reaches the foreground branch.
268. **Two PRs.** PR A is the Kotlin core above, reviewable on its own and inert for Swift (a new
     surface nobody observes yet, so no Swift is owed by it). PR B is the ten `RootView`s: one
     shared view in `ios-storage/Sources` (already compiled into all ten apps) and one modifier
     per root, each app built by `scripts/ios-smoke.sh --build-only`. The split keeps ten
     XCFramework builds and the Swift review out of the Kotlin review.
