### B.20 S0b-4 slice 1: the cutover from the shared file store, drain-gated wipe and re-sync (2026-11-01)

> ⚠⚠ **Superseded 2026-11-05 by B.22**: nothing shipped, so an old file store is reset at launch
> with no drain, and the store is on in every build. This cutover is unreachable and is deleted in a
> follow-up cleanup PR (B.22.4). Its switch-on gates (378, 401–403, 405, 406, Q61) are moot
> (B.22.3); 404 and 364 are done in B.22.

**What it is.** §8's open item, decided by the maintainer on 2026-11-01: **route (b)**, wipe and
re-sync, never an importer. A phone whose group container already holds the shared
`FileObjectStore` (`objects/`, and its watermark `sync-hlc/`) moves to the SQLite store only once
nothing in the old store is this device's alone; then the old store and its watermark go together,
and the SQLite store pulls from cursor 0. **Slice 1 is that cutover and its tests.** Slice 2 (its own
PR) is the protection class and backup flag (D3/D3b), Appendix A's threat-model amendment and the
switch decision. The legacy file-store code stays (B.20.6).

- ⭐ **Control performs the cutover; nobody else does.** It already owns the replica choice
  (B.14 (190)) and provisioning (§8 step 3).
- ⭐ **The drain is a proof, never a wait.** The wipe is refused while any outbound item, journal,
  unfinished upload or unsent-content marker remains, while the realm is locked, or while it was
  never registered with a relay; and while anything of that could not be read. There is no timeout.
- ⭐ **Resumable and idempotent**: the commit point is one `rename(2)`; a kill at any step is
  finished (or undone) by the next call, in any process.
- ⚠ With the switch off nothing changes (B.20.2). A switched build still needs the dev lab's relay
  (B.13 (180)) until slice 2 decides the switch.

#### B.20.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The drain proof over the store | `outboundBacklog`: every queue `purgeOutboundQueues` drops (the same list), each shared realm's pending blocks, the owner-scoped rekey tombstones, the rekey journal, the tombstone cascades, unfinished one-shot schedule items, and the realm (unlocked, registered); counted from the **durable** rows (`invalidateCached` first), as listed, never decoded | `sync-service-proxy/.../OutboundBacklog.kt` |
| The cutover | `LegacyFileStoreCutover`: what is there (`ABSENT`, `EMPTY_SHELL`, `PRESENT`, `UNKNOWN`), what is owed outside the store (upload staging with bytes, `files/.unsent-content/`), the commit under the file store's `flock`, the resume, the bulk delete | `core-common/src/iosMain/.../LegacyFileStoreCutover.kt` |
| The fence | `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock(fencedBy = objects/)`: every outermost entry, once it holds the `flock`, checks `objects/`' `dev:ino` against the one it first saw; a retired store throws `FileStoreRetired` | `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock.kt` |
| Control | `ControlSharedReplica.runtimeModule`: the cutover at launch (a resumed commit, a store with nothing to drain); otherwise Control on the file store (fenced), `files` declared, and a drain watcher that attempts the cutover over Control's live graph in the foreground and rebuilds the graph after; `cutoverStatus` | `tenshu-sdk-ios-core/.../ControlSharedReplica.kt` |
| The apps | a switched app on the file store (Control's choice not `sqlite`) takes the fenced lock | `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.sqliteBindingForAssembly`, `fencedFileStoreLockModule` |

#### B.20.2 The switch, and "off" unchanged

- Everything new runs only when `ControlSharedReplica.isSwitched` (the plist's `YES` **and** the dev
  lab's relay, B.13 (180)) or, for an app, when `sqliteBindingFor` answers a binding.
- `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock` gains an optional `fencedBy`; every unswitched construction passes
  none (`PlatformProxyModule`, `sharedReplicaStoreModule`'s file-store branch, the test replica
  directory), so its behaviour is byte for byte what it was. `purgeOutboundQueues`' list is shared,
  not changed.
- The build in App Store review (Control 1.0) is an uploaded archive and cannot be changed by a
  commit; and nothing here reaches a Release build, whose relay can never pass (180).

#### B.20.3 Decisions made in implementation, for review

353. ⚠⚠ **Control performs the cutover, the apps wait on the file store.** A switched Control whose
     group container still holds the old store binds **the file store** (the same directory and
     migrations config the platform module binds, with the fenced lock) and declares `files`, so
     every switched app follows it there (190), exactly as before. The apps never cut over: a
     route-1 app has no view of another app's in-memory work, and Control is the one process that
     declares. Two apps launching the new build at different times is therefore harmless: before
     Control's cutover each joins the file store (and its writes are part of Control's drain proof,
     since the queues are shared); after it each reads `sqlite` at its next assembly.
354. ⚠⚠ **The drain proof is the shared queues on disk plus the realm, under the `flock`.** One
     attempt, in Control's process, in the foreground, every 15 s while Control runs the old store:
     (1) `outboundBacklog` over Control's live graph, the realm included, with nothing stopped, and
     `outsideTheStore()` (staging, unsent content, every app's emit journal and `.orphaned` record:
     cheap; B.20.16 (398)); any backlog or reason ends the attempt with the graph untouched. (2) Control's own emit pipeline flushed (`awaitEmitIdle`, bounded at
     10 s: a save made but not yet queued). (3) Control's graph stopped (`stopGraph`: the
     `SyncManager` locked, pairing stopped). (4) `LegacyFileStoreCutover.cutOver` under the file
     store's writer lock, which asks the queues **again, from disk**: a sibling's enqueue since (1)
     refuses the commit. The realm is not asked at (4), because (3) just locked it on purpose.
     Whatever (4) answers, the graph is rebuilt (`rebuildRealRuntime`): over the SQLite store after a
     commit, over the file store again (and watched again) after a refusal.
355. **What the proof reads, and why each.** `PENDING_BLOCKS` (and `PENDING_BLOCKS::<owner>` per shared
     realm), `PENDING_TOMBSTONES`, `PENDING_REAP_REMOVALS`, `PENDING_LANE_DELTAS`,
     `PENDING_CONTENT_EMITS` (the purge's list, shared so the two cannot drift),
     `PENDING_REKEY_TOMBSTONES/<owner>` for the resident and every shared realm,
     `PENDING_REKEY_MIGRATIONS` (an interrupted `DataId` migration), `PENDING_TOMBSTONE_CASCADES`,
     every `ONE_SHOT` `ScheduleItem` still `PENDING` or `RUNNING` (a periodic one re-registers at
     init; the S0 inventory left one-shots "not established", so they block), a realm that is
     **locked** (its saves are held in memory and empty queues prove nothing, the locked-save gap)
     or **not registered with a relay** (none of it has a copy anywhere). Outside the store:
     `upload-staging/` holding bytes (Drive's background uploads), `files/.unsent-content/` (a write
     saved but not handed to the emitter). Deferred moves are gone since CR-2 B6 D4, so nothing reads them.
356. **Counted as listed, never decoded.** A queue is counted by its row's member hashes. An element
     this build cannot decode, or one whose row is gone, is still something queued; decoding it
     would turn a count into a blocker that never clears. ⚠ That is the file store's list layout;
     the proof is never asked of the SQLite store (B.19's segments). Anything the proof could not
     read is a blocker (**unknown is not empty**), never a zero.
357. ⚠⚠ **The commit is one rename, and every step resumes.** Under the lock: `replica-legacy.retired/`
     made; `objects/` renamed into it (**the commit point**; a store with no `objects/` commits by
     making it there); `sync-hlc/` renamed after it; Control told (it declares `reset`); the retired
     directory renamed to a unique `replica-legacy.removing-<random>`. After the lock: every
     `removing-*` deleted. Every call first finishes what it finds: a retired directory **with**
     `objects` is committed and finished without a new drain proof (the commit had one); one
     **without** is a kill before the commit and is removed, leaving `objects/` in place to be proven
     again; a `removing-*` is deleted. The unique name is what lets two finishers run at once without
     one deleting under the other, or under a store made again at `objects/`. Control is told before
     the hand-off, so a kill between them tells it twice (idempotent), never not at all.
358. ⚠⚠ **The watermark goes with its store, never after it in another launch.** ⚠ *Not true as first built: a sibling's raise could make `sync-hlc/` again after the retire, and a lone `sync-hlc/` (the SQLite store's) was retired at every launch; both fixed in fix round 1 (374), (375).* `sync-hlc/` is still
     the live watermark on the SQLite path (B.13.2: §5.4's `meta` copy is not built), so the
     cutover's removal is what makes the new store start with an empty watermark: one older than its
     store forges the tombstone-GC acknowledgement (§8). A kill between the two renames leaves it
     beside, and the next call (at Control's next launch, before any graph) moves it.
359. ⚠⚠ **A process still on the file store is fenced, not trusted.** Every file-store access already
     takes the writer `flock`; a switched process's lock (Control's for the drain, every switched
     app's while Control's choice is not `sqlite`) also checks `objects/`' `dev:ino` once it holds it.
     After the cutover the directory is gone, so the next access throws `FileStoreRetired` instead of
     writing into its absence (`writeToFile` into a missing directory fails **silently**, and a batch
     would make `objects/` again under its staging directory). The app's screens show an error until
     it is relaunched, when it reads `sqlite` and opens the SQLite store. *Chosen over a heartbeat or
     a presence lock* because a lock held across suspension is the `0xdead10cc` this whole design
     exists to end, and a heartbeat is a "waited long enough".
360. **At launch, before any graph**, Control calls the cutover with a proof that refuses a store
     with rows: so a resumed commit, a device that was never on the file store (`NothingToDo`) and
     an old store with nothing in it to drain (sidecars, a watermark alone, no upload owed) are
     settled at once and Control binds SQLite in the same launch. A store with rows needs the graph,
     so Control binds the file store for that launch.
361. **What the user sees.** *Draining*: nothing new. Control and every app work on the file store as
     before, and that is what the drain needs: Control open, online and unlocked. Nothing covers,
     because a cover would stop the very use (unlocking, staying open) that lets the drain finish.
     *The switch*: Control's graph stops and is rebuilt over the empty SQLite store, as S0b-3's
     rebuild after a forget does (`rebuildRealRuntime`); the old store's removal is a rename, so the
     stop lasts the rebuild. *The re-pull*: the sync-activity capsule (cross-process activity is its
     own track). *A drain that cannot finish* (offline, relay errors, a realm left locked, an upload
     that never ends): Control stays on the file store, every 15 s in the foreground and at every
     launch it looks again, and `cutoverStatus` says what is outstanding (logged). *Killed mid-way*:
     B.20.3 (357). `ControlSharedReplica.cutoverStatus` is Kotlin-only; no Swift reads it yet (Q58).
362. **A forget during the drain** ends the watcher; the forget's existing order runs (B.14 (191)),
     and the next assembly decides the cutover again (the forget's file-store wipe leaves an empty
     shell, retired at launch).
363. **`files/` stays.** It is the content cache, keyed by content; once the drain shows no unsent
     content and no unfinished upload, every byte in it is re-fetchable and is reused where the
     re-pulled rows name it. The S0 inventory's "lost, all derivable" applies only if it were removed.
364. ⚠ **Found, not fixed: `FileAdvisoryLock.open` can hand two first-ever openers different files.**
     It creates a missing lock file with `createFileAtPath`, which replaces a file another opener
     created a moment before; the two then `flock` different inodes and exclude nothing. The race
     test showed it (two threads, no lock file yet). It needs the lock file not to exist, so on a
     phone with a file store (the only place the cutover runs) it cannot happen; the test creates the
     file first, as such a phone has. Left as found because the class is deleted with the legacy code
     (B.20.6); the fix, if it is wanted before, is `open(O_RDWR | O_CREAT)` without the create call.

#### B.20.4 What this slice does not have

| `replica/`'s protection class and backup flag, and `files/`' and `upload-staging/`'s (D3, D3b) | slice 2 |
| Appendix A's threat-model amendment | slice 2 (the cutover changes no asset A1–A4 or A9, no relay data shape and no protocol) |
| The switch: on by default, or per build, and the relay guard (180) | slice 2 |
| A Swift surface for `cutoverStatus` | Q58 |
| `FileObjectStore`, its helpers, `HlcWatermarkFile`, `FileAdvisoryLock`, `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock` and the two `as? FileObjectStore` downcasts deleted | ⚠ **after App Store approval** of Control 1.0, in a hotfix (B.20.6); `tech-debt.md` |

| Q58 | The drain is silent: no surface says "Control is finishing sync before the storage update". | **A one-line, non-covering note in Control only** (Settings, under storage), from `cutoverStatus`: *"Finishing sync before a storage update: N changes still to send. Keep Tenshu Control open and online."* Never a cover (361). Small Swift change in Control's `RootView`; its own slice |
| Q59 | ~~A sibling's in-memory work at the instant of the commit is invisible to the proof.~~ | ⭐ **Closed by fix round 1 (373)**: not confined to Split View (a suspended Drive mid bulk move, a Timeline background wake), so it is not a residual. Every switched process on the file store keeps a durable "saves not yet queued" marker, counted before the row is written, and the proof refuses while any exists |
| Q60 | A queue whose elements can never drain (a dangling member, a block the relay keeps refusing) keeps the phone on the file store for good. | **Accept; no time-based escape** (the maintainer's rule). Add an explicit, person-made discard later if a real phone meets it, like `TENSHU_DISCARD_LEGACY_REPLICA`: a decision, not a timeout |
| Q61 | A phone with a mixed switch, or an **old build** of a sibling (iOS updates apps one at a time), writes `objects/` again after the cutover. ~~Nothing lost~~ ⚠ **wrong** (fix round 1, S2): an old build has no fence and no saves-not-yet-queued marker, so its in-memory saves at the commit are invisible and its later writes land in a new file store. | ⚠⚠ **A hard gate for slice 2's switch-on (378)**: no build turns the store on until every app that has used it is a fence-capable build |

two `as? FileObjectStore` downcasts (`FirstPartyLocalRuntime.rehydrate`, `ControlSurface.rehydrateSharedReplica`)
are **deleted in a hotfix after Control-iOS 1.0 is approved by App Store review**, not in S0b-4.
Until then they stay, unswitched builds keep using them, and this slice only adds the fence beside
them. `tech-debt.md` *"The legacy iOS file store is deleted after App Store approval"* tracks it.

#### B.20.9 Fix round 1 (the independent review and Codex on `0ed5ab12f`)

Two blockers, five Codex P1s and two should-fix, each with a test and a mutation that turns it red
(the table below).

370. ⚠⚠ **(a) A queue row a sibling created was read as "no such row".** `FileObjectStore`'s
     `present` is the index built at open, and `invalidateCached` cleared the cache only, so a row a
     sibling **created** since (a first `PENDING_BLOCKS::<owner>` or `PENDING_REKEY_TOMBSTONES/<owner>`)
     was answered absent without a disk read. `invalidateCached` now refreshes `present` from disk
     per hash, and the proof reads every queue row through the new `ObjectStore.readDurable` (a
     re-stat and re-read). ⚠ The same blind spot was in `RetiredBlockSweeper`'s keep-set, which
     deletes what it does not see: the `invalidateCached` fix closes it there too.
371. ⚠⚠ **(c) Unreadable is not empty.** `getObject(...)?.fields?.size ?: 0` read a torn, vanished or
     undecodable queue row as 0. `readDurable` answers `Absent`, `Present` or `Unreadable`; only
     `Absent` counts as an empty queue, `Unreadable` blocks (the schedule list too).
372. **(d) The final look lost the owner-scoped queue.** The look under the `flock` runs after the
     stop locked the session, so `residentOwnerId` was null and `PENDING_REKEY_TOMBSTONES/<owner>`
     was not read. The first look's owner (`OutboundBacklog.residentOwnerId`) is passed to it.
373. ⚠⚠ **(b) A save written but not yet queued** lives only in the writing process's memory
     (`SyncObserver` writes the row, then `trySend`s it to its emit channel or, locked, its hold),
     so a suspended Drive mid bulk move, or a Timeline background wake, could be wiped. Every switched
     process on the file store (and Control while it drains) installs `EmitBacklogMarker`: a file
     `replica-emit-pending/<app>`, counted **in `prepareSave`, before the row is written**, removed
     when the count is back at 0 after the block is queued (a held save stays counted until its
     replay is). The proof refuses while any file is there. A process that died with one leaves it;
     the app's next launch removes its own (its saves died with it). With no marker installed
     `SyncObserver` is exactly as before. Replaces the Q59 residual. ⚠ A save whose write then throws
     stays counted until that app's next launch (conservative).
374. ⚠⚠ **(e) The watermark is fenced too.** `HlcWatermarkFile.raiseTo` made `sync-hlc/` again under
     its own lock, outside the fence, so a sibling's tick after the retire wrote the old store's high
     stamp beside the new store. A switched process on the file store now raises **under its fenced
     writer lock** (`HlcWatermarkFile(guard)`, bound through `FileStoreFence` in its graph), so the
     raise fails `FileStoreRetired` and makes nothing. ⚠ (358)'s "never after it in another launch"
     was not true before this.
375. ⚠⚠ **B1: a lone `sync-hlc/` is not the old store.** It is also the SQLite store's live watermark
     (B.13.2), so classing it `EMPTY_SHELL` retired it at every Control launch after the cutover
     (tips stepping back, peers showing `DIVERGENCE`), and an upload in flight turned that into a
     refusal that declared `files` over a new, empty file store. `objects/` absent is now `ABSENT`
     whatever `sync-hlc/` holds; `EMPTY_SHELL` is `objects/` with no row, whose watermark still goes
     with it.
376. ⚠⚠ **B2: `reset` is never the file store.** An app reading Control's `reset` (Control killed
     between the commit and its SQLite open, or its open handed out the stand-in) bound the file
     store, whose first write made a new `objects/`, and the whole phone went back onto an empty file
     store. It now waits on the not-ready stand-in (retryable, rebuilt at the next foreground or
     entry). And `FileStoreFence` latches an absent `objects/` as an identity: a store made later is
     not the one this process opened.
377. **S1: `FileStoreRetired` is a `StoreHandleFenced`**, the typed "this handle no longer serves" the
     SQLite store's callers already tell apart, never a bare `IllegalStateException`. ⚠ **Owed:**
     routing it into the S0b-3 host (stop the graph, "Updating storage…", rebuild onto SQLite at the
     next foreground). A process on the file store has no host graph today; until then a fenced app
     shows errors until it is relaunched.
378. ⚠⚠ **S2, a hard gate for slice 2's switch-on.** An old-build sibling has no fence and no marker:
     its in-memory saves at the commit are invisible and its later writes land in a new file store.
     Before any build turns the store on, the cutover must refuse until every app that has used the
     store (its `RuntimeIdentity` rows name them) has written a "fence-capable build" marker.
     Recorded here rather than built; Q61 is corrected accordingly.
     ⚠⚠ The other switch-on gates are beside it in B.20.16 (401–406).
379. **Low, recorded:** `cutoverAtLaunch` and `attemptCutover` hold the file store's blocking `flock`
     across the commit's IO after one foreground check. The commit is renames and `stat`s (the bulk
     delete runs after the lock), so the window is short, but a suspension inside it is the
     `0xdead10cc` class. Owed: a `beginBackgroundTask` around the attempt.
380. **Low, recorded:** `theBindingsPrepareOpensNothingOnceItsTicketHasMoved` no longer exercises the
     host's own rebuild; that path is covered by
     `anExpiryFencedGraphIsStoppedInTheBackgroundAndRebuiltAtTheNextForeground` and
     `aRegainedQuiesceFenceIsRebuiltInTheSameForeground` (`SharedReplicaHostTest`).

#### B.20.10 Fix round 2 (Codex on `bb473bc11`)

381. ⚠⚠ **A dead process's saves are re-emitted, never forgotten.** Round 1's marker was a count, and
     a stale one was deleted at the app's next launch, though the save it stood for may never have
     been emitted: the row survives the kill, the in-memory event does not, and
     `reemitPendingLockedWork` replays only the live process's channels. Control would then see
     empty queues and no marker, and the cutover would wipe the change. Now:
     - the marker **names the rows**: an append-only journal `replica-emit-pending/<app>`, `+key`
       written in `prepareSave` before the row and `-key` once its block is queued, where a key is
       the row's `StringDataId` or `LongDataId` (`EmitBacklogMarker.keyOf`), or its hash alone for
       any other kind;
     - at the next launch the dead journal's outstanding keys are folded into
       `<app>.orphaned` (still in the directory, so the proof still refuses), and that process's
       `SyncObserver`, once the realm is enabled (`reemitPendingLockedWork`, the scheduler's enable
       edge), reads each row from the store and re-emits it, **counting it live first**, and only
       then lets the record go;
     - a key that names no row this build can rebuild (a hash alone), or whose row cannot be read,
       **stays recorded**, so the cutover keeps refusing; a row that is gone needs nothing (its
       delete is its own tombstone). A journal that cannot be read is kept as it is.
     - Only saves that emit blocks are recorded (a `Syncable` row, or an entity with a `Syncable`
       property: `processSavedData`'s rule). A re-emit of a save that had been queued after all makes
       a second block of the same row, which is harmless.
382. **A failed write's record resolves.** A save whose write throws was counted and never
     processed; at the next launch its key is an orphan whose row was never written, so the recovery
     finds nothing to send and lets it go. Round 1's "stays counted until the next launch" was the
     whole of it then; now the next launch also proves it.
383. ⚠⚠ **The schedule's members are read from the durable copy.** Round 1 refreshed the schedule
     list's own row, but `readArray` fetches members through `getObject` (this process's `present`
     index) and `DbEntryMapper` skips a member it does not find, so a one-shot item a sibling
     scheduled after Control opened counted 0. Now each listed member is read through `readDurable`
     (absent or unreadable blocks), the members and the composite rows they name are re-read
     (`invalidateCached`), and a decode that yields fewer items than the row lists blocks. The whole
     proof now runs under the store's lock, since the durable reads refresh the store's index.
384. **Audit of the proof and the sweeper.** The proof decodes nothing else: every queue is counted
     from its durable row's member list, and a queue that lists any member already blocks, so its
     members are not read one by one. `RetiredBlockSweeper`'s keep-set decoded each queue through
     `getArrayData`, the same pattern: it now takes the members **as the durable row lists them**,
     a superset of what a decode yields (it keeps more, never less), and an unreadable queue row
     stops the pass. ⚠ The old keep-set was not exploitable as found: the sweep's delete re-reads
     each candidate through the same index, so a block the index did not know was neither kept nor
     deleted. The change removes that dependence.

| (1) | `anOrphanThatNamesNoRebuildableRowIsKeptAndOneWhoseRowIsGoneResolves` (JVM) | G4: an unrebuildable key dropped; G5: a gone row kept | ✓, ✓ |

#### B.20.11 Fix round 3 (Codex on `602a8ab77`)

385. ⚠⚠ **Owner-keyed queues are found on disk, not through the registry.** The proof named the
     shared realms' queues (`PENDING_BLOCKS::<owner>`, `PENDING_REKEY_TOMBSTONES/<owner>`) from
     Control's in-memory `RealmRegistry`, which does not know a realm a sibling joined or created
     after Control's graph started, so that realm's queue went uncounted, the final look under the
     `flock` included. The relation names are hashed, so they cannot be listed by prefix; and no
     single row type names every realm a device belongs to (memberships, grants, its own genesis).
     So the **final look** (`outboundBacklog(exhaustive = true)`) trusts no list of owners:
     - the store's index is rebuilt from the disk (`ObjectStore.refreshIndex`; `FileObjectStore`
       re-lists its directory), then **every list row on disk** is enumerated
       (`scanRowsOfType("tenshu/core/list")`) and re-read through `readDurable`;
     - a list whose members are `RekeyMigrationMarker`s is a rekey journal (no other list holds
       them), counted whatever its owner;
     - a list whose members are `SyncBlock`s is a pending-blocks queue exactly when its hash is
       `PENDING_BLOCKS::<owner>` for the owner its blocks carry (or the bare `PENDING_BLOCKS`):
       counted. Any other list of blocks (`RECEIVED_TOMBSTONES`, inbound) is not a queue;
     - a list row there but unreadable blocks; a store that cannot enumerate blocks; a list none of
       whose first 8 members can be read is not identified, and is logged (a queue whose members are
       all gone could not be pushed either).
     The cheap first look keeps the registry (it decides only whether to stop the graph). ⚠ The
     final look reads every row of the store once per attempt: seconds on a large store, under the
     `flock`, in the foreground, and only after the first look found nothing.
     **Audit of the remaining in-memory sources:** the realm's state (unlocked, registered) is the
     first look's and is meant to be the session's; the resident owner of the final look is the first
     look's; everything else the proof reads (the bare queues, the schedule, upload staging,
     unsent-content markers, saves-not-yet-queued markers) is read from the disk.
386. ⚠⚠ **An orphan's record goes only on a confirmed absence.** The recovery read the row through
     `getData`, whose null also stands for a blob `FileObjectStore.readThrough` could not read for now
     (it then drops it from its index without throwing), so the record went with nothing queued. It
     now reads `Database.readDurable` first (`DatabaseImpl` → `ObjectStore.readDurable`): `Absent`
     releases the key, `Unreadable` keeps it, and a `Present` row that `getData` still cannot read
     keeps it too. A `Database` that cannot read its durable copy answers `Unreadable` by default,
     so it keeps every record. **Sweep of the round-2 code for other "null means gone" reads:** a
     `Syncable` save with no `DataId` was not recorded at all (it still emits a block): it is now
     recorded under a key no later process can rebuild, so it stays and the cutover refuses; the
     marker's file reads already tell a missing file from an unreadable one.

| (1) | `aRekeyJournalOfAnOwnerNobodyNamesRefusesTheExhaustiveLook` (JVM) | H1; H2: a rekey journal not recognised | ✓, ✓ |

#### B.20.12 Fix round 4 (Codex on `fd7377838`)

387. ⚠⚠ **A save's record goes only once its block is durably queued.** The emit consumer let the key
     go in a `finally`, so a save whose block was never queued (serialisation, encryption or the
     queue write threw; or `generateSyncBlock` found no realm to make it in and returned silently;
     or a teardown cancelled it) lost its record. Now `generateSyncBlock` says whether it queued,
     `processSavedData` is true only when every block it owes is queued, a lane save counts once its
     delta is in the durable lane journal, and only then is the key released. Otherwise the key stays
     in this process's journal (logged each time), the cutover keeps refusing, and the next launch's
     recovery retries it. The held-save path (a locked realm) and the re-emit path go through the same
     consumer, so the same rule. ⚠ A row that fails every time keeps the cutover refused for good, and
     says so in the log at every attempt; no other surface.
388. ⚠⚠ **An unidentifiable list blocks.** A list is identified by its first member that can be read,
     **looking through all of them**; one none of whose members can be read blocks, and is skipped
     only when every member is confirmed absent on disk. Also blocking now: a list of blocks whose
     owner cannot be read (it may be any realm's queue), a list member that is not a row reference,
     and **a row the enumeration had to pass over**: `FileObjectStore.scanRowsOfType` steps past a
     blob it cannot decode without saying so, so the store now counts them
     (`ObjectStore.unreadableRowsSeen`) and the final look compares the count before and after.
     ⚠ A torn blob of any type anywhere in the store therefore keeps the cutover refused until it is
     removed: unknown is not empty, and it may have been a queue.
389. **Every skip the proof and the recovery still make, and why each is sound** (the pass the
     coordinator asked for, branch by branch):
     - *Bare queues*: a queue row `readDurable` confirms `Absent` counts 0 (the file store re-stats
       it); `Unreadable` blocks; a non-empty queue blocks whatever its members hold, so its members
       are not read.
     - *Schedule*: `Absent` row → 0 (confirmed); a member `Absent` or `Unreadable` blocks; a decode
       that throws or yields fewer items blocks; periodic and finished items are not owed work.
     - *Disk lists*: a list already counted by name is skipped (counted once); a list row `Absent` is
       skipped (confirmed gone since the index listed it); an empty list holds nothing; a list whose
       every member is confirmed absent holds nothing that exists; a list whose first readable member
       is neither a `SyncBlock` nor a `RekeyMigrationMarker` is not an owner-keyed queue (only those
       two kinds are, and the bare queues of every other kind are counted by name); a list of blocks
       whose hash is neither `PENDING_BLOCKS` nor `PENDING_BLOCKS::<its blocks' owner>` is not a queue
       (a queue's blocks carry its owner by construction: `generateSyncBlock` names both from one
       realm). Everything else unknown blocks.
     - *Realm*: the first look's unlocked and registered checks fail closed (an exception reads as
       locked or unregistered).
     - *Orphan recovery*: no marker installed means an unswitched process (nothing recorded); a record
       that cannot be read is neither re-emitted nor released (it stays on disk); a key with no
       rebuildable `DataId` is kept; a row confirmed `Absent` is released (its delete is its own
       tombstone); `Unreadable`, or `Present` but not readable through `getData`, is kept; a re-emit
       is released only by the consumer's rule above.
     - *Marker files*: a dead journal or orphan record that cannot be read is left as it is; a missing
       file is the only "nothing".

#### B.20.13 Fix round 5 (Codex on `46e06aa8a`)

390. ⚠⚠ **A failed listing is not an empty index.** `FileObjectStore.refreshIndex` rebuilt the index
     with `contentsOfDirectoryAtPath(...).orEmpty()`, so a listing that failed left an index of
     nothing and the final look's enumeration saw no lists at all. It now lists strictly
     (`listDirectory`: `null` only for a failure, empty only for a directory the disk says is
     empty) and throws `StoreIndexUnreadable`, leaving the index as it was; the final look turns the
     throw into a blocker.
391. ⚠⚠ **A save that cannot be recorded is refused.** A failed `+key` append was only logged, so
     `prepareSave` returned and the row was written with no durable record. Now the append's failure
     throws `EmitBacklogUnrecorded` from `prepareSave`, **before the row is written**: the save fails
     with that typed error (an operation reports it as its failure, never an empty success). A save
     that reaches the observer only after its row is written (no `prepareSave`) cannot be refused:
     its key is written to the orphan record instead (`recordUnqueued`), still emitted now, and
     re-emitted by the next process; if that write fails too, the observer throws, never swallows.
392. **Every `.orEmpty()`, `?: emptyList()`, `?: emptySet()`, `?: 0` on a file call or a read in the
     legacy store, the marker files and the cutover, and why each left is sound:**
     - `FileObjectStore.refreshIndex`: changed (390).
     - `FileObjectStore.readHashes` at `open`, the batch-staging commit's two listings, `wipeBlobs`:
       not on the proof's path. The proof's first look reads every queue row through `readDurable`
       (a `stat` and a read each), and its final look rebuilds the index strictly (390); a failed
       listing in those legacy paths deletes or moves nothing it did not list (the safe direction),
       as before.
     - `readObjectStoreEntries`: diagnostics and tests only. `wipeFileObjectStore` answers `-1` for
       a failed listing already. The format-version `?: 0`: the legacy open's gate, as before.
     - `LegacyFileStoreCutover`: has none; every look goes through `entryExists`, `listDirectory` and
       `countFilesUnder`, which keep "could not tell" apart, and every removal is checked afterwards.
     - The marker files: `readLines` now tells a missing file from one it could not look at
       (`pathExistsStrictly`; `fileExistsAtPath` answers false for both), so its `.orEmpty()` runs only
       on a confirmed missing record; the journal's `?: 0` is counting arithmetic.
     **Every write in the marker and journal code:** `+key` (refuses the save, 391); the orphan record
     of a written save (throws, 391); `-key` and the journal's removal at 0 (a failure leaves the key
     outstanding: still blocking, re-emitted once more by the next process, harmless); the dead
     journal's fold into the orphan record (a failure keeps the dead journal: still blocking); the
     orphan record's rewrite after recovery (a failure keeps every key: still blocking); the
     directory's creation (a failure makes the next `+key` fail: refused).

#### B.20.14 Fix round 6 (Codex on `e8ff6d940`)

393. ⚠⚠ **A follower decides, and opens, under the cutover's `flock`.** A switched app that read
     `files` could be suspended before its file store opened; meanwhile Control's cutover retired
     `objects/` and declared `sqlite`; on resume `openFileObjectStore` made `objects/` again and the
     fence's first check adopted that new directory, so an unfenced file replica ran beside the SQLite
     store. Now:
     - the follower's decision is taken **under the file store's writer `flock`** (the one the
       cutover holds while it retires the store), reading in one moment the replica choice again,
       whether a cutover was ever committed here, and the identity (`dev:ino`) of `objects/`;
     - a commit now writes **`replica-legacy.cutover-done`**, never removed: after it no follower
       joins a file store again, whatever made `objects/` since;
     - the follower joins the file store only when the choice still says so, no cutover was ever
       committed, and `objects/` **exists**: ⚠ a follower never makes `objects/` (only Control, the
       store's owner, does, before any cutover); otherwise it waits on the retryable stand-in, rebuilt
       at the next foreground or entry, when Control may have declared `sqlite`;
     - its open runs under the same `flock` and only over the identity captured with the choice
       (`FileStoreFence(presetIdentity)` too, so the fence never adopts a directory first seen later);
       a store retired in between is the stand-in, not a new `objects/`.
     A follower now installs the binding (its host rebuilds the stand-in), but rule P's loops stay
     unbound over the file store, as before. ⚠ Control's own open of the file store for the drain is
     not under this rule: Control is the one process that cuts over, so it cannot race its own
     cutover between its launch check and its open.
394. ⚠⚠ **Each process its own emit journal.** The live journal was the app's one file, so a dead
     journal that could not be adopted (unreadable, or its keys not recordable) stayed at that path
     with this process's count at 0, and the first live save's release deleted it, dead keys and all.
     The live journal is now `<app>.live-<launch>`, a file no other process writes: a dead journal
     (any other `<app>.live-*`, or the bare `<app>` an earlier build wrote) leaves **only** through
     a successful adoption into the orphan record. **Audit of every live operation on a file it did
     not create:** `enqueued` and `processed` touch only this process's journal; `recordUnqueued`
     rewrites the orphan record as a union (nothing leaves); `orphansHandled` now removes **only the
     keys it was handed and resolved**, so a key recorded since (a written save that could not be
     journalled) is not dropped with them; the adoption removes a dead journal only after the orphan
     record holds its keys; the cutover deletes only the directories it renamed itself.

#### B.20.15 Fix round 7 (Codex on `5f7a4b782`)

395. ⚠⚠ **The lane path answers what it wrote.** The consumer's lane branch answered `true` whatever
     `stageIntoLane` had done. Its unopened-lane fallback (every L2 op's `taskId` arrives as a lane
     id nobody opened) is the ordinary per-save path. When a sibling locked the realm between enqueue
     and consume, that path queued nothing and said so, the answer was thrown away, and the save's
     record was released with nothing queued. The answer is now an `EmitHandoff` (`Queued` /
     `NotQueued(why)`, `sync-service-proxy/.../EmitHandoff.kt`), not a `Boolean`, and every lane path
     returns its own:
     - the unopened fallback returns `processSavedData`'s answer;
     - an opened lane's shared-realm / no-hash fallback returns `generateSyncBlock`'s;
     - an opened lane's journal row is `Queued` only once `addToArray` has returned. A failed write
       throws, and the consumer's catch keeps the record.
     ⚠⚠ The journal row is a real handoff only if nothing drops it unsealed, and two paths did: the
     checkpoint and the D6 replay removed the journal whether or not `sealBatch` had a realm to seal
     in. Both now remove it only on `Queued`. A replay that sealed some chunks before the realm went
     keeps the whole journal and seals it again (receivers skip equal-HLC deltas).
396. **Audit: every producer and consumer of the "queued" answer.**
     - The `EmitEvent.Saved` consumer is the only place a record is released. It does so in an
       exhaustive `when` over the handoff.
     - `stageIntoLane` → `processSavedData` | `stageDelta`*, combined with `and`.
     - `stageDelta` → `generateSyncBlock` | the journal row.
     - `processSavedData` → `generateSyncBlock` (entity + each `Syncable` property), combined with `and`.
     - `sealBatch` → its two callers above.
     - `emitPropertyBlock` is the one caller that does not return it. Its `SyncBlockEmitter` contract
       is best-effort (no realm is a silent no-op, and no save record rides on it), so a `NotQueued`
       is logged there.
     - The `trySend` results at the three `EmitEvent.Saved` producers (`onSaved`, the orphan
       re-emit, the locked-hold replay) are still unchecked, and that is safe: the key is recorded
       before the send, and only the consumer releases it, so a send that fails leaves it recorded.
     - The content-plane `Boolean`s (`emitFileContent*`, `ensureTargetHeld`) carry no save record and
       are out of scope.
     ⚠ The compiler is **not** what enforces this. `-Xreturn-value-checker=check` with
     `RETURN_VALUE_NOT_USED:error` and `@file:MustUseReturnValues` on `SyncObserver.kt` does catch a
     dropped `processSavedData` (probed). But it is module-wide, and it also flags the module's
     existing stdlib discards (`getOrPut`, `runCatching`, `addAndFetch`) and test code in every
     source set, about 20 unrelated sites, so it was not kept. It is a follow-up.

#### B.20.16 Final round (independent review on `9587aa67a`): the cheap fixes, and the switch-on gates

The review found the PR mergeable with the switch at NO. The fixes below are cheap and were made
now. The gates in 401–406 are not built: each one has to be closed before any build turns the store
on, alongside (378).

397. ⚠⚠ **A durable read is told apart in its own function.** `countOneShots` (`OutboundBacklog.kt`)
     and the orphan re-emit (`SyncObserver`) each had `val row = try { readDurable } catch {
     Unreadable(..) }` followed by a `when`/`is` over `row` in the same function. That is the K/N
     shape that segfaults on iOS: a value merged from an inline try is typed by its default's
     concrete class, so `is Unreadable` answers yes for `Absent`/`Present`, and reading `.reason`
     crashes (memory knative-typetest-after-inline-try-default). Each try is now its own function
     returning `DurableRow` (`durableOrUnreadable`). A grep of the PR's whole Kotlin diff for
     inline `try`/`runCatching`/`getOrDefault` values found no other type-tested in place:
     - `OutboundBacklog`'s queue count tests inside the try, on the call's own value;
     - the re-emit's `getData` read is only null-tested;
     - `cutOver`'s `Outcome` is returned, so it is tested in another function;
     - the `FileEmitBacklogMarker` reads are lists.
     ⚠ **Where these paths actually run on K/N.** `:sync-service-proxy:iosSimulatorArm64Test`
     compiles and runs nothing: the root `build.gradle.kts` disables every `-proxy` module's iOS
     tests. `countOneShots` runs on the simulator through `ControlSharedReplicaTest`'s
     `attemptCutover` cases (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`), with the schedule list absent and present. The
     orphan re-emit ran on K/N in no suite until `OrphanReEmitOnNativeTest` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`,
     new), which drives it with one `Absent` and one `Present` key.
398. ⚠⚠ **The cheap check comes before the stop and before the scan.** `attemptCutover` asked
     `outsideTheStore()` only inside `cutOver`, after stopping Control's graph. A `.orphaned` record,
     which only a later launch of that app can clear, therefore cost a stop, an exhaustive scan of
     every blob under the `flock`, a refusal and a rebuild on every 15 s tick, for as long as the
     record stayed. Step 1 now asks it too, and any reason ends the attempt with the graph untouched.
     `commitUnderLock` evaluates it first and runs the scan only when it is empty (`ifEmpty`, not `+`).
399. **The refusal says what helps.** A `.orphaned` record is cleared by a new process of that app,
     whose launch adopts it, never by bringing a suspended one forward. The message now says
     "force-quit it if it is still in the background, then open it again".
400. **A failed journal removal is logged.** `FileEmitBacklogMarker.processed` ignored
     `removeItemAtPath`'s answer, and so did the dead-journal removal after adoption and the resolved
     orphan record's removal. Keeping the file is the safe direction each time: it still counts, or
     it is adopted or handed out again. Each now logs when the file stays.

**Hard gates for switch-on** (beside (378); none of them is built):

401. ⚠⚠ **The exhaustive scan's cost under the cross-process `flock`.** The final look enumerates
     every row (`refreshIndex`, then every `tenshu/core/list`), and the measured phone has about 106k
     blobs. While it runs, every sibling's write waits on the `flock`. That risks a sibling's launch
     watchdog (an app whose first store write is in launch) and freezes a Split View sibling. The
     gate: the scan's wall time on the measured phone, and either a bound that keeps it under the
     watchdog margin or a scan that does not hold the `flock` throughout.
402. ⚠⚠ **A live process's stuck count.** A save whose block can never be queued (no realm, a
     queue write that keeps failing) keeps its key in that process's live journal, and the journal
     only grows (`+key` per save, `-key` per release) for the process's lifetime (review item 3).
     Nothing tells the user which app, and the cutover refuses for as long as the process lives. The
     gate: a bounded journal (compact on release), and the stuck key surfaced with its app.
403. ⚠⚠ **Keys no later process can rebuild refuse for good (Q58).** `u\t` (a row with no id),
     `h\t` (a hash alone) and any `DataId` that `dataIdOf` cannot parse back (e.g.
     `CompositeEntityDataId`) are kept by the orphan re-emit on every launch. The cutover then
     refuses forever, with no surface naming the cause. The gate: either every emitting `DataId`
     shape round-trips through `keyOf`/`dataIdOf` (pinned by a test over every shape), or such a key
     is resolved by a reconcile that does not need its row, and either way the refusal is surfaced.
404. **The no-realm lane.** An opened lane whose checkpoint finds no realm keeps its staged deltas
     in memory and its journal on disk (B.20.15 (395)). The memory grows with every save until the
     lane closes, and it logs on every checkpoint. The gate: a cap that spills to the journal alone,
     and logging once per lane.
405. ⚠⚠ **A fenced `SharedReplicaStore` answers `readDurable` from its fenced reads.** It does not
     override `readDurable`, so the default answers from `getObject`, which a fenced handle answers
     absent. Every "confirmed absence" rule (the orphan re-emit, the drain proof's member reads)
     would then let a record go, or count a queue as empty, on a store that simply cannot be read.
     The gate: an override that answers `Unreadable` (or throws) once fenced, plus a test.
     ⚠ **Moot, no override needed** (`readDurable` is deleted, `chore/remove-file-store-seams`). For
     the sweeper: a fenced handle reads every row absent, every write throws `ReplicaReplaced`
     (`requireServing`), and the fence never lifts. A pass that sees the fence re-reads each
     candidate as absent and skips it, and its cursor write throws, so it deletes nothing and
     leaves the cursor. Pinned by `aFenceBetweenTheScanAndTheKeepSetReadDeletesNothingAndLeavesTheCursor`.
     No other confirmed-absence consumer survives B.22.
406. ⚠ **`FileObjectStore.invalidateCached` mutates `present` outside the DB lock — denied, not
     always under it.** `outboundBacklogOf` runs inside `database.transaction` (under the lock). But
     `RetiredBlockSweeper.sweepOnce` calls the store directly, with no transaction:
     `invalidateCached` (since B.20.9 (370) it also mutates `present`), `scanRowsOfType` and
     `readRaw`'s drop. It runs on its own loop in Control's iOS `PlatformProxyModule`, concurrently
     with the graph's locked writes, so `present` (a plain `MutableSet`) and `cache` race. This is
     not cheap to fix: the choice is between holding the `flock` across a sweep page and making the
     store's index thread-safe, and it touches the unswitched production path. Recorded, not fixed.
     The gate: the sweeper's store access under the DB lock, or a locked index, with a concurrent
     test over `FileObjectStore`.
407. ⚠⚠ **The sweeper's keep-set is read under the DatabaseLock (a regression of B.20.10, fixed).**
     Master read `RetiredBlockSweeper`'s queues through `database.getArrayData`, which takes the
     lock. Fix round 2 replaced that with a direct `store.readDurable`, and `FileObjectStore.readDurable`
     mutates `present`. So the PR had added an unlocked `present` mutation that raced ordinary saves
     on today's unswitched iOS Control, whose maintenance hook runs `sweepOnce` bare. The keep-set's
     `invalidateCached` and `readDurable` calls now run inside one `database.transaction`, and only
     those few rows, never the page's scan. Pinned by `theKeepSetIsReadUnderTheDatabaseLock`
     (`RetiredBlockSweeperTest`: a lock double counts its depth, and the store counts keep-set
     reads made outside it). Mutation: the transaction removed → red. The rest of `sweepOnce`
     (cursor load/store, `scanRowsOfType`) was unlocked before B.20 too, and 406 and
     `tech-debt.md` record it.
408. ⚠⚠ **A pass whose keep-set cannot be read leaves the cursor (Codex P2, a regression of B.20.10).**
     Fix round 2 made the keep-set answer null on an unreadable queue row ("unknown is not empty"),
     but `sweepOnce` had already persisted the next cursor, or `SWEEP_COMPLETE` on the last page.
     So the page was skipped for good, and after a completion it was never retried. The keep-set
     and the `blockId` index are now read first, and the cursor advances (`advancePast`) only once
     the page is processed. An empty page still advances at once, as before. Pinned by
     `anUnreadableKeepSetOnTheLastPageLeavesTheCursorAndTheNextPassSweepsIt`: on the last page, the
     cursor is unchanged and the orphan kept; once the queue is readable, the next pass deletes it
     and writes `SWEEP_COMPLETE`. Mutation: the old order restored → red.

### B.21 S0b-4 slice 2: D3 and D3b, Appendix A landed, and the switch (2026-11-01)

> ⚠⚠ **The switch decision (369) and Q62/Q63 are superseded by B.22 (2026-11-05)**: no switch, no
> relay guard, on in every build. D3/D3b stand; (414), `sync-hlc/` at rest, is done in B.22.

**What it is.** The rest of S0b-4 but the device steps: `replica/`'s protection class and backup
exclusion (D3), the same two on `files/` and `upload-staging/` (D3b), Appendix A's threat-model
amendment **as built** (House Rule 2), and the decision on the switch. On slice 1 (B.20, merged
with its fix rounds B.20.9–B.20.16).

#### B.21.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `ContainerAtRest` | makes a directory, sets `NSFileProtectionCompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication` on it and on each listed file that exists, sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` on it, and **reads both back** (the exclusion from a fresh `NSURL`); `NotProtectedAtRest` names what did not hold | `core-common/src/iosMain/.../ContainerAtRest.kt` |
| D3 | the production `SharedReplicaStore.open` protects `replica/`, `objects.db`, `-wal` and `-shm` **at every open**, after the registry's protection check and before the opener; a failure is `ReplicaNotProtected`, a `StoreUnavailable` (retryable "not ready", the stand-in, "Try again"); skipped before the first unlock, where the open's own `ProtectedDataUnavailable` answers | `SharedReplicaStore.kt`, `ReplicaVerdicts.kt` |
| D3b | the binding protects `files/` and `upload-staging/` at every open of a switched process, best effort (logged, retried at the next open), never a refusal of the store | `SharedReplicaBinding.openOnce` |
| Appendix A | landed in `threat-model.md`: A5, T-C-04, T-T-08, T-C-09, **amended to what is built** (B.21.2 (365)) | `docs/sync/threat-model.md` |

#### B.21.2 Decisions made in implementation, for review

365. ⚠⚠ **Appendix A as built, not as drafted.** Two of its sentences describe what is not built and
     would have made the threat model claim it: T-T-08's watermark "in the shared replica's
     database, bound to the `(ownerId, deviceId)`, with identity-bound per-app copies in the shared
     Keychain group" (§5.4) — the binding still uses the `sync-hlc/` file (B.13.2) — and its "kept
     across deleting every app". The landed T-T-08 text says what is true: the watermark is still
     `sync-hlc/`; the cutover removes it with the old store in one commit; residual (1) the initial
     cutover's `DIVERGENCE`; residual (2) unchanged from TC-2b (a wipe of the SQLite store does not
     reset it); §5.4 owes its own amendment. A5 and T-C-04 say "on a build with the shared store
     switched on", because an unswitched build still runs the file store with the container's
     defaults, and T-C-04 records that gap as still open there. A5 adds the cutover's drain proof.
     ⚠ Rebased onto as-built slice 1 (2026-11-04): A5's proof now names what B.20.9–B.20.16 made it
     read beside the queues (every app's saves not yet queued, staged uploads, unsent content) and
     the cutover-done mark, and it states that the proof cannot see an old-build sibling (378), so
     no build may switch on until 378 and 401–406 are closed.
366. **Strict for `replica/`, best effort for `files/` and `upload-staging/`.** The store is not handed
     out without its flags: the threat model now says "asserted at every open", and a store that
     could be restored from a backup is the orphaned-identity class (§2.4). The other two are not the
     store: refusing the store because `upload-staging/` could not be flagged would stop the app for
     a cache directory, so a failure is logged and tried again at the next open.
367. **The class is read back only where the platform reports one.** The simulator's file system has
     no Data Protection and reports no class; that is accepted on the simulator and **refused on a
     device** (`IS_IOS_DEVICE_BUILD`). Whether files SQLite creates after the directory is set take its
     class is *GK*: each open sets the class on `objects.db`, `-wal` and `-shm` explicitly anyway, and
     the phone pass reads them back (Q0 (h)).
368. **Before the first unlock nothing is set.** `setAttributes` cannot answer then; the open decides
     by its own protected-data rule, as before this slice (its `ProtectedDataUnavailable` and Q42's
     retry), and the flags are set at the next open that finds protected data available.
369. ⚠⚠ **The switch: not flipped, and the doc never asked for it.** §13's S0b-4 is "§8's steps on the
     phone", run by the maintainer on builds made with the switch on; nothing in §8 or §13 turns it on
     for shipped builds, and the maintainer's 2026-11-01 decision keeps the file store (and its code)
     until after Control 1.0's App Store approval. So after S0b-4:
     - **every build is on the file store unless it is built with `TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE=YES`**
       (`xcodebuild … TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE=YES`, per build, per app; all ten from one commit,
       §8 step 2), **and** its relay is the dev lab's (B.13 (180)): only debug binaries honour
       `TENSHU_DEV_RELAY`, so **no Release build (TestFlight, App Store) binds the SQLite store**,
       whatever its plist says;
     - the in-review Control 1.0 is an uploaded archive and is not changed by any commit.
     ⚠⚠ And before **any** build turns the switch on, slice 1's switch-on gates must be closed: (378)'s
     old-build sibling with no fence and no marker, and B.20.16 (401–406): the exhaustive scan's cost
     under the `flock`, a stuck live count, unrebuildable keys, the no-realm lane, a fenced store's
     `readDurable`, and the sweeper's unlocked index. Slice 2 closes none of them.
     ⚠ That means the S0b-4 phone pass **on the real realm** (the maintainer's phone, production relay)

#### B.21.6 Fix round 1 (the independent review on `e454ba95a`)

410. ⚠⚠ **D3/D3b are not gated on `isProtectedDataAvailable` (S1, House Rule 2).** Both were gated on
     it, and it is false whenever the phone is **locked**, not only before the first unlock. So a
     Timeline location wake or a `BGTask` on a locked phone created `replica/` and `objects.db` with
     no class and no exclusion, and iCloud backup runs exactly then. That contradicted A5 and T-C-04
     ("at every open, never handed out without it"). The code is fixed, not the text:
     - `ContainerAtRest.protect` now sets and reads back the exclusion at **every** call, since it
       needs no protected data.
     - It sets and reads back the class whenever the class keys exist: `isProtectedDataAvailable`,
       **or** a first-unlock signal (`classKeysAvailable`). The signal writes and reads back a small
       `CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication` probe file (`.at-rest-probe`) in the container, beside
       the directory and never inside it. That class is readable while locked after the first unlock
       and never before it.
     - Only before the first unlock is anything deferred (`Outcome.DEFERRED_UNTIL_FIRST_UNLOCK`):
       nothing is refused, an exclusion failure is logged, and the open decides by its own
       protected-data rule, as before.
     - D3 (`SharedReplicaStore.open`) and D3b (`SharedReplicaBinding.openOnce`) both call it at every
       open now.
411. **L3: a `-wal`/`-shm` that vanishes between the existence check and the set is absent**, not a
     refusal: a checkpoint or a sibling removed it, and existence is re-checked on a failed set.
412. ⚠ **L2: a directory that reports no class on a device is accepted on its files' class, with a
     log line.** Otherwise, if devices do not report `NSFileProtectionKey` on a directory, a permanent
     `ReplicaNotProtected` would brick every app. A *file* reporting none on a device is still
     refused. Whether a device reports a class on a directory is unknown until B.21.5 item 1. The
     simulator test that accepts null is vacuous there (no Data Protection), and says so.
413. **L4:** `upload-staging` is `LegacyFileStoreCutover.UPLOAD_STAGING`, no longer a literal. The
     directory is made `0700`, as `ReplicaFiles` makes its own, with the class at creation when the
     keys exist; a directory that could not be made is a refusal.
414. **L5: what D3/D3b do not cover.** Both are outside, and T-C-04 lists them:
     - `sync-hlc/`, the HLC watermark, one stamp and no user data. It keeps the container's defaults
       and goes to backup. A restore beside a re-pulling replica is T-T-08's residual (2) direction
       (the tip over-states what the store has applied), which is **not** OK as a design end state.
       Owed with the switch-on: the same two flags on `sync-hlc/`.
     - `replica-legacy.retired/` and `replica-legacy.removing-*`, the old file store on its way out.
       It is transient, removed right after the commit, and carries the unswitched build's gap
       (T-C-04) for as long as it exists.

| Fix | Test | Mutation | Red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 410 | `aLockedPhoneAfterTheFirstUnlockStillGetsBothFlags` (`ContainerAtRestTest`); `aLockedOpenAfterTheFirstUnlockSetsTheClassAndTheExclusion` (`SharedReplicaBindingSurfaceTest`, the production open with `protectedDataAvailable = false`) | P1: the class gated on `protectedDataAvailable()` alone again | ✓ (both) |
| 410 | `beforeTheFirstUnlockTheClassIsDeferredNotRefusedAndTheExclusionIsStillTried`; `beforeTheFirstUnlockNoClassIsSetAndTheOpenDecidesAsBefore` | P2: the exclusion skipped while deferred | ✓ (the first) |
| 411 | `aWalThatVanishesBetweenTheCheckAndTheSetCountsAsAbsent` | P3: no re-check on a failed set | ✓ |
| 412 | `aDirectoryThatReportsNoClassOnADeviceIsAcceptedOnItsFilesClassAndLogged` | P4: a directory's null refused on a device again | ✓ |

Each applied alone and restored, on the simulator. ⚠ D3b's own gate in `SharedReplicaBinding.openOnce`
(the removed `if (installed.protectedDataAvailable())`) has no test of its own: the binding's
fixture has no locked-adapter seam. It now passes the same `protectedDataAvailable` into the same
`ContainerAtRest.protect` that P1 pins.

### B.22 SQLite by default, and the old store reset at launch, not drained (2026-11-05)

**The decision (the maintainer, 2026-11-05).** No iOS build has reached a user. Control-iOS 1.0 was
rejected once and will be resubmitted, and the only phones that hold the old shared `FileObjectStore`
are the maintainer's own test phones, whose realm is test data. So **nothing has to be migrated**:

- every first-party iOS app and Control binds the SQLite store, in every build configuration and
  against any relay. There is no switch any more;
- an old file store found at launch is **reset**: deleted with no drain proof, and the app re-pulls
  from the relay into SQLite;
- S0b-4's drain-gated cutover (B.20; and its switch decision in B.21) is not needed.
  ⚠⚠ **Its code is deleted in a follow-up cleanup PR, not in this one** (B.22.4 lists what it owes;
  done, with the launch reset, in B.22.9).

#### B.22.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| No switch | `SharedReplicaSwitch` is gone (the plist key `TenshuSharedReplicaSqlite`, the build setting `TENSHU_SHARED_REPLICA_SQLITE` in all ten `project.yml`s, `isOn`, `allows`, the dev-lab guard `isDevLabRelay`). `SharedReplicaLocation.SUBDIRECTORY` is what is left. `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.sqliteBindingFor` makes the binding on every production assembly; Control's `isSwitched` and its `plistOn`/`relay` seams are gone; `sharedReplicaStoreModule` opens SQLite whatever the graph's relay | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt`, `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.kt`, `ControlSharedReplica.kt`, `ControlSurface.kt`, `*-ios/project.yml` |
| The reset | `LegacyFileStoreReset.resetIfPresent()`: renames under the writer `flock`, the delete in the background | `core-common/src/iosMain/.../LegacyFileStoreReset.kt` |
| Who runs it | every app's assembly (`sqliteBindingForAssembly`, before the choice is read) and Control's (`runtimeModule`, before the binding is installed) | `FirstPartyLocalRuntime.kt`, `ControlSharedReplica.kt` |
| Control's choice | a `files` or "file store written since" reading no longer keeps Control on the file store: it declares `reset`, binds SQLite, then declares `sqlite` once bound (B.14 (190)'s protocol otherwise unchanged) | `ControlSharedReplica.runtimeModule` |
| `sync-hlc/` at rest | the watermark joins D3b: class and backup exclusion, read back, at every open (B.21.6 (414)) | `SharedReplicaBinding.contentDirectories` |
| The no-realm lane | capped (B.20.16 (404)) | `SyncObserver` (`Lane.spilled`, `spill`) |
| `FileAdvisoryLock.open` | one `open(O_RDWR \| O_CREAT)` (B.20.3 (364), fixed) | `FileAdvisoryLock.kt` |

#### B.22.2 Decisions made in implementation, for review

415. ⚠⚠ **What the reset removes, and why each.**
     - `objects/`, the file store. Its pull, tombstone and back-fill cursors and its first-pull marker
       are rows in it (A1, `SyncManagerImpl.lastSyncTimestamp`), so the re-pull starts at cursor 0 with
       nothing else to clear. No cursor or checkpoint of the replica lives outside it: the Keychain
       slots are the realm identity and realm-level latches (`REALM_RELAY_REGISTERED`,
       `JOINED_FUNDED_REALM`, `CONTENT_DESCRIBED_FROM_GENESIS`), which the reset must keep, exactly as
       B.20's cutover kept them.
     - `sync-hlc/`, the HLC watermark (TC-2b), **only beside an old store** (`objects/`, or S0b-4's
       `replica-legacy.retired/`). Kept, it would over-state what the new store holds and forge the
       relay's tombstone-GC acknowledgement (B.20.3 (358), T-T-08). ⚠⚠ Alone, it is the SQLite
       store's live watermark (B.20.9's B1) and is never touched.
     - What S0b-4's cutover may have left: `replica-legacy.retired/`, every `replica-legacy.removing-*`,
       and `replica-emit-pending/` (the saves-not-yet-queued records, which only a process on the file
       store writes: they name rows of the old store).
416. ⚠ **What stays, and why it is valid for the new store.**
     - `files/`: content keyed by content id. A re-pulled row names the same id, so its bytes are
       reused; an id no row names is never read. Its `.unsent-content/` markers only stop an overwrite
       with the same bytes from being a no-op (`UploadFileImplementation.heldContentId`), the safe
       direction.
     - `upload-staging/`: sealed chunks, each PUT by its content ref with a JWT minted per enqueue from
       the realm identity, which the reset keeps. Finishing them is right whatever the store holds,
       and a chunk whose row the reset lost (a row never pushed) is an unreferenced blob the relay's
       sweep reclaims.
     - `replica/`, `replica.choice`, `replica.writer.lock`, and `replica-legacy.cutover-done` (written
       by the reset too, (417)).
417. ⚠⚠ **The order, and why every kill resumes.** Under the writer `flock`, once the trigger is seen
     again under it: the cutover-done mark first (so even a reset that fails part-way keeps any
     follower off a file store, B.20's follower check), a unique `replica-legacy.removing-<random>`
     made, then renamed into it: `sync-hlc/` (when it is the old store's), the leftovers, and
     `objects/` **last**. The commit point is `objects/` gone. A kill before it leaves `objects/`, which
     the next launch resets again; at no kill point is the old watermark left beside no old store
     (`aResetKilledAfterEveryStep…`). The delete of every `removing-*` runs after the lock, off the
     calling thread, and is started again by every call, so one killed mid-delete is finished at the
     next launch.
418. ⚠⚠ **Renames at launch, deletes in the background.** A wipe at launch has blown iOS's 20 s
     watchdog before (memory "wipe blows 20s watchdog"). The launch does a few `stat`s when there is
     nothing to reset, and a handful of `rename(2)`s under the `flock` when there is; the bulk delete
     goes to a low-priority GCD queue. It holds no lock while it deletes, so a suspension mid-delete is
     not the `0xdead10cc` class.
419. **Every app resets, not only Control.** The cutover was Control's because only Control could
     prove the drain; a reset proves nothing, so whichever process launches first does it. The
     writer `flock` makes two launches at once reset once (`twoAppsLaunchingAtOnce…`). An app that
     resets still waits for Control's declaration (B.14 (190)) before it binds, unchanged.
420. **Control binds SQLite whatever the choice reads.** A `files` or "file store written since"
     reading is a leftover of S0b-4's drain or of an old build. Control declares `reset` first (the apps
     wait on their stand-in, and Control's own foreground re-read keeps it chosen), then `sqlite` once
     its store is bound. Control's fence when the file store is written while it runs (B.14 (196)) is
     kept: an old build writing `objects/` stops Control's graph, and the rebuild's assembly resets it.
421. ⚠ *Superseded by (432) in fix round 1: the branch below was still reachable (Control's install
     fallback); it is now removed from the decision, and its code is dead.* **The follower path is unreachable, not deleted.** After an app's own reset `objects/` is
     gone and the cutover-done mark is written, so `sqliteBindingForAssembly`'s "join the file store"
     branch can no longer be taken, and Control's `cutoverAtLaunch`, drain watcher and
     `attemptCutover` are never reached. They and their tests stay until the cleanup PR (B.22.4); the
     tests that exercise them build Control's drain graph directly (`fileStoreForCutoverModule`, now
     `internal` for that) or set the app's reset seam to a no-op, and say so. `theDrainWatcherDoesNothingInTheBackground`
     is deleted: nothing can start the watcher.
422. ⚠ *Superseded by (432): it now binds the stand-in.* **A binding that cannot be installed still leaves Control on the file store** (an app extension,
     `installAtLaunch` throwing; B.14). Unchanged here, because it is the fallback the cleanup PR
     removes with the file store. Its `objects/` is reset at the next launch.
423. **(414) done: `sync-hlc/` excluded from backup.** It is the third of D3b's directories, with the
     same class (`CompleteUntilFirstUserAuthentication`, which a locked background wake can still
     read) and the exclusion read back from a fresh `NSURL`, at every open, best effort (logged and
     retried, never a refusal of the store, like D3b). ⚠ The directory is made by D3b at the open
     when it is missing, before any raise; a raise that makes it again between opens (after a reset
     removed it) is flagged at the next open.
424. **(404) done: the no-realm lane is capped.** A checkpoint that finds no realm to seal in now
     *spills* the lane: its in-memory deltas are dropped (each is already a journal row, its only
     durable copy), every later save of the lane is journalled alone, and the miss is logged once for
     the lane. A spilled lane's next checkpoint or close, once a realm is there, runs the D6 replay,
     which seals the whole journal (and clears every lane, as the replay always did); with no realm it
     is silent. ⚠ The change is in `commonMain` (`SyncObserver`), so Android and desktop get it too:
     only that no-realm path behaves differently.
425. **(364) fixed: `FileAdvisoryLock.open` is one `open(O_RDWR | O_CREAT, 0644)`.** The reset can
     meet a missing lock file with two apps launching at once; the old "create, then open" handed the
     two different inodes.
426. **House Rule 9: no bump.** No stored row, composite or wire shape changes: the reset removes
     directories, the choice file keeps its format, and the lane change is in memory only.

#### B.22.3 The switch-on gates are moot, and what of B.20/B.21 is done here

| Item | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| (378), Q61 | an old-build sibling has no fence and no saves record, so the drain proof cannot see it | ⚖ moot: there is no proof; an old build's writes to `objects/` are reset at the next launch (test data) |
| (401) | the exhaustive scan under the `flock` | moot: no scan |
| (402), (403), Q58, Q60 | a stuck live count; keys no later process can rebuild; the drain is silent; a queue that never drains | moot: nothing waits on the drain |

| (406) | `FileObjectStore.invalidateCached` mutating `present` outside the DB lock | moot on iOS: no production process opens a `FileObjectStore` (except (422)'s fallback); the class goes in the cleanup |
| Q62 | lift the relay guard for debug binaries | done, for every build: the guard is gone |
| Q63 | `files/` and `upload-staging/` on an unswitched build | moot: there is no unswitched build |
| (404) | the no-realm lane | **done** here, (424) |
| (414) | `sync-hlc/` and backup | **done** here, (423) |
| (364) | `FileAdvisoryLock.open`'s race | **done** here, (425) |

so a press runs PR-5's foreground pass only. Nothing here changes it. ✅ *Resolved by B.23 (2026-11-05): a task's token; the decline is gone.*

  `FirstPartyLocalRuntime` (`switchedOnFileStore`, `fencedFileStoreLockModule`, `followerLock`,
  `fileStoreIdentityAtChoice`), with the tests B.22.2 (421) names.
- Then the legacy file store itself (B.20.6's list): `FileObjectStore`, `wipeFileObjectStore`,
  `readObjectStoreEntries`, `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock` and `FileStoreFence`, the two
  `as? FileObjectStore` downcasts, and (422)'s fallback. ⚠ `LegacyFileStoreReset` uses
  `FileAdvisoryLock` and the writer lock's path: keep both while the reset is kept, or retire the
  reset too once every test phone has run it.
- `HlcWatermarkFile` stays: it is the live watermark on SQLite until §5.4's `meta` copy is built.

#### B.22.6 Fix round 1 (Codex P1 and the independent review)

Each claim was checked against the code before it was fixed.

427. ⚠⚠ **(A, Codex P1, verified) A reset that does not complete never binds SQLite.** Both callers
     ignored `resetIfPresent()`'s answer. A reset that failed before `sync-hlc/` moved (a `stat` that
     could not be answered, a rename refused) bound the SQLite store beside the old store's watermark.
     A `FAILED` now puts that assembly on the **retryable not-ready stand-in**, never the file store and
     never SQLite. The host rebuilds it at the next foreground or entry, whose assembly tries the reset
     again. Control uses `ControlSharedReplica.runtimeModule`, the apps `sqliteBindingForAssembly` with
     its own reason.
428. ⚠⚠ **(E, verified) The reset's `flock` is tried, never waited on.** It ran `flock(LOCK_EX)` on the
     launch's main thread with no bound, so a holder in another process (an older build mid-write, a
     suspended holder) would have cost the 20 s watchdog at every relaunch. The lock is now tried
     every 20 ms for at most `LOCK_WAIT_MS` (300 ms). Still busy past that is `FAILED`, handled by (427).
429. ⚠⚠ **(B, verified, and a pre-existing hazard for every joining device) The orphan sweep waits for
     the store's history.** `OrphanedFileSweeper` treats "an ancestor row is absent" as garbage and,
     on a realm member, removes the row **with a real tombstone**, which every device applies. It runs
     as a maintenance hook at the start of every tick, before the enabled guard and after the pages
     of earlier ticks. The pull does **not** deliver parents first:
     - the C2 backward walk (`SyncScheduler.backfillOnce`) applies the log **newest-first**, by design;
     - a file written into a folder has a higher `relay_seq` than the folder's creation, so it
       arrives first;
     - in the window until the walk reaches the folder, the sweep would tombstone a live file
       realm-wide.

     This is not specific to the reset. It holds for any device that joins a realm with history on
     a merged-lane relay (production), and for any store wiped to re-pull. Nothing in ingest creates
     a missing parent (searched).

     The fix is at that level, in the sweeper. A realm member (or an emitter not attached yet) sweeps
     only once `ObjectStore.hasPulledItsHistory()` holds:
     - the first-pull marker is `COMPLETED` (no marker with a forward cursor above zero is an
       upgraded store and counts);
     - **and** the backward walk is not mid-way (its floor is `null` or `0`).

     Unknown, or any other marker, is not complete. The check comes before the scan and before the
     cursor moves, so nothing is skipped later. A runtime without sync, or a device in no realm,
     sweeps as before.

     The predicate is one definition, `pulledHistoryComplete` (`:core-common`), which the scheduler
     uses too (430).

     ⚠ **Not closed:** in steady state, after the history is pulled, a forward page boundary that
     splits a folder's row from a child's is still possible in principle. That needs a move or a
     re-creation whose rows straddle two pages, the sweep's tick in between, and a missing ancestor at
     that moment. It is pre-existing, and recorded in `core-local-store-orphan-gc.md`.
430. ⚠⚠ **(C, verified) The watermark is trusted only once the store has pulled its history.** An
     older-build process still on the old store after the reset raises its `HlcWatermarkFile` and
     `ensureDirectory` makes `sync-hlc/` again with its high stamp. The next launch then sees a lone
     `sync-hlc/` and keeps it as the SQLite store's own.

     Two smaller options were rejected:
     - binding the file to the store by adjacency is exactly what failed here;
     - an owner/epoch stamp in the file would need the untestable `-proxy` adapter and a format.

     The fix is in `SyncScheduler.mergedHlc`, the one place the watermark reaches the relay: until
     `storeHistoryPulled()`, the signed tip is the process's own clock, and the watermark is neither
     read nor raised.

     Why this is enough: once the store has pulled the realm's history, it has applied every
     tombstone the relay holds, so no stamp in the file can over-state what it applied. The only
     stamps above the relay's own are those of writes the reset discarded, which name no tombstone.
     A deflated tip only stalls GC, the safe side.

     It is `commonMain`, so it holds on Android, desktop and web too, and it **closes T-T-08
     residual (2)** (a wiped store beside an un-reset watermark) everywhere.

     ⚠⚠ **The cost is more than a deflated tip** (fix round 2 (3)). While the history is being
     pulled, the tip is each process's own clock:
     - it can step **backwards** against tips this device already sent;
     - on iOS every route-1 app writes its own unrelated clock into the one `(ownerId, deviceId)`
       slot, which is exactly the TC-2b sawtooth (`sync-hlc-tip-device-identity.md` §1).

     So peers show this device as `DIVERGENCE` (the T-T-04 tell) for the **whole re-pull**, not once,
     and the relay's tombstone-GC quorum reads its lowest value meanwhile (GC stalls). Both end when
     the history is pulled. Accepted, because the alternative publishes a stamp the store never
     observed.
431. **(G) An old cutover's `replica-legacy.retired/` beside a live `sync-hlc/`.** The reset counts the
     watermark as the old store's when `retired/` is there, and so may remove SQLite's live one. That
     only under-states. With (430) a stamp is trusted only after a full pull anyway, so this is left
     as is.
432. ⚠⚠ **(D, verified) The file store is unreachable.** Three paths still led to it:
     - Control's `installAtLaunch`-throws fallback ran the file store and declared `files`;
     - an app reading `files` with no cutover-done mark then **joined** it, and its writes were reset
       at the next launch;
     - Control's foreground re-read declared `files` when it fenced.

     Now:
     - an app treats **any** reading but `sqlite` as "wait on the stand-in";
     - Control's install failure binds the stand-in (not retried by itself, relaunch) and declares
       nothing;
     - Control's `stillChosen` is always true and its `onUnchosen` is gone. Control is the declarer
       and never leaves SQLite; an older build's `objects/` is reset at the next launch, and the apps
       still fence on the "written since" reading.

     This **supersedes (421) and (422)**: no production path opens a `FileObjectStore`. The follower
     fields and `fencedFileStoreLockModule` are dead code for the cleanup PR, and so is the
     `FileEmitBacklogMarker.install` call in that branch.
433. **(F, verified) A replay keeps every open lane open.** `replayLaneJournalOnConsumer`'s
     `lanes.clear()` dropped every other open lane mid-task, so the rest of each task went one block
     per save, and a spilled lane never un-spilled. The replay now drops lane *state* only: each open
     lane is re-made fresh and un-spilled. A replay that cannot seal (still no realm) leaves the same
     fresh lanes, and the journal keeps everything. `commonMain`; only the replay's lane bookkeeping
     changes.
434. **(H) The runbook: update all ten apps from one build first.** `ios-drive-parity.md` §19.1 has
     the step. A mixed set loops, because an older build on the file store writes `objects/` and
     `sync-hlc/` again:
     - every new-build launch resets it, and Control's re-declaration fences the apps at their
       foreground;
     - an older build never fenced keeps writing into a store the next launch deletes.

| 428 | `aBusyWriterLockFailsFastAndTheNextLaunchResets` (iOS: the holder keeps it 2 s) | E1: the blocking `lock()` again | ✓ (`RESET` after the holder let go, not `FAILED`) |
