#### B.22.7 Fix round 2 (the independent re-review of `d24887f`)

435. ⚠⚠ **(1, verified) "No realm" is a shortcut only over a store that has never pulled.** The
     sweeper skipped the history check whenever its emitter's `residentOwnerId` was null. On iOS that
     owner is the *app's* own, null until it adopts Control's identity (a first launch, a sealed
     process). The store, though, is the shared replica, which Control may be re-pulling, so a
     not-yet-adopted app swept a half-pulled store with **silent** local deletes. The shortcut now
     also needs `ObjectStore.hasNeverPulled()`: no marker, both forward cursors at zero, and no
     backward-walk row. Otherwise the history rule applies.
436. ⚠⚠ **(2, verified, every platform) A backfill floor counts as pending only while this process
     walks it.** A floor above zero can be permanent:
     - a relay that lost the merged lane never advances it (`raiseBeforePull`'s own comment);
     - the walk's "did not descend" retry repeats as long as the relay answers that way.

     Read alone, it held the sweep and the watermark, and so the realm's tombstone GC, off with no
     limit.
     - `SyncScheduler.storeHistoryPulled()` now uses `raiseBeforePull`'s rule: the floor counts only
       while `mergedLaneSupported && mergedLaneWired()`.
     - The sweeper asks that function where it is registered (`historyPulled`, in all three
       `PlatformProxyModule`s); unwired, it keeps the store's stricter rule.
     - The watermark gate logs once per process while it holds.

     ⚠ **Not closed:** the "did not descend" loop with the lane still wired. There, history may
     really be missing (the WARN says so), so not trusting it is the honest answer; it is logged at
     every page.
437. **(3) The cost of (430) stated in full**, in (430) above and in T-T-08: a backward-stepping tip
     and the iOS per-app sawtooth for the whole re-pull, not only a deflated tip.
438. **(4, verified) Unknown marker means not pulled, in both readers.**
     `SyncManagerImpl.firstPullMarker` reads an unrecognised value as absent, so the scheduler fell
     through to "cursor moved, so upgraded, so pulled", and `raiseBeforePull` even latched it
     `COMPLETED`.
     - `SyncManager.firstPullMarkerUnrecognised` (default false) tells the two apart;
       `storeHistoryPulled` answers not pulled.
     - `raiseBeforePull` rewrites such a marker to `STARTED`, so the pull completes it as it would
       any first pull.
439. **(5, verified) Control heals a stale "written since" at its foreground.** Control's `sqlite`
     declaration records `objects/` when its store resolves, lazily and after the reset. An older
     build that made `objects/` in that gap, removed by a later reset, left the reading "written
     since" for good, and every app on the stand-in until Control relaunched. At each foreground,
     with no `objects/` left, Control declares `sqlite` again (its `stillChosen` hook). Declaring
     right after the reset instead was rejected: it cannot see a re-creation after the declaration,
     and it would let the apps bind before Control's own store had resolved.

|---|---|---|---|
| 435 | `anAppThatHasNotAdoptedYetNeverSweepsAStoreSomeoneIsStillPulling` (JVM: owner null, store `STARTED` / walking) | G1: the no-realm shortcut without `hasNeverPulled` | ✓ |
| 436 | `aBackfillFloorLeftByALostMergedLaneDoesNotHoldTheWatermarkForEver`, `theSchedulersAnswerDecidesWhereItIsWired` (JVM) | G2: the floor counted whatever the lane; G3: the sweeper ignores `historyPulled` | G2 ✓, G3 ✓ |
| 438 | `aStoreStillPullingItsHistory…`'s "an unknown marker" case (JVM, through the scheduler) | G4: `storeHistoryPulled` ignores the flag; G5: `raiseBeforePull` latches it `COMPLETED` | G4 ✓, G5 ✓ (the stamp adopted) |
| 439 | `controlHealsAStaleWrittenSinceDeclarationAtItsForeground` (iOS) | G6: no heal | ✓ |

#### B.22.8 The S0b cleanup: what B.22 made unreachable, deleted (2026-11-05)

A pure deletion: no behaviour changes on any platform. For each symbol, every source set (common,
iOS, JVM, Android, JS) and the Swift sources were searched for callers before it went.

**Deleted:**
- `LegacyFileStoreCutover` (`:core-common` iosMain) and `LegacyFileStoreCutoverTest`, with
  `directoryIdentity`.
- `OutboundBacklog` / `outboundBacklog` (`:sync-service-proxy` commonMain) and `OutboundBacklogTest`.
  Its one caller was `ControlSharedReplica.attemptCutover`.
- The saves-not-yet-queued record: `FileEmitBacklogMarker` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`) and its
  `EmitBacklogMarker` seam (`:sync-service-proxy` commonMain), with `EmitBacklogUnrecorded`.
  - In `SyncObserver`: `prepareSave`'s marking, `MarkedSave`, `markKeyOf`, `journalWrittenSave`,
    `emitsBlocks`, the orphan re-emit (`reemitOrphanedSaves`, `durableOrUnreadable`), and the
    `markKey` of `EmitEvent.Saved` and `HeldSave`.
  - Why this is no behaviour change: `EmitBacklogMarker.current` was set only by
    `FileEmitBacklogMarker.install`. On master (after B.22), `install` was referenced only as the
    default of `ControlSharedReplica`'s `installEmitMarker` seam, and nothing invoked that seam: the
    drain path that called it was already unreachable, and no app path called `install` (the
    follower's call went with B.22.6's fix round 1 (D)). So `current` was null in every process on
    every platform, and every use was a null-safe no-op.
  - Tests: `OrphanReEmitOnNativeTest` and `EmitBacklogMarkerTest`'s marker tests went. Its three
    lane tests moved to `SyncLaneNoRealmTest`, without the marker. The two direct tests of
    `FileObjectStore.readDurable` / `invalidateCached` that lived in `LegacyFileStoreCutoverTest`
    (`aRowASiblingCreatedIsSeenAfterInvalidateCachedAndByReadDurable`,
    `aRowThatIsThereButDoesNotDecodeIsUnreadableNeverAbsent`) moved to
    `FileObjectStoreDurableReadTest`: `RetiredBlockSweeper`'s keep-set still relies on that read.
- `ControlSharedReplica`'s cutover half: `cutoverAtLaunch`, `committed`, `fileStoreForCutoverModule`,
  the drain watcher, `attemptCutover`, `backlogOf`, `cutoverStatus`, `LegacyCutoverStatus`,
  `isApplicationActive`, and the seams `legacy`, `inForeground`, `drainPollMs`, `installEmitMarker`
  and `fileStoreFallbackDirectory`.
  - `legacyReset` now defaults over a `containerRoot` seam.
  - Tests: the drain and marker tests of `ControlSharedReplicaTest`.
- `FirstPartyLocalRuntime`'s follower half: `switchedOnFileStore`, `fileStoreIdentityAtChoice`,
  `followerLock`, `legacyCutover` and `fencedFileStoreLockModule`.
- `FileStoreFence`, `FileStoreRetired`, `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock`'s `fence` / `fencedBy`, the
  `guard` of `HlcWatermarkFile` and `IosSharedHlcWatermarkStore`, and the iOS
  `PlatformProxyModule`'s `getOrNull<FileStoreFence>()`.
  - Why this is no behaviour change: nothing bound a fence once the two fenced modules went, so the
    guard was always null.
- From `ObjectStore` and `FileObjectStore`: `refreshIndex`, `unreadableRowsSeen` and
  `StoreIndexUnreadable`, the drain proof's exhaustive scan. Also `fileStoreIdentity`,
  `FILE_STORE_ABSENT`, `pathExistsStrictly` and `listDirectoryStrictly`.

**Kept, and why:**
- **`FileObjectStore`, `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock`, `openFileObjectStore`, `wipeFileObjectStore`,
  `readObjectStoreEntries`: still reached.**
  - Production: the iOS `PlatformProxyModule` still binds the file store and its writer lock as the
    *default* `ObjectStore` / `DatabaseLock`, which `sharedReplicaStoreModule` overrides last-wins.
  - `AppGroupProbe` uses it (deleted 2026-11-05), and Control's forget wipes `objects/` with `wipeFileObjectStore`.
  - Every app module's iOS tests assemble over a test replica directory, which is a `FileObjectStore`.
  - Deleting it means re-pointing those defaults and every test fixture: a design change, not a
    deletion.
- **The two `as? FileObjectStore` downcasts** (`FirstPartyLocalRuntime.rehydrate`,
  `ControlSurface.rehydrateSharedReplica`).
  - They are called from all ten apps' Swift.
  - They answer -1 on the SQLite store, and they refresh a test replica's `FileObjectStore`, which
    `DriveLocalRuntimeTest` and others pin.
  - Removing them changes a Swift-visible API across ten apps.
- `LegacyFileStoreReset` and what it uses: `FileAdvisoryLock`, the writer lock's path, and the
  cutover-done mark (it still writes it first, so a reset that fails part-way leaves the same mark
  as before).
- `HlcWatermarkFile`, D3/D3b (`ContainerAtRest`), the history-pulled gates of B.22.6/B.22.7, and
  `EmitHandoff`. The lane's checkpoint and replay still keep the journal on `NotQueued`, and a
  spilled lane is told by it.
- `ObjectStore.readDurable` / `DurableRow` and `invalidateCached`: `RetiredBlockSweeper`'s keep-set
  reads them. ⚠ Since deleted (`chore/remove-file-store-seams`): no live store overrode either, so
  the keep-set is a plain `getObject` of each queue row, still under the DatabaseLock.

**House Rule 9:** no bump. No stored row, composite, wire type or `TConstant` was removed. The
marker's journal files and the drain proof never were schema types.

#### B.22.9 The 1.0.1 re-cut: the file store and the launch reset deleted too (2026-11-05)

⚠ Supersedes B.22.8's "kept" items: `FileObjectStore`, `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock`, the two downcasts
and the launch reset are gone. Parts of the list below repeat what B.22.8 had already deleted.

**The decision (the maintainer, 2026-11-05).** The release is re-cut: every test phone is cleared or
reinstalled at the operational reset, and all apps ship again together as 1.0.1. So no phone will
ever hold `objects/` again, and B.22.4 is done in full, **the launch reset included** (B.22.4's
"retire the reset too once every test phone has run it").

**Deleted.**
- `:core-common` iOS: `FileObjectStore` (with `openFileObjectStore`, `wipeFileObjectStore`,
  `readObjectStoreEntries`, `StoreIndexUnreadable`), `LegacyFileStoreCutover`, `LegacyFileStoreReset`,
  `LegacyAppLocalReplica` (`reclaimLegacyAppLocalReplica`: the pre-App-Group app-local replica, an
  older on-disk layout too), `SharedReplicaDatabaseLock`, `FileStoreFence`, `FileStoreRetired`,
  `sharedReplicaWriterLockPath`, `HlcWatermarkFile`'s fenced `guard`; and their eight iOS test classes.
  `ObjectStore.refreshIndex` and `unreadableRowsSeen` (S0b-4's, nothing else called them).
- `:sync-service-proxy`: `OutboundBacklog`, the `EmitBacklogMarker` seam (nothing else held it) and
  `SyncObserver`'s marker half (the counted save, the orphan re-emit). `EmitHandoff` stays: the lane
  path keeps its journal on it. The two lane tests of `EmitBacklogMarkerTest` live on as
  `SyncLaneNoRealmTest`.
- `:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`: `FileEmitBacklogMarker`; `ControlSharedReplica`'s cutover, drain watcher,
  `attemptCutover`, `cutoverStatus`, `LegacyCutoverStatus`, launch reset, `healDeclaration` (fix round
  2 (5)) and `liveFileStoreToWipe`; `FirstPartyLocalRuntime`'s follower path, launch reset and
  `rehydrate`; `AppGroupProbe`'s file-store probes (`objectStoreBlobCount`, `readReplicaEntries`,
  `writeReplicaProbeEntry`, `acquireWriterLock`).
- The two `as? FileObjectStore` downcasts, and with them every app's `rehydrateSharedReplica()` and its
  Swift foreground calls (nine apps and Control): on SQLite they answered `-1` and did nothing. Photos
  keeps its foreground hook as `checkAtForeground()` (the inference stamp's second check point).
  Control's `wipeLocalObjectStore` (the file store's store-less wipe in the forget) is gone: the D3
  wipe is `wipeThenPurgeCustody`'s. The Swift harness routes over the file store (`-replicaRead`,
  `-replicaWrite`, `-replicaReadProbe`, `-holdWriterLock`) went with it.
- The replica choice's file-store half: `files`, "file store written since" and the recorded
  `objects/` state. ⚠ The protocol between Control and the apps is unchanged: Control declares `sqlite`
  once its store resolved and `reset` at its forget, and an app binds only on `sqlite`. A line an
  older build wrote reads by its first word.
- `OrphanedFileSweeper.IOS_EXAMINE_PAGE`: the file store's measured examine budget. SQLite's type
  index makes the examine budget moot (as on `SqliteObjectStore`).

**What stays, and why.**
- `HlcWatermarkFile` and `FileAdvisoryLock`: the live watermark on SQLite (until §5.4's `meta` copy),
  and the lock it and the C4d/C4e-3b probes use.
- `InMemoryStoreMigration`, `StoreVersionGate`: the JS `IndexedDbObjectStore` still uses both.
- `ObjectStore.readDurable` and `invalidateCached`: `RetiredBlockSweeper` uses both. ⚠ Since deleted,
  with `Database.readDurable` (`chore/remove-file-store-seams`).

**What replaced what.**
- The iOS platform module binds **no** usable store: its `ObjectStore` fails loudly and its
  `DatabaseLock` is the new `InProcessDatabaseLock` (an `NSRecursiveLock`), both overridden in every
  production graph by `sharedReplicaStoreModule`. A graph without that module is a defect, not a
  non-durable store.
- A test's `replicaDirectory` binds `TestReplicas` (`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`): one row set per name in
  the process, a handle per assembly with its own listeners, one lock per name. ⚠ Like SQLite across
  processes, a sibling assembly's write reaches this one's reads, never its listeners; the old file
  store's "stale until a rehydrate" no longer exists to be tested, so `DriveLocalRuntimeTest`'s
  rehydrate case and the stale-cache premise of `SyncActivitySharedReplicaTest` changed with it.

⚠⚠ **Still open, and older than this:** on SQLite a sibling process's write reaches no listener here
(`ios-sync-activity-indicator.md` §12.3). The heartbeat's member re-notification ran only from the file
store's rehydrate, which no production process ever reached after B.22; deleting it changes nothing
that shipped. Over the test replica (which behaves as SQLite does here) the two
`SyncActivitySharedReplicaTest` cases that assert a sibling's beat lights a **mounted** surface
(`aSiblingsPull_lightsThisAppsSurface…`, `aSiblingsLaterPull_rewritesItsBeatInPlace…`) fail, so
they are `@Ignore`d with that reason, to be un-ignored with the fix — they were never evidence about
the shipped store.

### B.23 A task's token: *Index now* continues under the store's protection (2026-11-05)

**What it is.** Q1 of `ios-on-device-inference.md` §15.4, and the precondition `tech-debt.md` named
*S0b-4 owes a continued task's token*. Since B.22 the store is on in every iOS build, so PR-7's
decline (`declinedWhen = { SharedReplicaEntries.isInstalled }`) was always true and every *Index
now* press ran PR-5's foreground pass only. Verified against the code before building: the entry's
token (`protectEntry`) was the store's only background token, it begins a `beginBackgroundTask`
assertion through `BackgroundTimeAssertions`, and §4.2.1's admission read
`UIApplication.backgroundTimeRemaining` through the same seam whenever the app was not in front.

#### B.23.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| The token | `ReplicaProtection.acquireTask(reason, onExpired)`: an explicit token (it clears the latch like any) whose assertion is the platform's running `BGTask`: **nothing is begun or ended on the platform** for it, so it is never refused for want of time. Its `release()` is a release (the last one quiesces: step 3's 1 s, a 2 s drain, no interrupt, (200)); its `expire()` is the assertion's expiry, B.15.3's table unchanged (the first row when it ends protection: interrupt, 2 s drain, latch; W7 otherwise). Each is idempotent and either after the other a no-op, through the existing token states | `ReplicaProtection.kt` |
| The task's time | `remainingMs()`: in front, null (unchanged); with a task's token **live**, `Long.MAX_VALUE`, without asking the platform; otherwise `backgroundTimeRemaining` as before | `ReplicaProtection.kt` |
| The seam | `SharedReplicaLifecycle.protectTask(reason, onExpired)` → `SharedReplicaTaskToken` (`release`, `expire`), under the same `ERROR` opt-in and `@HiddenFromObjC`; `SharedReplicaBinding.protectTask` | `SharedReplicaPlatform.kt`, `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| The order | `SharedReplicaEntries.protectTask(reason)` → `SharedReplicaTaskProtection`: `begin()` at the launch; `expire()` from the `expirationHandler` marks the end as an expiry; `finish(then)` ends the token, **then** runs `then` (`setTaskCompleted`); `endToken()` ends it once, and every other end **waits for what is in flight**: a `begin()` still taking the token (then ends what it got, as an expiry if marked), or another end (and turns an in-flight release into an expiry once, if marked since: B.23.6). A release on the main thread is moved off it with its completion. With no binding, a pass-through. ⚠ Lives in `:core-common` since fix round 1, so its tests run over the real protection | `SharedReplicaTaskProtection.kt` (`:core-common`); `SharedReplicaEntries.protectTask` makes it |
| PR-7 wired | `PhotosLocalRuntime.onIndexNowTaskLaunched` takes the hold **before** the claim goes live (only for the claim's identifier; a stray completes at once with no token) and wraps the task so its completion ends the token first; `onIndexNowTaskExpired` marks it, lets `ContinuedIndexing.expired` cancel the pass and complete the task (which expires the token first), then ends the token as a backstop. `PhotosIndexNow.install` has no `declinedWhen` any more | `PhotosLocalRuntime.kt`, `PhotosOnDeviceAi.kt` |

**Swift:** none changed. `IndexNowContinuation.swift` already sets the `expirationHandler` before
it calls Kotlin, and calls `setTaskCompleted` only when Kotlin says.

#### B.23.2 Decisions made in implementation, for review

Numbered on from B.22 (439).

440. ⚠⚠ **The token ends before the task is completed, always.** The task is what keeps the
     process from being suspended; once `setTaskCompleted` runs, a store left open for writing is
     `0xdead10cc`. So the completion `ContinuedIndexing` makes (once, by `OnceTask`) is wrapped:
     the token is released (or expired) and only then is the task completed. This is the Q2 order
     an entry already keeps (its release before its caller's completion handler).
441. ⚠⚠ **The task's time is "no deadline" while its token is live.** A `BGContinuedProcessingTask`
     or `BGProcessingTask` states no remaining time; it runs until the system calls its
     `expirationHandler`. As in the foreground (where the backgrounding token supplies the time),
     what bounds an operation is the expiry: every transaction interrupted, the 2 s drain for
     rollbacks, and the uninterruptible work B.15.3 lists. ⚠⚠ *(Fix round 1, MED-3.)*
     **Under a task, admission keeps no margin before the expiry: the 2 s post-expiry drain is the
     whole margin.** With `remaining = Long.MAX_VALUE`, every reserve (`expiryMarginMs`,
     `2 · S_full`, `R(Wmax + δ)`) passes trivially, so nothing is refused for being too close to an
     expiry nobody can predict. The uninterruptible work an expiry can find in flight is, at the
     placeholders, about 1.3 s (an open's WAL-index rebuild 200 ms, two `F_FULLFSYNC` 2 × 500 ms,
     the commit sync 100 ms; the `CORRUPT` marker's syncs are those two), inside the 2 s drain
     only **if iOS lets the `expirationHandler` block that long**: B.23.5 item 3 is a hard gate. **Not null**: `isForeground` and
     `inForeground()` stay false, so a migration chunk is still refused outside the foreground
     (S13) and `CKPT_MAX` still applies. Once the task's token is gone, an entry's token reads
     `backgroundTimeRemaining` again. *Rejected:* a fixed budget per task (a number nothing on the
     platform states).
442. **The expiry is the owner's, in an order: cancel, then interrupt, then complete.** The
     `expirationHandler` marks the hold; `ContinuedIndexing.expired` releases the claim (in the
     background that is the leave's stop: a `beginBackgroundTask` window, the pass cancelled at its
     next photo) and completes the task with `false`; that completion expires the token (B.15.3,
     blocking for at most the cancel, the 2 s drain and the closes) and then calls
     `setTaskCompleted`. A pass still mid-transaction when the token expires is interrupted and
     fenced, (204) as for any expiry. The pass's next access meets the closed gate and the latch, and
     parks (holding nothing) until the foreground. ⚠ The expiry blocks the thread the
     `expirationHandler` runs on, as every expiry handler of the store does.
443. **A task's token takes no part in the fence's background rebuild** (B.16 (232)): it does not
     count as an active entry, so a fence met during a continued pass is rebuilt at the next
     foreground. A rebuild under a live task would tear down the graph that owns the task.
444. **No token, no task.** If none can be had (only if it is gone before it is handed over), the
     request is answered as refused and the task completed with `false` at once: the pass stays
     PR-5's foreground pass, which a leave cancels.

#### B.23.3 Not built

- **PR-6's `BGProcessingTask`** is not built at all (no handler, no `processing` mode in
  `photos-ios/project.yml`). When it is, its handler takes `SharedReplicaEntries.protectTask` exactly
  as PR-7's launch does, and completes the task through `finish`.

expiry during the pass's release finds the hold, turns the release into an expiry, and returns

#### B.23.5 Device-only items (📱, not run)

1. Press *Index now* on iOS 26+, leave Photos: the system's progress UI continues, and the pass
   goes on writing (the log shows no `[gate] parked` and no `ReplicaAdmissionDeferred`).
2. Let it expire (or stop it from the live activity) mid-pass: the log shows
   `[protection] token-expiry interrupt (expiry of 'task:photos-index-now')` and a `QUIESCED`
   quiesce before the completion, and **no `0xdead10cc` crash report** afterwards
   (`xcrun devicectl device info files --domain-type systemCrashLogs …`).
3. ⚠⚠ **A hard gate, not a nice-to-know** (fix round 1, MED-3): how long iOS lets the
   `expirationHandler` block before it suspends or kills. The expiry blocks for up to the 2 s
   drain plus the closes, and under a task that drain is the **only** margin (441): an open's
   rebuild, the two full syncs and a commit's sync (~1.3 s at the placeholders) must fit inside
   what iOS allows. **If it allows less than ~2.5 s, a task's time must stop being "no deadline"**
   (an admission reserve kept against a fixed expiry allowance) before the build ships.
4. A pass that finishes in the background: the token's release quiesces (up to 3 s) before
   `setTaskCompleted`; no watchdog kill for a late completion.

#### B.23.6 Fix round 1 (Codex and the independent review)

Every finding was a window in which the `expirationHandler` could return with the store still live
or draining: the `0xdead10cc` shape. Each was checked against the code before the fix.

1. **The hold removed before its token ended** (Codex P2, MED-1): `PhotosLocalRuntime`'s wrapped
   completion took the hold out of the map, then released. An expiry during that release (or while
   its off-main hop was queued) found nothing and returned at once. Now the hold is removed in the
   completion's own callback, after the token has ended, so the expiry's `endToken()` waits for it.
2. **An expiry during a release stayed a release** (MED-2): the mark was only read by an end not
   yet started, so `ReplicaProtection`'s RELEASING-expiry branch (drain cut to 2 s, interrupt,
   latch) never ran and the store was not latched after the task expired. Now a waiter that finds a
   release in flight and the mark set calls `expire()` on the token once, then waits for the end.
3. **An expiry while `begin()` was still taking the token** (Codex P2, LOW-6): `endToken()` saw no
   token, marked the hold ended and returned; the late grant was then only *released*, so the store
   was protected after the handler returned. Now an acquisition in flight is tracked, every end
   waits for it, and ends what it got (an expiry if marked); a `begin()` after the hold ended takes
   no token. B.23.1's "an expiry that arrives before the token was handed over is kept" was wrong
   for Photos' real sequence (mark, then end at once); it now holds.
4. **A completion before the token ended** (LOW-5): a teardown's `finish` while `begin()` was in
   flight ran `setTaskCompleted` first. It now waits for the `begin`, like every end.
5. **The N-B hand-off** (LOW-4): a registry-lock holder's release returns before its shutdown runs,
   and a task token has no assertion whose end could be waited for. `release()`/`expire()` of a task
   token now fail with `IllegalStateException` on such a thread, as `acquireForJob` does (86).
6. **No margin before the expiry** (MED-3, docs only): (441) amended; B.23.5 item 3 is a hard gate.
   Nothing concrete was found to change in code: the alternative is a reserve against an allowance
   only the phone can measure.
7. *(Fix round 2, Codex P2.)* **An escalated expiry that wins the race into the release.** The
   release was chosen, then the waiter's `expire()` reached `ReplicaProtection.expired()` first,
   which marks the token DEAD before its shutdown runs; the `release()` that followed met a DEAD
   token and returned at once, and `finish` completed the task with the interrupt and the drain
   still running. **Fixed in `ReplicaProtection`, not in the wrapper**: a task token's `release()`
   and `expire()` now return only once an expiry that took the token from LIVE has finished
   (`expiryRunning`, set under the state lock in the step that marks it DEAD; bounded at 10 s and
   logged; never on the expiry's own thread). *Why there:* it covers every caller of a task token
   (PR-7's wrapper today, PR-6's handler tomorrow), and the token is where the fact lives. An
   entry's token is unchanged: its platform assertion, which is what keeps the process running,
   ends only inside the expiry's own `endOnce`, so its early-returning release is harmless.

### B.24 The schema registry's chains bound: a store behind is migrated, not wiped (2026-11-05)

**Why.** B.13 (167) bound the store with no chain (`NoMigrationChains`) and every floor at its own
version, so any store behind the build classified `Behind(belowFloor = true)` and was **wiped and
re-synced**, outbound queues included. Harmless while nothing had shipped (the 1.0.1 re-cut
restarted every chain at v1); after release it is the data loss House Rule 9 forbids, on the first
service bump, on every iPhone. The chunked migrator (§5.3, slices 2 to 4) was built and tested; it was
never given a step.

#### B.24.1 What exists

| Piece | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `RegistryReplicaMigrationSteps` | The registry's chains as `ReplicaMigrationSteps`: `step(service, from)` is the registered `from → from + 1` step, with `typeIds` = its `CompositeMigration`s' types **and** its `droppedProperties`' types, and `migrate` = `StoreRowMigrationCodec.migrateRow` (a reshaped type only) then the property strip. `:core` is addressed as `CORE_SERVICE_ID`. The chains are `verify`d at construction, as the JVM verifies them at every configured open | `core-common/src/iosSqliteMain/.../RegistryReplicaMigrationSteps.kt` |
| `replicaBuild()` | `ReplicaBuild` with **each floor the oldest version its registered chain reaches** (`SchemaMigrationRegistry.floorFor`, the JVM's derivation), core and every service, from the same registry as the steps; plus the list-segment stamp (floor = version) | same file; the binding's `replicaBuildOf` delegates to it |
| The binding | `sharedReplicaStoreModule` builds the steps from the graph's own `StoreSchemaMigrations` and opens with both; `Seams.open` and `SharedReplicaBinding.open` take the steps; `preOpen` reopens with the last build **and its steps** together. One module, so every graph: the nine apps (`FirstPartyLocalRuntime`) and Control (`ControlSharedReplica.runtimeModule`) | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| `WipeJobsNeverMigrate` | What a wipe call's job is given: steps that **throw** if asked | `SharedReplicaBinding.kt` |
| `NoMigrationChains` | Moved to `iosTest` (`ReplicaChainsTestSupport.kt`), with a one-argument `open(build)` for the tests whose builds floor at their version. No production open can omit its chains | `tenshu-sdk-ios-core/src/iosTest` |

#### B.24.2 What was verified, against what the docs said

- **The JVM migrator** (`StoreSchemaMigrator.runStep`): one `rowsOfTypes` over the step's
  `CompositeMigration` types, `migrateRow` per row (null: dropped by decision), the strip of
  `droppedProperties` from every surviving row of each retired type (on top of the rewrite when the
  step also reshapes it), a `TList` membership sweep of dropped hashes, and one transaction with the
  rewrites, deletes, sweeps, the journal clear and the stamp. B.3 (25)'s description of the adapter
  matches it, **with one gap**: `migrateRow` **throws** ("No migration registered for row type") for a
  row of a type the step does not reshape, so an adapter that ran it on every row of `typeIds` would
  fail every row of a strip-only type, count it, and after `N` runs wipe the store. The adapter runs it
  on reshaped types only.
- **`ReplicaMigrationSteps`**: a step per `(service, from)`, `null` meaning "no step: these rows cannot
  be read". `ReplicaReplacement.migrationChunk` turns a null into a wipe's first chunk (`no-step`).
  ⚠ So a defect that asked for a step the build does not migrate *from* and got `null` would wipe.
- **The chunked migrator** (`ReplicaReplacement`): the Start (one transaction, under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`,
  after `classify` re-read under the lock) writes `meta.migration` with every service below this build
  as a target, a new epoch and `seq + 1`; row chunks bounded by `chunkMaxRows`, the WAL budget and the
  hold ceiling, each recording its rows in `migration_done` and moving the cursor in the same
  transaction; a `VERIFY` pass over rows not in `migration_done`; the sweep of `migration_dropped`;
  the cleanup; the step finish (stamp; `user_version` for `:core`); the Finish (marker cleared, epoch
  moved). Every chunk re-reads the marker and re-applies `classify` under the lock. A row the step
  fails on is counted in the marker, at most once a run, and at `N` the job becomes a wipe.
- **What a floor means**: `classify` (`ReplicaClassification.kt`) wipes when any recorded version is
  below its floor (`Behind(belowFloor = true)`) and migrates when one is behind but none below
  (`Behind(belowFloor = false)`). With every floor at its version, the second case could not occur.
- ⚠ **Found: on the JVM a `:core` step's row migrations never run.** `coreReadableFloor()` reads the
  core chain, but `StoreSchemaMigrator.migrateStoreAtOpen` walks `serviceSchemas()`, which `:core` is
  not in: `SqliteObjectStore` re-stamps `user_version` and rewrites no row. Harmless while every core
  step is empty; recorded in `tech-debt.md`. The iOS migrator addresses `:core` like a service and
  runs them (tested below).

#### B.24.3 Decisions made in implementation, for review

445. **The adapter is in `iosSqliteMain`, not `commonMain`** (B.3 (25)'s rule): `:core-common`
     commonMain is untouched, so the JVM, Android and JS stores are unchanged by construction.
     `StoreRowMigrationCodec` is `internal` to `:core-common`, which the adapter is in.
446. ⚠⚠ **A step asked at or above this build's version throws; it never answers `null`.** The JVM's
     "written by newer code" wipe has no iOS twin: the JVM migrator never runs on iOS, a newer store is
     `Skew` at open and at every chunk (`classify`, rule 1), and a marker whose targets pass this build
     is `Skew` too. So the migrator never asks for such a step. If a defect ever did, `null` would be
     read as "wipe"; a throw rolls the chunk back and stops the run with nothing written. The same for
     a service the registry does not declare (the list-segment stamp included, which has no chain).
447. **Floors and steps from one registry instance**, built in the graph's `single<ObjectStore>` inside
     the open's `try`: a floor can only say "migratable" where a step exists, and a chain that fails
     `verify` refuses the open (the stand-in, not retried), as the JVM refuses the proxy start.
448. **A wipe job gets `WipeJobsNeverMigrate`.** A wipe's first chunk deletes any `meta.migration`;
     every later chunk reads `meta.wipe`; no open starts a migration on a store marked for a wipe. So
     its job never asks for a step, and the wipe calls (`startCustodyWipe`, the custody purge) keep
     their signatures. If it were asked, it throws (446's reasoning), never wipes by default.
449. **No version bump.** Production chains are all empty at the 1.0.1 baseline; every floor is still
     its version, and no shipped behaviour changes until the first bump registers its step.
     `ServiceMigrationChainsReachTheirVersionTest` and `SchemaShapeBaseline` are untouched.
450. ⚠⚠ **Accepted trade: a step that fails deterministically on a row wipes the store, losing the
     unpushed outbound changes, where the JVM never wipes.** B.3 (41)/(53): a row the step fails on
     is counted once a run, and at the `migrationRowAttempts`th counted run (`N = 3`,
     `ReplicaLimits`) the job becomes a wipe, so the outbound queues the older apps had not pushed
     go with it. The JVM migrator has no count: `StoreSchemaMigrator.runStep` throws, the open fails,
     and it fails again on every launch, the data kept and the app unusable until a build with a
     fixed step ships. iOS chose recoverability of the app over the unpushed tail, because on the
     shared replica one bad row would otherwise lock every app on the phone out at once, with no
     route back but an update. Bound, now that real chains run: it fires only for a step that throws
     on a stored row (a decode or `derive` defect), which the step's own tests should catch. ⚠ The
     first two counts are silent to the user: a diagnostic signal at count 1 is a follow-up
     (`tech-debt.md`).
451. **Every step is built once, at the open** (`RegistryReplicaMigrationSteps.built`), on the
     graph's thread: `step()` is asked once per chunk inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, under `HOLD_MAX`, and
     on the worker's thread, so it is a map lookup and constructs nothing. Only `migrate` runs on
     the worker, and its registry calls are the ones every concurrent reader of the live graph makes:
     the registry's module list is not written after the graph is built, and its caches are
     lock-free compare-and-set maps. Building a codec resolves nothing from the DI graph (E2j-4).

#### B.24.4 Across processes: what already held, and what was added

Nothing was missing; the tests below pin it with real chains.

- **Only one migration, never a duplicated row.** The Start is one transaction under
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, re-classified under the lock, so a second process that also found the store
  behind re-reads the marker and resumes rather than starting again (§5.2 step 2a). Two processes of
  the same build may both run chunks of the job; they are serialised by the write lock, every chunk
  re-reads the cursor, and `migration_done` keeps any row from being migrated twice.
- **A same-build sibling that opens mid-migration** classifies `Updating(MIGRATION)`: it is handed no
  store (nothing serves a half-migrated row), and its job may carry the migration on. A sibling
  already open is fenced `REPLACED` by the Start's epoch at its next access.
- **An older build's sibling** is `Skew`: the marker's targets are above it (judged by the read-only
  classification, before any read/write connection), and after the Finish so are the stamps. It
  writes nothing, migrates nothing, wipes nothing (S12, S19, D5).

`RegistryReplicaMigrationStepsTest` (`:core-common` `iosSqliteTest`, 9 tests, on the simulator) runs
real schema registries with a real bump of a test-only service (the JVM's `THING` fixtures: rename,
drop, derive, convert, so a row migrated twice or not at all cannot come out right) and of `:core`
under a test core version, through the production open and chunked migrator, seven rows a chunk:

| Test | Pins |
|---|---|
| `eachFloorIsTheOldestVersionItsRegisteredChainMigratesFrom` | the floors: no chain → the version; one and two steps → v1; a cut chain → v2; `:core` likewise |
| `aStoreAtVnOpenedByVnPlusOneWithItsStepIsMigratedNotWiped` | rows rewritten in place, other rows and the outbound queue (a list and its entries) byte for byte, no wipe, the version stamped |
| `aDroppedPropertyLeavesEveryRowOfItsTypeWhetherOrNotTheStepReshapesIt` | the strip, on a reshaped type and on a **strip-only** type that must never reach `migrateRow` |
| `aStoreTwoStepsBehindRunsTheWholeChainInOneJob` | v1 → v3 in one job: the reshape, then a strip-only step |
| `aCoreStepMigratesItsRowsAndStampsUserVersion` | a `:core` step's rows rewritten, `user_version` stamped, the service untouched |
| `aStoreBelowTheFloorIsWiped` | a chain cut at v2: the v1 store wipes and is stamped at this build |
| `aNewerStoreIsRefusedUntouchedAndTheStepsRefuseToBeAskedForIt` | a newer store `Skew` in the foreground and the background, the database and `-wal` byte for byte; the steps throw at or above the version, for an unknown service and for the list-segment stamp |
| `aRowDroppedByDecisionIsDeletedSweptFromEveryListAndNeverStripped` (fix round) | a step whose migrate returns null for some rows, with a property strip on the same type: the rows deleted, their hashes swept from a plain list and from a list kept in segments, the step answering null (never a stripped copy) for a dropped row |
| `aChainKilledAtEveryCommitResumesWithNoRowSkippedOrMigratedTwice` | a two-step chain killed at every commit in turn, resumed by a new process: never a wipe, every row once per step |
| `aSecondProcessOpeningDuringTheMigrationWaitsOrCarriesItOnAndAnOlderBuildIsRefused` | an old build's open handle fenced; an old build's open `Skew` with nothing written; a same-build process `Updating`, carrying the job on; each row once |

`SharedReplicaBindingTest.theGraphsOpenIsGivenTheRegistrysChainsAndFloorsTheyReach`
(`:tenshu-sdk-ios-core`): the production modules plus a made-up service at v2 with a strip-only 1→2
step; the graph's open is given that step and a floor of 1, the strip works, and a step at v2 throws.

**Mutations**, each applied, run, and restored:

| Mutation | Red |
|---|---|
| M1 each floor is its version (`floorOf` returns the declared version) | 8 of 9: every test but the below-floor one |
| M2 `migrateRow` on every row of `typeIds`, a strip-only type included | the strip, the two-step chain, the kill/resume test |
| M3 no property strip | the strip, the two-step chain, the kill/resume test |
| M4 a step at or above the version answers `null` instead of throwing | the newer-store test |
| M6 `typeIds` without the dropped properties' types | the strip, the two-step chain, the kill/resume test |
| M7 a row dropped by decision kept (`migrateRow(row) ?: return null` → `?: row`) | the drop test (survived every other test before the fix round) |
| M5 the binding opens with no chain (`{ _, _ -> null }`) in place of the registry's | `theGraphsOpenIsGivenTheRegistrysChainsAndFloorsTheyReach` |

`CoreStepsReshapeNothingTest` (`:system-test-utils`, the real graph, every platform's registry) fails
while any `:core` step carries `migrations` or `droppedProperties`: the JVM never runs a core step's row
work (B.24.2), so a reshaping core step would leave every non-iOS store old-shaped. Its message names
the `tech-debt.md` entry. Mutation: a core step with a dropped property injected into its registry → red.
